vertax

A differentiable JAX-based framework for vertex modeling and inverse design of epithelial tissues.

Epithelial tissues dynamically reshape through local mechanical interactions among cells. Understanding, inferring, and designing these mechanics is a central challenge in developmental biology and biophysics. VertAX is a computational framework built to address this challenge.

VertAX is a framework for vertex-based modeling: it represents epithelial tissues as two-dimensional polygonal meshes in which cells are faces, junctions are edges, tricellular contacts are vertices, and mechanical equilibrium is defined by the minimum of a user-specified energy.

Built on JAX, VertAX is designed not only for forward simulation, but also for inverse problems such as parameter inference and tissue design.

In VertAX, a Mesh represents a vertex model of an epithelial tissue. It is made of faces (cells), edges (interface between cells) and vertices (where 3 cells or more meet).

More specifically, two types of meshes are currently supported:

  • PbcMesh have Periodic Boundary Conditions, and are used for bulk tissue dynamics without explicit external boundaries.
  • BoundedMesh are designed for finite tissue clusters, with curved free interfaces.

The other first class objects of VertAX are called Bilevel Optimizers. They allow to formulate inverse problems as nested optimizations:

$$ \begin{aligned} \textbf{Outer problem (learning):} \quad \theta^{\ast} &= \arg\min_{\theta} \mathcal{C}\left(X^{\ast}_{\theta},\theta\right) && \leftarrow \text{fit data or reach a target} \ \end{aligned} $$ $$ \begin{aligned} \textbf{Inner problem (physics):} \quad \text{s.t.}& X^{\ast}_{\theta} \in \arg\min_{X} \mathcal{E}(X,\theta) && \leftarrow \text{compute mechanical equilibrium} \end{aligned} $$

Here, $X$ denotes the tissue configuration, i.e. the vertex positions of the mesh, and $\theta$ denotes the model parameters, such as line tensions, target areas, or shape factors.

In other words, VertAX repeatedly solves a mechanical equilibrium problem for a given parameter set $\theta$, then updates those parameters to better match data or a design objective.

In symmetry with meshes, a base abstract class _BilevelOptimizer defines common hyper-parameters and methods for the bilevel optimization, but you need to use the specialized classes:

  • PbcBilevelOptimizer for PbcMesh,
  • BoundedBilevelOptimizer for BoundedMesh.

VertAX comes with pre-defined energy and cost functions but you can easily define your own functions. See the examples folder in the repository to have a typical example on how to use VertAX.

Finally, there are plot functions to easily see the results of your experiments. See plot_mesh for example.

Users can define their own energy functions for the inner optimization and cost function for the outer optimization, however we provide some basic ones. If you use your own make sure to use the exact same signature as we do for these functions, otherwise it won't work. See the cost and energy functions we provide in this documentation.

 37class Mesh(metaclass=NoPublicConstructor):
 38    """Generic mesh structure. It is an abstract base class, not to be used directly.
 39
 40    It defines common attributes and functions between `PbcMesh` and `BoundedMesh`.
 41    """
 42
 43    def __init__(self) -> None:
 44        """Do nothing but create attributes. Do not call this, but call specialized class methods to create meshes.
 45
 46        See `PbcMesh` and `BoundedMesh`.
 47
 48        Technically, it uses a DCEL structure.
 49        """
 50        self.faces: Array = jnp.array([])
 51        """The cells of the tissue."""
 52        self.edges: Array = jnp.array([])
 53        """The interface between cells. Technically half-edges."""
 54        self.vertices: Array = jnp.array([])
 55        """The mesh vertices, where cells meet."""
 56        self.width: float = 0
 57        """The mesh live in a rectangle of size [0, width] in the X direction."""
 58        self.height: float = 0
 59        """The mesh live in a rectangle of size [0, height] in the Y direction."""
 60
 61        self.faces_params: Array = jnp.array([])
 62        """Parameters attached to faces. Can be optimized."""
 63        self.edges_params: Array = jnp.array([])
 64        """Parameters attached to edges. Can be optimized."""
 65        self.vertices_params: Array = jnp.array([])
 66        """Parameters attached to vertices. Can be optimized."""
 67
 68    @property
 69    def nb_faces(self) -> int:
 70        """Get the number of faces of the mesh."""
 71        return len(self.faces)
 72
 73    @property
 74    def nb_edges(self) -> int:
 75        """Get the number of edges of the mesh."""
 76        return self.nb_half_edges // 2
 77
 78    @property
 79    def nb_half_edges(self) -> int:
 80        """Get the number of half-edges of the mesh, ie. twice the number of edges."""
 81        return len(self.edges)
 82
 83    @property
 84    def nb_vertices(self) -> int:
 85        """Get the number of vertices of the mesh."""
 86        return len(self.vertices)
 87
 88    def save_mesh(self, path: str) -> None:
 89        """Save mesh to a file.
 90
 91        All mesh data is saved.
 92
 93        Args:
 94            path (str): Path to the saved file. The extension is .npz.
 95        """
 96        raise NotImplementedError
 97
 98    @classmethod
 99    def load_mesh(cls, path: str) -> Self:
100        """Load a mesh from a file.
101
102        Args:
103            path (str): Path to the mesh file (.npz).
104
105        Returns:
106            The mesh loaded from the .npz file.
107        """
108        raise NotImplementedError

class PbcMesh(vertax.Mesh): 
 21class PbcMesh(Mesh):
 22    """Periodic Boundary Condition on a mesh.
 23
 24    For a PbcMesh, `vertices` is a 2D array of floats of size (nb_vertices, 2) ;
 25    with the coordinates of the vertices (in ]0, width[ x ]0, height[ ).
 26    The floats use JAX's default float dtype: `float32`, or `float64` when `jax_enable_x64` is enabled
 27    before the mesh is built.
 28
 29    `edges` is a  2D array of integers of size (nb_half_edges, 8), with:
 30
 31    - id of previous half-edge,
 32    - id of next half-edge,
 33    - id of twin half-edge,
 34    - id of source vertex,
 35    - id of target vertex,
 36    - id of the face containing the half-edge.
 37    - x-offset (either -1, 0 or 1) depending on the target vertex crossing a boundary.
 38    - y-offset (either -1, 0 or 1) depending on the target vertex crossing a boundary.
 39
 40    `faces` is a 1D array of integers of size (nb_faces) containing the id of a half-edge belonging to this face.
 41    """
 42
 43    def __init__(self) -> None:
 44        """Do not call the constructor directly, use the dedicated class methods such as:
 45
 46        - `from_random_seeds`,
 47        - `from_seeds`,
 48        - `from_image`,
 49        - `from_mask`,
 50        - `create_empty`.
 51        """  # noqa: D415
 52        super().__init__()
 53
 54        self.MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE: int = 20
 55        """Optimization parameter : must be more than the estimated maximum number of edges in a face. Base value is 20."""  # noqa: E501
 56
 57    @classmethod
 58    def from_random_seeds(cls, nb_seeds: int, width: float, height: float, random_key: int) -> Self:
 59        """Create a Periodic Boundary Conditions Mesh from a Voronoi diagram based on random seeds.
 60
 61        Args:
 62            nb_seeds (int): Number of random seeds to use.
 63            width (float): Width of the rectangular domains the seeds will be in.
 64            height (float): Height of the rectangular domains the seeds will be in.
 65            random_key (int): Set the random key for reproducibility.
 66
 67        Returns:
 68            Self: The corresponding mesh.
 69        """
 70        key = jax.random.PRNGKey(random_key)
 71        seeds = jnp.array((width, height)) * jax.random.uniform(key, (nb_seeds, 2))
 72        try:
 73            return cls.from_seeds(seeds, width, height)
 74        except _FaceOrderingError as exc:
 75            # `_make_he_structure` cannot name the seed, and the seed is what a caller varies.
 76            msg = f"{exc} Reached from from_random_seeds(nb_seeds={nb_seeds}, random_key={random_key})."
 77            raise _FaceOrderingError(msg) from exc
 78
 79    @classmethod
 80    def from_seeds(cls, seeds: Array, width: float, height: float) -> Self:
 81        """Create a Periodic Boundary Conditions Mesh from a Voronoi diagram based on a list of seeds.
 82
 83        The seeds are assumed to have positive x and y positions.
 84
 85        Args:
 86            seeds (Array): jax float array of seed positions of shape (nbSeeds, 2).
 87            width (float): width of the box containing the seeds.
 88            height (float): height of the box containing the seeds.
 89        """
 90        (
 91            periodic_voronoi_vertices_idx,
 92            periodic_voronoi_vertices_pos,
 93            periodic_voronoi_edges,
 94            offsets,
 95            periodic_voronoi_faces,
 96        ) = _make_periodic(seeds, width, height)
 97
 98        vertices, edges, faces = _make_he_structure(
 99            width,
100            height,
101            periodic_voronoi_vertices_idx,
102            periodic_voronoi_vertices_pos,
103            periodic_voronoi_edges,
104            offsets,
105            periodic_voronoi_faces,
106        )
107
108        pbc_mesh = cls._create()
109        pbc_mesh.vertices = jnp.array(vertices, dtype=jnp.result_type(float))
110        pbc_mesh.edges = jnp.array(edges, dtype=np.int32)
111        pbc_mesh.faces = jnp.array(faces, dtype=np.int32)
112        pbc_mesh.width = width
113        pbc_mesh.height = height
114
115        return pbc_mesh
116
117    @classmethod
118    def from_image(
119        cls,
120        image: NDArray,
121    ) -> Self:
122        """Create a rudimentary mesh with periodic boundary conditions from an image.
123
124        To do that, we perform a segmentation using Cellpose and we try to fill the holes.
125        The result will probably be imperfect and it will always be better if you
126        provide directly a mask (with no holes) with the function "periodic_from_mask".
127
128        The mask is made periodic by mirroring its edges.
129
130        Args:
131            image (NDArray): The image which will act as a template for the mesh.
132
133        Returns:
134            Self: The corresponding mesh.
135        
136        .. warning::
137
138            **Junction extraction is unreliable on real masks, and this method is currently
139            unsupported for them.** It builds the mesh with
140            `mask_analysis.find_vertices_edges_faces`, which keeps a label triple only where
141            exactly one 2x2 window carries it. A real trijunction is generally a small cluster of
142            windows, so genuine junctions are discarded and spurious short cycles close in their
143            place.
144
145            MEASURED on `examples/image.tif`, the image shipped with this method's own example:
146            `V - E + F = 55` and **472 faces from 64 segmented cells**. On a raw microscopy crop,
147            `V - E + F = 6`. A correct planar mesh gives 0.
148
149            For a segmented tissue, use :mod:`vertax.trace` instead, which extracts junctions on the
150            pixel-corner lattice and is tested against a stored reference.
151
152            **The gap is real and `vertax.trace` does not close it.** `trace` produces a *clamped
153            patch* -- a finite tissue fragment with a boundary -- not a periodic mesh. There is
154            currently **no working route from an image to a periodic mesh**. Substituting the
155            corner-lattice extraction here is the intended fix; it is deferred, and its three
156            preconditions are recorded in the freeze checklist.
157
158        """
159        return cls.from_mask(mask_from_image(image))
160
161    @classmethod
162    def from_mask(  # noqa: C901
163        cls,
164        mask: NDArray,
165    ) -> Self:
166        """Create a rudimentary mesh with periodic boundary conditions from a mask with no holes.
167
168        The mask is made periodic by mirroring its edges.
169
170        Args:
171            mask (NDArray): The mask with no holes which will act as a template for the mesh.
172
173        Returns:
174            Self: The corresponding mesh.
175        
176        .. warning::
177
178            **Junction extraction is unreliable on real masks, and this method is currently
179            unsupported for them.** It builds the mesh with
180            `mask_analysis.find_vertices_edges_faces`, which keeps a label triple only where
181            exactly one 2x2 window carries it. A real trijunction is generally a small cluster of
182            windows, so genuine junctions are discarded and spurious short cycles close in their
183            place.
184
185            MEASURED on `examples/image.tif`, the image shipped with this method's own example:
186            `V - E + F = 55` and **472 faces from 64 segmented cells**. On a raw microscopy crop,
187            `V - E + F = 6`. A correct planar mesh gives 0.
188
189            For a segmented tissue, use :mod:`vertax.trace` instead, which extracts junctions on the
190            pixel-corner lattice and is tested against a stored reference.
191
192            **The gap is real and `vertax.trace` does not close it.** `trace` produces a *clamped
193            patch* -- a finite tissue fragment with a boundary -- not a periodic mesh. There is
194            currently **no working route from an image to a periodic mesh**. Substituting the
195            corner-lattice extraction here is the intended fix; it is deferred, and its three
196            preconditions are recorded in the freeze checklist.
197
198        """
199        padded_mask = pad(mask, save=False, output_path="refined_and_padded_image.tiff")
200        # Find vertices, edges, faces
201        vertices, edges, faces = find_vertices_edges_faces(padded_mask)
202
203        # imread tiff = Y is the first axis, X the second.
204        height: int = mask.shape[0]  # original image length. Padded is 3 times bigger.
205        y_min = height / 2
206        y_max = 2 * height + (height / 2)
207        width: int = mask.shape[1]
208        x_min = width / 2
209        x_max = 2 * width + (width / 2)
210
211        col0_mask = (vertices[:, 0] >= x_min) & (vertices[:, 0] < x_max)
212        col1_mask = (vertices[:, 1] >= y_min) & (vertices[:, 1] < y_max)
213
214        periodic_vertices_idx = np.arange(len(vertices))[col0_mask & col1_mask]
215        periodic_vertices_pos = vertices[col0_mask & col1_mask]
216
217        # store map between vertex id -> inside vertex id
218        inside_vertex: dict[int, int] = {idx: idx for idx in periodic_vertices_idx}
219        for i, vertex in enumerate(vertices):
220            if i not in periodic_vertices_idx:
221                x, y = vertex
222                if x < x_min:
223                    x += 2 * width
224                elif x >= x_max:
225                    x -= 2 * width
226
227                if y < y_min:
228                    y += 2 * height
229                elif y >= y_max:
230                    y -= 2 * height
231
232                # Find corresponding inside vertex to the outside dest vertex
233                for idx, pos in zip(periodic_vertices_idx, periodic_vertices_pos, strict=True):
234                    if np.max(np.abs(pos - [x, y])) < 1:
235                        inside_vertex[i] = idx
236                        break
237
238        edges_inside = []
239        edges_outside = []
240        offsets_inside = {}
241        offsets_outside = {}
242        visited = []
243
244        for e in edges:
245            if e[0] in periodic_vertices_idx and e[1] in periodic_vertices_idx:
246                edges_inside.append(tuple(sorted((e[0], e[1]))))
247                offsets_inside[(e[0], e[1])] = (0, 0)
248                offsets_inside[(e[1], e[0])] = (0, 0)
249            elif bool(e[0] in periodic_vertices_idx) != bool(e[1] in periodic_vertices_idx):
250                if e[0] in periodic_vertices_idx:
251                    # origin in, dest out
252                    # check x coord
253                    if vertices[e[1]][0] < x_min:
254                        offset_x1 = -1
255                    elif vertices[e[1]][0] >= x_max:
256                        offset_x1 = 1
257                    else:
258                        offset_x1 = 0
259
260                    # Now check y coord
261                    if vertices[e[1]][1] < y_min:
262                        offset_y1 = -1
263                    elif vertices[e[1]][1] >= y_max:
264                        offset_y1 = 1
265                    else:
266                        offset_y1 = 0
267
268                    # Find corresponding inside vertex to the outside dest vertex
269                    if e[1] not in inside_vertex:
270                        print(f"Error, no inside vertex found for vertex {e[1]}.")
271                    else:
272                        idx = inside_vertex[e[1]]
273                        edges_outside.append(tuple(sorted((e[0], idx))))
274                        if (e[0], e[1]) not in visited and (e[1], e[0]) not in visited:
275                            offsets_outside[(e[0], idx)] = (offset_x1, offset_y1)
276                            offsets_outside[(idx, e[0])] = (-offset_x1, -offset_y1)
277                            visited.append((e[0], e[1]))
278                            visited.append((e[1], e[0]))
279                else:
280                    # dest in, origin out
281                    if vertices[e[0]][0] < x_min:
282                        offset_x0 = -1
283                    elif vertices[e[0]][0] >= x_max:
284                        offset_x0 = 1
285                    else:
286                        offset_x0 = 0
287
288                    if vertices[e[0]][1] < y_min:
289                        offset_y0 = -1
290                    elif vertices[e[0]][1] >= y_max:
291                        offset_y0 = 1
292                    else:
293                        offset_y0 = 0
294
295                    # Find corresponding inside vertex to the outside dest vertex
296                    if e[0] not in inside_vertex:
297                        print(f"Error, no inside vertex found for vertex {e[0]}.")
298                    else:
299                        idx = inside_vertex[e[0]]
300                        edges_outside.append(tuple(sorted((idx, e[1]))))
301                        if (e[0], e[1]) not in visited and (e[1], e[0]) not in visited:
302                            offsets_outside[(idx, e[1])] = (-offset_x0, -offset_y0)
303                            offsets_outside[(e[1], idx)] = (offset_x0, offset_y0)
304                            visited.append((e[0], e[1]))
305                            visited.append((e[1], e[0]))
306
307        periodic_edges = list(set(edges_inside)) + list(set(edges_outside))
308        offsets = offsets_inside | offsets_outside
309
310        periodic_faces: list[set[int]] = [
311            {inside_vertex[i] for i in face} for face in faces if any(v_id in periodic_vertices_idx for v_id in face)
312        ]
313
314        vertices, edges, faces = _make_he_structure(
315            2 * width,
316            2 * height,
317            periodic_vertices_idx,  # ty:ignore[invalid-argument-type]
318            periodic_vertices_pos,
319            periodic_edges,
320            offsets,
321            periodic_faces,
322            vertices_offset=(x_min, y_min),
323        )
324
325        pbc_mesh = cls._create()
326        pbc_mesh.vertices = jnp.array(vertices, dtype=jnp.result_type(float))
327        pbc_mesh.edges = jnp.array(edges, dtype=np.int32)
328        pbc_mesh.faces = jnp.array(faces, dtype=np.int32)
329        pbc_mesh.width = 2 * width
330        pbc_mesh.height = 2 * height
331
332        return pbc_mesh
333
334    @classmethod
335    def create_empty(cls) -> Self:
336        """Create an empty mesh. Use if you know what you're doing !"""
337        return cls._create()
338
339    @classmethod
340    def copy_mesh(cls, other_mesh: Self) -> Self:
341        """Copy all parameters from another mesh in a new mesh."""
342        mesh = cls._create()
343        mesh.vertices = other_mesh.vertices.copy()
344        mesh.edges = other_mesh.edges.copy()
345        mesh.faces = other_mesh.faces.copy()
346        mesh.width = other_mesh.width
347        mesh.height = other_mesh.height
348        mesh.vertices_params = other_mesh.vertices_params.copy()
349        mesh.edges_params = other_mesh.edges_params.copy()
350        mesh.faces_params = other_mesh.faces_params.copy()
351        mesh.MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE = other_mesh.MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE
352
353        return mesh

376        )

378    @classmethod
379    def load_mesh(cls, path: str) -> Self:
380        """Load a mesh from a file.
381
382        All PBCMesh data is reloaded.
383
384        Args:
385            path (str): Path to the mesh file (.npz), numpy format.
386
387        Returns:
388            Mesh: the mesh loaded from the numpy .npz file.
389        """
390        mesh_file = np.load(path)
391        mesh = cls._create()
392        mesh.vertices, mesh.edges, mesh.faces = (
393            jnp.array(mesh_file["vertices"]),
394            jnp.array(mesh_file["edges"].reshape(-1, 8)),
395            jnp.array(mesh_file["faces"]),
396        )
397        mesh.width, mesh.height = float(mesh_file["width"]), float(mesh_file["height"])
398        mesh.vertices_params = jnp.array(mesh_file["vertices_params"])
399        mesh.edges_params = jnp.array(mesh_file["edges_params"])
400        mesh.faces_params = jnp.array(mesh_file["faces_params"])
401        mesh.MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE = int(mesh_file["MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE"])
402        return mesh

404    def save_mesh_txt(
405        self,
406        directory: str,
407        vertices_filename: str = "vertTable.txt",
408        edges_filename: str = "heTable.txt",
409        faces_filename: str = "faceTable.txt",
410        vertices_params_filename: str = "vertParamsTable.txt",
411        edges_params_filename: str = "heParamsTable.txt",
412        faces_params_filename: str = "faceParamsTable.txt",
413        constants_filename: str = "constants.txt",
414    ) -> None:
415        """Save a mesh in separate text files that can be read by numpy.
416
417        Save the vertices, edges and faces tables, the vertex, edge and face parameter tables and the
418        constants (width, height and MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE), one text file each.
419
420        Args:
421            directory (str): Path to the directory where to save the files.
422            vertices_filename (str, optional): Filename for the vertices table. Defaults to "vertTable.txt".
423            edges_filename (str, optional): Filename for the half-edges table. Defaults to "heTable.txt".
424            faces_filename (str, optional): Filename for the faces table. Defaults to "faceTable.txt".
425            vertices_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the vertices parameters table.
426                    Defaults to "vertParamsTable.txt".
427            edges_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the half-edges parameters table.
428                    Defaults to "heParamsTable.txt".
429            faces_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the faces parameters table.
430                    Defaults to "faceParamsTable.txt".
431            constants_filename (str, optional): Filename for width/height/MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE.
432                    Defaults to "constants.txt".
433        """
434        dirpath = Path(directory)
435        dirpath.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
436        np.savetxt(dirpath / vertices_filename, self.vertices)
437        np.savetxt(dirpath / edges_filename, self.edges)
438        np.savetxt(dirpath / faces_filename, self.faces)
439        np.savetxt(dirpath / vertices_params_filename, self.vertices_params)
440        np.savetxt(dirpath / edges_params_filename, self.edges_params)
441        np.savetxt(dirpath / faces_params_filename, self.faces_params)
442        with (dirpath / constants_filename).open("w") as f:
443            f.write(f"{self.width} {self.height} {self.MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE}")
444
445    @classmethod
446    def load_mesh_txt(
447        cls,
448        directory: str,
449        vertices_filename: str = "vertTable.txt",
450        edges_filename: str = "heTable.txt",
451        faces_filename: str = "faceTable.txt",
452        vertices_params_filename: str = "vertParamsTable.txt",
453        edges_params_filename: str = "heParamsTable.txt",
454        faces_params_filename: str = "faceParamsTable.txt",
455        constants_filename: str = "constants.txt",
456    ) -> Self:
457        """Load a mesh from text files.
458
459        Load the vertices, edges and faces tables, the vertex, edge and face parameter tables and the
460        constants (width, height and MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE), one text file each.
461
462        Args:
463            directory (str): Directory where the text files are stored.
464            vertices_filename (str, optional): Filename for the vertices table. Defaults to "vertTable.txt".
465            edges_filename (str, optional): Filename for the half-edges table. Defaults to "heTable.txt".
466            faces_filename (str, optional): Filename for the faces table. Defaults to "faceTable.txt".
467            vertices_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the vertices parameters table.
468                    Defaults to "vertParamsTable.txt".
469            edges_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the half-edges parameters table.
470                    Defaults to "heParamsTable.txt".
471            faces_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the faces parameters table.
472                    Defaults to "faceParamsTable.txt".
473            constants_filename (str, optional): Filename for width/height/MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE.
474                    Defaults to "constants.txt".
475
476        Returns:
477            Self: The loaded mesh.
478        """
479        dirpath = Path(directory)
480        dirpath.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
481
482        mesh = cls._create()
483        # Index tables are WRITTEN by `np.savetxt` in float notation ('0.00...e+00'), so reading
484        # them with `dtype=np.int64` makes numpy parse an integer via a float -- a
485        # DeprecationWarning that this project's `filterwarnings = ["error"]` turns into a hard
486        # error, which is why this loader had no test. Read as float and cast, which also keeps
487        # every file written by earlier versions readable.
488        mesh.vertices = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / vertices_filename, dtype=np.float64))
489        mesh.edges = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / edges_filename, dtype=np.float64).astype(np.int64))
490        mesh.faces = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / faces_filename, dtype=np.float64).astype(np.int64))
491        # `edges_params` and `faces_params` are PHYSICAL PARAMETERS (tensions, target areas,
492        # shape factors), never indices, so they must be read as float: reading them with
493        # `dtype=np.int64` silently truncates -- a tension field of mean 1 and spread 0.1
494        # round-trips to all-ones, destroying the whole signal. See tests/test_mesh_txt_roundtrip.py.
495        mesh.vertices_params = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / vertices_params_filename, dtype=np.float64))
496        mesh.edges_params = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / edges_params_filename, dtype=np.float64))
497        mesh.faces_params = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / faces_params_filename, dtype=np.float64))
498        with (dirpath / constants_filename).open("r") as f:
499            numbers = f.readline().split()
500            mesh.width = float(numbers[0])
501            mesh.height = float(numbers[1])
502            mesh.MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE = int(numbers[2])
503        return mesh
504
505    def get_length(self, half_edge_id: Array) -> Array:
506        """Get the length of given edges."""
507
508        def _get_length(half_edge_id: Array) -> Array:
509            return get_length(half_edge_id, self.vertices, self.edges, self.faces, self.width, self.height)
510
511        return jax.vmap(_get_length)(half_edge_id)
512
513    def get_length_with_offset(self, half_edge_id: Array) -> Array:
514        """Get the length of given edges along with its offsets in an array (length, offset x, offset y)."""
515
516        def _get_length_with_offset(half_edge_id: Array) -> Array:
517            return get_length_with_offset(half_edge_id, self.vertices, self.edges, self.faces, self.width, self.height)
518
519        return jax.vmap(_get_length_with_offset)(half_edge_id)
520
521    def get_perimeter(self, face_id: Array) -> Array:
522        """Get the perimeter of given faces."""
523
524        def _get_perimeter(face_id: Array) -> Array:
525            return get_perimeter(
526                face_id, self.vertices, self.edges, self.faces, self.width, self.height, self.MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE
527            )
528
529        return jax.vmap(_get_perimeter)(face_id)
530
531    def get_area(self, face_id: Array) -> Array:
532        """Get the area of given faces."""
533
534        def _get_area(face_id: Array) -> Array:
535            return get_area(
536                face_id, self.vertices, self.edges, self.faces, self.width, self.height, self.MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE
537            )
538
539        return jax.vmap(_get_area)(face_id)

542        """Force periodic boundary conditions again after an update.
543
544        Most likely you'll never have to use it yourself, as it can be made automatically with a `PbcBilevelOptimizer`.
545        """
546        self.vertices, self.edges, self.faces = update_pbc(
547            self.vertices, self.edges, self.faces, self.width, self.height
548        )

Periodic Boundary Condition on a mesh.

For a PbcMesh, vertices is a 2D array of floats of size (nb_vertices, 2) ; with the coordinates of the vertices (in ]0, width[ x ]0, height[ ). The floats use JAX's default float dtype: float32, or float64 when jax_enable_x64 is enabled before the mesh is built.

edges is a 2D array of integers of size (nb_half_edges, 8), with:

  • id of previous half-edge,
  • id of next half-edge,
  • id of twin half-edge,
  • id of source vertex,
  • id of target vertex,
  • id of the face containing the half-edge.
  • x-offset (either -1, 0 or 1) depending on the target vertex crossing a boundary.
  • y-offset (either -1, 0 or 1) depending on the target vertex crossing a boundary.

faces is a 1D array of integers of size (nb_faces) containing the id of a half-edge belonging to this face.

@classmethod
def from_random_seeds(cls, nb_seeds: int, width: float, height: float, random_key: int) -> Self: 
57    @classmethod
58    def from_random_seeds(cls, nb_seeds: int, width: float, height: float, random_key: int) -> Self:
59        """Create a Periodic Boundary Conditions Mesh from a Voronoi diagram based on random seeds.
60
61        Args:
62            nb_seeds (int): Number of random seeds to use.
63            width (float): Width of the rectangular domains the seeds will be in.
64            height (float): Height of the rectangular domains the seeds will be in.
65            random_key (int): Set the random key for reproducibility.
66
67        Returns:
68            Self: The corresponding mesh.
69        """
70        key = jax.random.PRNGKey(random_key)
71        seeds = jnp.array((width, height)) * jax.random.uniform(key, (nb_seeds, 2))
72        try:
73            return cls.from_seeds(seeds, width, height)
74        except _FaceOrderingError as exc:
75            # `_make_he_structure` cannot name the seed, and the seed is what a caller varies.
76            msg = f"{exc} Reached from from_random_seeds(nb_seeds={nb_seeds}, random_key={random_key})."
77            raise _FaceOrderingError(msg) from exc

 80    def from_seeds(cls, seeds: Array, width: float, height: float) -> Self:
 81        """Create a Periodic Boundary Conditions Mesh from a Voronoi diagram based on a list of seeds.
 82
 83        The seeds are assumed to have positive x and y positions.
 84
 85        Args:
 86            seeds (Array): jax float array of seed positions of shape (nbSeeds, 2).
 87            width (float): width of the box containing the seeds.
 88            height (float): height of the box containing the seeds.
 89        """
 90        (
 91            periodic_voronoi_vertices_idx,
 92            periodic_voronoi_vertices_pos,
 93            periodic_voronoi_edges,
 94            offsets,
 95            periodic_voronoi_faces,
 96        ) = _make_periodic(seeds, width, height)
 97
 98        vertices, edges, faces = _make_he_structure(
 99            width,
100            height,
101            periodic_voronoi_vertices_idx,
102            periodic_voronoi_vertices_pos,
103            periodic_voronoi_edges,
104            offsets,
105            periodic_voronoi_faces,
106        )
107
108        pbc_mesh = cls._create()
109        pbc_mesh.vertices = jnp.array(vertices, dtype=jnp.result_type(float))
110        pbc_mesh.edges = jnp.array(edges, dtype=np.int32)
111        pbc_mesh.faces = jnp.array(faces, dtype=np.int32)
112        pbc_mesh.width = width
113        pbc_mesh.height = height
114
115        return pbc_mesh

117    @classmethod
118    def from_image(
119        cls,
120        image: NDArray,
121    ) -> Self:
122        """Create a rudimentary mesh with periodic boundary conditions from an image.
123
124        To do that, we perform a segmentation using Cellpose and we try to fill the holes.
125        The result will probably be imperfect and it will always be better if you
126        provide directly a mask (with no holes) with the function "periodic_from_mask".
127
128        The mask is made periodic by mirroring its edges.
129
130        Args:
131            image (NDArray): The image which will act as a template for the mesh.
132
133        Returns:
134            Self: The corresponding mesh.
135        
136        .. warning::
137
138            **Junction extraction is unreliable on real masks, and this method is currently
139            unsupported for them.** It builds the mesh with
140            `mask_analysis.find_vertices_edges_faces`, which keeps a label triple only where
141            exactly one 2x2 window carries it. A real trijunction is generally a small cluster of
142            windows, so genuine junctions are discarded and spurious short cycles close in their
143            place.
144
145            MEASURED on `examples/image.tif`, the image shipped with this method's own example:
146            `V - E + F = 55` and **472 faces from 64 segmented cells**. On a raw microscopy crop,
147            `V - E + F = 6`. A correct planar mesh gives 0.
148
149            For a segmented tissue, use :mod:`vertax.trace` instead, which extracts junctions on the
150            pixel-corner lattice and is tested against a stored reference.
151
152            **The gap is real and `vertax.trace` does not close it.** `trace` produces a *clamped
153            patch* -- a finite tissue fragment with a boundary -- not a periodic mesh. There is
154            currently **no working route from an image to a periodic mesh**. Substituting the
155            corner-lattice extraction here is the intended fix; it is deferred, and its three
156            preconditions are recorded in the freeze checklist.
157
158        """
159        return cls.from_mask(mask_from_image(image))

Create a rudimentary mesh with periodic boundary conditions from an image.

To do that, we perform a segmentation using Cellpose and we try to fill the holes. The result will probably be imperfect and it will always be better if you provide directly a mask (with no holes) with the function "periodic_from_mask".

The mask is made periodic by mirroring its edges.

Args: image (NDArray): The image which will act as a template for the mesh.

Returns: Self: The corresponding mesh.

Junction extraction is unreliable on real masks, and this method is currently unsupported for them. It builds the mesh with mask_analysis.find_vertices_edges_faces, which keeps a label triple only where exactly one 2x2 window carries it. A real trijunction is generally a small cluster of windows, so genuine junctions are discarded and spurious short cycles close in their place.

MEASURED on examples/image.tif, the image shipped with this method's own example: V - E + F = 55 and 472 faces from 64 segmented cells. On a raw microscopy crop, V - E + F = 6. A correct planar mesh gives 0.

For a segmented tissue, use vertax.trace instead, which extracts junctions on the pixel-corner lattice and is tested against a stored reference.

The gap is real and vertax.trace does not close it. trace produces a clamped patch -- a finite tissue fragment with a boundary -- not a periodic mesh. There is currently no working route from an image to a periodic mesh. Substituting the corner-lattice extraction here is the intended fix; it is deferred, and its three preconditions are recorded in the freeze checklist.

@classmethod
def from_mask( cls, mask: numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[+_ScalarType_co]]) -> Self: 
161    @classmethod
162    def from_mask(  # noqa: C901
163        cls,
164        mask: NDArray,
165    ) -> Self:
166        """Create a rudimentary mesh with periodic boundary conditions from a mask with no holes.
167
168        The mask is made periodic by mirroring its edges.
169
170        Args:
171            mask (NDArray): The mask with no holes which will act as a template for the mesh.
172
173        Returns:
174            Self: The corresponding mesh.
175        
176        .. warning::
177
178            **Junction extraction is unreliable on real masks, and this method is currently
179            unsupported for them.** It builds the mesh with
180            `mask_analysis.find_vertices_edges_faces`, which keeps a label triple only where
181            exactly one 2x2 window carries it. A real trijunction is generally a small cluster of
182            windows, so genuine junctions are discarded and spurious short cycles close in their
183            place.
184
185            MEASURED on `examples/image.tif`, the image shipped with this method's own example:
186            `V - E + F = 55` and **472 faces from 64 segmented cells**. On a raw microscopy crop,
187            `V - E + F = 6`. A correct planar mesh gives 0.
188
189            For a segmented tissue, use :mod:`vertax.trace` instead, which extracts junctions on the
190            pixel-corner lattice and is tested against a stored reference.
191
192            **The gap is real and `vertax.trace` does not close it.** `trace` produces a *clamped
193            patch* -- a finite tissue fragment with a boundary -- not a periodic mesh. There is
194            currently **no working route from an image to a periodic mesh**. Substituting the
195            corner-lattice extraction here is the intended fix; it is deferred, and its three
196            preconditions are recorded in the freeze checklist.
197
198        """
199        padded_mask = pad(mask, save=False, output_path="refined_and_padded_image.tiff")
200        # Find vertices, edges, faces
201        vertices, edges, faces = find_vertices_edges_faces(padded_mask)
202
203        # imread tiff = Y is the first axis, X the second.
204        height: int = mask.shape[0]  # original image length. Padded is 3 times bigger.
205        y_min = height / 2
206        y_max = 2 * height + (height / 2)
207        width: int = mask.shape[1]
208        x_min = width / 2
209        x_max = 2 * width + (width / 2)
210
211        col0_mask = (vertices[:, 0] >= x_min) & (vertices[:, 0] < x_max)
212        col1_mask = (vertices[:, 1] >= y_min) & (vertices[:, 1] < y_max)
213
214        periodic_vertices_idx = np.arange(len(vertices))[col0_mask & col1_mask]
215        periodic_vertices_pos = vertices[col0_mask & col1_mask]
216
217        # store map between vertex id -> inside vertex id
218        inside_vertex: dict[int, int] = {idx: idx for idx in periodic_vertices_idx}
219        for i, vertex in enumerate(vertices):
220            if i not in periodic_vertices_idx:
221                x, y = vertex
222                if x < x_min:
223                    x += 2 * width
224                elif x >= x_max:
225                    x -= 2 * width
226
227                if y < y_min:
228                    y += 2 * height
229                elif y >= y_max:
230                    y -= 2 * height
231
232                # Find corresponding inside vertex to the outside dest vertex
233                for idx, pos in zip(periodic_vertices_idx, periodic_vertices_pos, strict=True):
234                    if np.max(np.abs(pos - [x, y])) < 1:
235                        inside_vertex[i] = idx
236                        break
237
238        edges_inside = []
239        edges_outside = []
240        offsets_inside = {}
241        offsets_outside = {}
242        visited = []
243
244        for e in edges:
245            if e[0] in periodic_vertices_idx and e[1] in periodic_vertices_idx:
246                edges_inside.append(tuple(sorted((e[0], e[1]))))
247                offsets_inside[(e[0], e[1])] = (0, 0)
248                offsets_inside[(e[1], e[0])] = (0, 0)
249            elif bool(e[0] in periodic_vertices_idx) != bool(e[1] in periodic_vertices_idx):
250                if e[0] in periodic_vertices_idx:
251                    # origin in, dest out
252                    # check x coord
253                    if vertices[e[1]][0] < x_min:
254                        offset_x1 = -1
255                    elif vertices[e[1]][0] >= x_max:
256                        offset_x1 = 1
257                    else:
258                        offset_x1 = 0
259
260                    # Now check y coord
261                    if vertices[e[1]][1] < y_min:
262                        offset_y1 = -1
263                    elif vertices[e[1]][1] >= y_max:
264                        offset_y1 = 1
265                    else:
266                        offset_y1 = 0
267
268                    # Find corresponding inside vertex to the outside dest vertex
269                    if e[1] not in inside_vertex:
270                        print(f"Error, no inside vertex found for vertex {e[1]}.")
271                    else:
272                        idx = inside_vertex[e[1]]
273                        edges_outside.append(tuple(sorted((e[0], idx))))
274                        if (e[0], e[1]) not in visited and (e[1], e[0]) not in visited:
275                            offsets_outside[(e[0], idx)] = (offset_x1, offset_y1)
276                            offsets_outside[(idx, e[0])] = (-offset_x1, -offset_y1)
277                            visited.append((e[0], e[1]))
278                            visited.append((e[1], e[0]))
279                else:
280                    # dest in, origin out
281                    if vertices[e[0]][0] < x_min:
282                        offset_x0 = -1
283                    elif vertices[e[0]][0] >= x_max:
284                        offset_x0 = 1
285                    else:
286                        offset_x0 = 0
287
288                    if vertices[e[0]][1] < y_min:
289                        offset_y0 = -1
290                    elif vertices[e[0]][1] >= y_max:
291                        offset_y0 = 1
292                    else:
293                        offset_y0 = 0
294
295                    # Find corresponding inside vertex to the outside dest vertex
296                    if e[0] not in inside_vertex:
297                        print(f"Error, no inside vertex found for vertex {e[0]}.")
298                    else:
299                        idx = inside_vertex[e[0]]
300                        edges_outside.append(tuple(sorted((idx, e[1]))))
301                        if (e[0], e[1]) not in visited and (e[1], e[0]) not in visited:
302                            offsets_outside[(idx, e[1])] = (-offset_x0, -offset_y0)
303                            offsets_outside[(e[1], idx)] = (offset_x0, offset_y0)
304                            visited.append((e[0], e[1]))
305                            visited.append((e[1], e[0]))
306
307        periodic_edges = list(set(edges_inside)) + list(set(edges_outside))
308        offsets = offsets_inside | offsets_outside
309
310        periodic_faces: list[set[int]] = [
311            {inside_vertex[i] for i in face} for face in faces if any(v_id in periodic_vertices_idx for v_id in face)
312        ]
313
314        vertices, edges, faces = _make_he_structure(
315            2 * width,
316            2 * height,
317            periodic_vertices_idx,  # ty:ignore[invalid-argument-type]
318            periodic_vertices_pos,
319            periodic_edges,
320            offsets,
321            periodic_faces,
322            vertices_offset=(x_min, y_min),
323        )
324
325        pbc_mesh = cls._create()
326        pbc_mesh.vertices = jnp.array(vertices, dtype=jnp.result_type(float))
327        pbc_mesh.edges = jnp.array(edges, dtype=np.int32)
328        pbc_mesh.faces = jnp.array(faces, dtype=np.int32)
329        pbc_mesh.width = 2 * width
330        pbc_mesh.height = 2 * height
331
332        return pbc_mesh

340    def copy_mesh(cls, other_mesh: Self) -> Self:
341        """Copy all parameters from another mesh in a new mesh."""
342        mesh = cls._create()
343        mesh.vertices = other_mesh.vertices.copy()
344        mesh.edges = other_mesh.edges.copy()
345        mesh.faces = other_mesh.faces.copy()
346        mesh.width = other_mesh.width
347        mesh.height = other_mesh.height
348        mesh.vertices_params = other_mesh.vertices_params.copy()
349        mesh.edges_params = other_mesh.edges_params.copy()
350        mesh.faces_params = other_mesh.faces_params.copy()
351        mesh.MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE = other_mesh.MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE
352
353        return mesh

404    def save_mesh_txt(
405        self,

414    ) -> None:
415        """Save a mesh in separate text files that can be read by numpy.
416
417        Save the vertices, edges and faces tables, the vertex, edge and face parameter tables and the
418        constants (width, height and MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE), one text file each.
419
420        Args:
421            directory (str): Path to the directory where to save the files.
422            vertices_filename (str, optional): Filename for the vertices table. Defaults to "vertTable.txt".
423            edges_filename (str, optional): Filename for the half-edges table. Defaults to "heTable.txt".
424            faces_filename (str, optional): Filename for the faces table. Defaults to "faceTable.txt".
425            vertices_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the vertices parameters table.
426                    Defaults to "vertParamsTable.txt".
427            edges_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the half-edges parameters table.
428                    Defaults to "heParamsTable.txt".
429            faces_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the faces parameters table.
430                    Defaults to "faceParamsTable.txt".
431            constants_filename (str, optional): Filename for width/height/MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE.
432                    Defaults to "constants.txt".
433        """
434        dirpath = Path(directory)
435        dirpath.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
436        np.savetxt(dirpath / vertices_filename, self.vertices)
437        np.savetxt(dirpath / edges_filename, self.edges)
438        np.savetxt(dirpath / faces_filename, self.faces)
439        np.savetxt(dirpath / vertices_params_filename, self.vertices_params)
440        np.savetxt(dirpath / edges_params_filename, self.edges_params)
441        np.savetxt(dirpath / faces_params_filename, self.faces_params)
442        with (dirpath / constants_filename).open("w") as f:
443            f.write(f"{self.width} {self.height} {self.MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE}")

@classmethod
def load_mesh_txt( cls, directory: str, vertices_filename: str = 'vertTable.txt', edges_filename: str = 'heTable.txt', faces_filename: str = 'faceTable.txt', vertices_params_filename: str = 'vertParamsTable.txt', edges_params_filename: str = 'heParamsTable.txt', faces_params_filename: str = 'faceParamsTable.txt', constants_filename: str = 'constants.txt') -> Self: 
445    @classmethod
446    def load_mesh_txt(
447        cls,
448        directory: str,
449        vertices_filename: str = "vertTable.txt",
450        edges_filename: str = "heTable.txt",
451        faces_filename: str = "faceTable.txt",
452        vertices_params_filename: str = "vertParamsTable.txt",
453        edges_params_filename: str = "heParamsTable.txt",
454        faces_params_filename: str = "faceParamsTable.txt",
455        constants_filename: str = "constants.txt",
456    ) -> Self:
457        """Load a mesh from text files.
458
459        Load the vertices, edges and faces tables, the vertex, edge and face parameter tables and the
460        constants (width, height and MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE), one text file each.
461
462        Args:
463            directory (str): Directory where the text files are stored.
464            vertices_filename (str, optional): Filename for the vertices table. Defaults to "vertTable.txt".
465            edges_filename (str, optional): Filename for the half-edges table. Defaults to "heTable.txt".
466            faces_filename (str, optional): Filename for the faces table. Defaults to "faceTable.txt".
467            vertices_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the vertices parameters table.
468                    Defaults to "vertParamsTable.txt".
469            edges_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the half-edges parameters table.
470                    Defaults to "heParamsTable.txt".
471            faces_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the faces parameters table.
472                    Defaults to "faceParamsTable.txt".
473            constants_filename (str, optional): Filename for width/height/MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE.
474                    Defaults to "constants.txt".
475
476        Returns:
477            Self: The loaded mesh.
478        """
479        dirpath = Path(directory)
480        dirpath.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
481
482        mesh = cls._create()
483        # Index tables are WRITTEN by `np.savetxt` in float notation ('0.00...e+00'), so reading
484        # them with `dtype=np.int64` makes numpy parse an integer via a float -- a
485        # DeprecationWarning that this project's `filterwarnings = ["error"]` turns into a hard
486        # error, which is why this loader had no test. Read as float and cast, which also keeps
487        # every file written by earlier versions readable.
488        mesh.vertices = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / vertices_filename, dtype=np.float64))
489        mesh.edges = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / edges_filename, dtype=np.float64).astype(np.int64))
490        mesh.faces = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / faces_filename, dtype=np.float64).astype(np.int64))
491        # `edges_params` and `faces_params` are PHYSICAL PARAMETERS (tensions, target areas,
492        # shape factors), never indices, so they must be read as float: reading them with
493        # `dtype=np.int64` silently truncates -- a tension field of mean 1 and spread 0.1
494        # round-trips to all-ones, destroying the whole signal. See tests/test_mesh_txt_roundtrip.py.
495        mesh.vertices_params = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / vertices_params_filename, dtype=np.float64))
496        mesh.edges_params = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / edges_params_filename, dtype=np.float64))
497        mesh.faces_params = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / faces_params_filename, dtype=np.float64))
498        with (dirpath / constants_filename).open("r") as f:
499            numbers = f.readline().split()
500            mesh.width = float(numbers[0])
501            mesh.height = float(numbers[1])
502            mesh.MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE = int(numbers[2])
503        return mesh
