541    def update_boundary_conditions(self) -> None:
542        """Force periodic boundary conditions again after an update.
543
544        Most likely you'll never have to use it yourself, as it can be made automatically with a `PbcBilevelOptimizer`.
545        """
546        self.vertices, self.edges, self.faces = update_pbc(
547            self.vertices, self.edges, self.faces, self.width, self.height
548        )

Force periodic boundary conditions again after an update.

Most likely you'll never have to use it yourself, as it can be made automatically with a PbcBilevelOptimizer.

class BoundedMesh(vertax.Mesh): 
 77class BoundedMesh(Mesh):
 78    """Bounded mesh with arc circles for boundary cells.
 79
 80    For a BoundedMesh, `vertices` is a 2D array of floats of size (nb_vertices, 2) ;
 81    with the coordinates of the vertices (in ]0, width[ x ]0, height[ ).
 82
 83    `edges` is a  2D array of integers of size (nb_half_edges, 8), with:
 84
 85    - id of previous half-edge,
 86    - id of next half-edge,
 87    - id of twin half-edge,
 88    - id of source vertex + 2 if current half-edge is an inside edge, else 0,
 89    - id of target vertex + 2 if current half-edge is an inside edge, else 1,
 90    - id of source vertex + 2 if current half-edge is an outside edge, else 0,
 91    - id of target vertex + 2 if current half-edge is an outside edge, else 1,
 92    - id of the face containing the half-edge.
 93
 94    `faces` is a 2D array of integers of size (nb_faces, 2), with:
 95
 96    - id of a half-edge belonging to the face,
 97    - fate marker of the cell, between 0 and `nb_fates - 1` (see `from_seeds`).
 98
 99    `angles` is a 1D array of floats of size (nb_angles), with the angles sustaining the arcs of the free interfaces ;
100    between 0 and PI / 2.
101
102    Every face is traversed counterclockwise (`from_seeds` orders it so, and T1 transitions keep it),
103    and the arc of a free interface bulges to the right of the directed chord of its half-edge, away
104    from the cell. Cell areas (`vertax.geo`) rely on this orientation and do not read it from the
105    sign of a cell's chord polygon, which turns over when the cell's interior vertices cross the
106    chord of its arc while the cell keeps its side. A mesh built outside VertAX must therefore list
107    its faces counterclockwise; `load_mesh` and `load_mesh_txt` refuse a clockwise mesh.
108
109    The floats of `vertices` and `angles` use JAX's default float dtype: `float32`, or `float64` when
110    `jax_enable_x64` is enabled before the mesh is built.
111    """
112
113    def __init__(self) -> None:
114        """Do not call the constructor."""
115        super().__init__()
116        self.angles: Array = jnp.array([])
117        """Angle sustaining the arced free interfaces. Between 0 and PI / 2."""
118
119    @property
120    def nb_angles(self) -> int:
121        """Get the number of angles (free interfaces) of the mesh."""
122        return len(self.angles)
123
124    @classmethod
125    def from_random_seeds(cls, nb_seeds: int, width: float, height: float, random_key: int, nb_fates: int = 2) -> Self:
126        """Create a bounded Mesh from random seeds, based on a Voronoi diagram with arced free interfaces.
127
128        Args:
129            nb_seeds (int): Number of random seeds to use.
130            width (float): width of the box containing the seeds.
131            height (float): height of the box containing the seeds.
132            random_key (int): seed for a random number generator to add new seeds if needed, decide on cell fates...
133            nb_fates (int, default=2): number of possible different fate marker for a cell.
134
135        Returns:
136            Self: The corresponding mesh.
137        """
138        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=random_key)
139        seeds = rng.random((nb_seeds, 2)) * (width, height)
140        return cls.from_seeds(seeds, width, height, random_key, nb_fates)
141
142    @classmethod
143    def from_seeds(cls, seeds: NDArray, width: float, height: float, random_key: int, nb_fates: int = 2) -> Self:  # noqa: C901
144        """Create a bounded Mesh from a list of given seeds.
145
146        The seeds are assumed to have x-coordinate in ]0, width[ and y-coordinate in ]0, height[.
147        Note that the final mesh might not use your seeds if they don't work to create a correct
148        bounded mesh via our method.
149
150        Args:
151            seeds (Array): jax float array of seed positions of shape (nbSeeds, 2).
152            width (float): width of the box containing the seeds.
153            height (float): height of the box containing the seeds.
154            random_key (int): seed for a random number generator to add new seeds if needed, decide on cell fates...
155            nb_fates (int, default=2): number of possible different fate marker for a cell.
156        """
157        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=random_key)
158        n_cells = len(seeds)  # starting number of seeds must be equal to the desired number of cells (faces)
159
160        # We'll try to construct a Voronoi diagram with n_cells closed (bounded) cells.
161        # This will not work with exactly n_cells seeds because there will be unbounded cells.
162        # If the number of bounded cells is insufficient, we add a new seed to the list.
163        # If there is too many bounded cells, we retry with entirely new seeds.
164        # We also check that the bounded cells are connected.
165        while True:
166            success = 0  # if 1 : not enough bounded cells. If 2 : too many bounded cells.
167
168            # Create the Voronoi diagrams from current seed list.
169            voronoi = Voronoi(seeds)
170            vertices = voronoi.vertices
171            edges = voronoi.ridge_vertices
172            faces = voronoi.regions  # regions = faces = cells
173
174            # We count the number of bounded cells and the connectivity of vertices.
175            inbound_faces = []
176            inbound_vertices = np.zeros(vertices.shape[0], dtype=np.int32)
177            for face in faces:
178                if face and all(item > -1 for item in face):  # the face must not be an empty list
179                    face_vertices_positions = vertices[face]
180                    # We check that all of the face's vertices are in a box [0, width]x[0, height]
181                    if (
182                        np.all(face_vertices_positions[:, 0] < width)
183                        and np.all(face_vertices_positions[:, 1] < height)
184                        and np.all(face_vertices_positions > 0)
185                    ):
186                        inbound_faces.append(face)  # the face is bounded
187                        inbound_vertices[face] += 1  # +1 to the connectivity of the face's vertices.
188
189            # getting rid of faces connected to a single other inbound face
190            # (these can be problematic and lead to many special cases later on)
191            while True:
192                num_infaces = len(inbound_faces)
193                del_count = 0
194                for i, face in enumerate(reversed(inbound_faces)):
195                    # only 2 (or less (not sure it's possible)) vertices of the face are shared with other faces :
196                    # that means it is connected to one other bounded face only -> We remove it.
197                    if np.sum(inbound_vertices[face] > 1) <= 2:
198                        inbound_vertices[face] -= 1
199                        del inbound_faces[num_infaces - i - 1]
200                        del_count += 1
201                # Removing one face can possibly alter other faces so we might do another loop.
202                # We stop when there is no more face to remove.
203                if del_count == 0:
204                    break
205
206            # Check that we have the correct number of cells.
207            if num_infaces < n_cells:
208                success = 1
209            elif num_infaces > n_cells:
210                success = 2
211            else:
212                # There is exactly n_cells connected bounded faces.
213                # Now, it is possible that a bounded face has vertices or edges
214                # that are not shared with other faces. We get rid of those,
215                # in order to have only one exterior edge that will be an arc circle.
216                for i, face in enumerate(inbound_faces):
217                    useful_vertices = []  # List of the face vertices that are shared with other.
218                    # (We'll keep them and call them "useful").
219                    extra_edges = []  # List of edges to replace what we have removed
220                    last_useful = -1  # ID of the last "useful" vertex. -1 at the beginning (we'll treat that case)
221                    new_edge = []  # New edge that will replace current vertices we're trying to remove
222                    incomplete_new_edge = False  # State boolean : are we replacing vertices right now ?
223                    for vertex in face:
224                        if inbound_vertices[vertex] == 1:  # We found a vertex that is not shared with other faces.
225                            # We plan to remove it by not adding it to the useful vertices list,
226                            # and by creating a new edge from last useful vertex to the next one.
227                            if not incomplete_new_edge:  # Detect if we're not already in the incomplete edge state
228                                new_edge = []  # re-init
229                                new_edge.append(last_useful)
230                                incomplete_new_edge = True  # Move to incomplete edge state.
231                        else:  # We found a useful vertex
232                            useful_vertices.append(vertex)
233                            last_useful = vertex
234                            if incomplete_new_edge:  # If in incomplete edge state we can finally close the new edge.
235                                new_edge.append(vertex)
236                                extra_edges.append(new_edge)
237                                incomplete_new_edge = False
238                    # After looping through the vertices of the face, we need to take care of
239                    # two special cases : the first or the last vertex is not shared.
240                    if extra_edges and extra_edges[0][0] == -1:
241                        extra_edges[0][0] = useful_vertices[-1]
242                    elif incomplete_new_edge:
243                        new_edge.append(useful_vertices[0])
244                        extra_edges.append(new_edge)
245                    # The extra edges are added to the list of all edges
246                    edges.extend(extra_edges)
247                    inbound_faces[i] = tuple(
248                        sorted(useful_vertices)
249                    )  # And the face itself is replaced by only the useful vertices.
250                    # Note that the vertices here are not ordered in clockwise or counterclockwise order anymore.
251                useful_vertices_set = set(np.where(inbound_vertices > 1)[0])  # We filter the useful vertices.
252
253                # HALF EDGE DATA STRUCTURE
254                # Filter edges with useful vertices only.
255                useful_edges = [tuple(sorted(e)) for e in edges if set(e).issubset(useful_vertices_set)]
256
257                # failing to abide by the following relation results in disconnected topologies
258                if len(useful_edges) != (n_cells - 1) * 3:
259                    success = 2  # Case : we want to restart with new seeds because current solution is not OK.
260                else:
261                    # We construct the half-edges.
262                    half_edges = []
263                    for e in useful_edges:
264                        half_edges.append(e)
265                        # reciprocating edges
266                        half_edges.append((e[1], e[0]))
267
268                    # finding clockwise (or counterclockwise) half edge set for each face,
269                    # as we broke it earlier.
270                    ordered_edges_inbound_faces = []
271                    for face in inbound_faces:
272                        # Find all edges fon this face and we'll loow through them to order them.
273                        edges_face = [(f1, f2) for f1 in face for f2 in face if (f1, f2) in useful_edges]
274
275                        i = 0
276                        start_edge = edges_face[i]
277                        ordered_face = [start_edge]
278                        e = start_edge
279                        visited = [e]
280                        while sorted(edges_face) != sorted(visited):
281                            if e[0] == start_edge[1] and e not in visited:
282                                ordered_face.append(e)
283                                start_edge = e
284                                visited.append(e)
285                            # We must be careful because some edges might be in the wrong order.
286                            if e[1] == start_edge[1] and e not in visited:
287                                ordered_face.append((e[1], e[0]))
288                                start_edge = (e[1], e[0])
289                                visited.append(e)
290                            i += 1
291                            e = edges_face[i % len(edges_face)]
292
293                        # Sanity check : do we have a correct ordering ?
294                        order = 0
295                        for e in ordered_face:
296                            idx0 = e[0]
297                            idx1 = e[1]
298
299                            order += (vertices[idx1][0] - vertices[idx0][0]) * (vertices[idx1][1] + vertices[idx0][1])
300
301                        if order < 0:
302                            ordered_edges_inbound_faces.append(ordered_face)
303                        if order > 0:
304                            ordered_edges_inbound_faces.append([(e[1], e[0]) for e in reversed(ordered_face)])
305                        if order == 0:
306                            print("\nError: no order detected for face " + str(face) + "\n")
307                            exit()
308
309                    # Now we fill the tables with the info we have.
310                    useful_vertices_list = list(useful_vertices_set)
311                    vertTable = np.zeros((len(useful_vertices_list), 2))
312                    for i, idx in enumerate(useful_vertices_list):
313                        pos = vertices[idx]
314                        vertTable[i][0] = pos[0]  # x pos vert
315                        vertTable[i][1] = pos[1]  # y pos vert
316
317                    faceTable = np.zeros((len(inbound_faces), 1), dtype=np.int32)
318                    for i, hedges_face in enumerate(ordered_edges_inbound_faces):
319                        for j, he in enumerate(half_edges):
320                            if he == hedges_face[0]:
321                                faceTable[i] = j  # he_inside
322                    faceTable = _fate_selection(faceTable, nb_fates, rng)
323
324                    nb_half_edges = len(half_edges)
325                    heTable = np.zeros((nb_half_edges, 8), dtype=np.int32)
326                    heTable[:, 4] = 1
327                    heTable[:, 6] = 1
328                    relevant_twins = []
329                    # HE TABLE :
330                    # 0 : previous half-edge.
331                    # 1 : next half-edge.
332                    # 2 : twin half-edge.
333                    # 3 : source vertex id + 2 if edge is inside, 0 if the edge is outside
334                    # 4 : target vertex id + 2 if edge is inside, 0 if the edge is outside
335                    # 5 : source vertex id + 2 if edge is outside, 0 if the edge is inside
336                    # 6 : target vertex id + 2 if edge is outside, 0 if the edge is inside
337                    # 7 : id of the face containing this half-edge.
338                    for i, he in enumerate(half_edges):
339                        belongs_to_any_face = False
340                        for hedges_face in ordered_edges_inbound_faces:
341                            if he in hedges_face:
342                                idx = hedges_face.index(he)
343                                heTable[i][0] = half_edges.index(hedges_face[(idx - 1) % len(hedges_face)])  # he_prev
344                                heTable[i][1] = half_edges.index(hedges_face[(idx + 1) % len(hedges_face)])  # he_next
345                                # indices 0 and 1 are reserved for source or target vertices of "outside" edges.
346                                # So we have to add +2 to other indices.
347                                heTable[i][3] = useful_vertices_list.index(he[0]) + 2  # vert source inner edges
348                                heTable[i][4] = useful_vertices_list.index(he[1]) + 2  # vert target inner edges
349                                heTable[i][7] = ordered_edges_inbound_faces.index(hedges_face)  # face
350                                belongs_to_any_face = True
351                                break
352                        twin_idx = half_edges.index((he[1], he[0]))
353                        heTable[i][2] = twin_idx  # he twin
354                        if not belongs_to_any_face:
355                            relevant_twins.append(twin_idx)
356
357                    # Angles are randomly chosen between 0 and pi/2 (with some margin to avoid extreme cases).
358                    angTable = np.ones(nb_half_edges // 2)
359                    for tidx in relevant_twins:
360                        angTable[tidx // 2] = rng.random() * (np.pi / 2 - 0.018) + 0.017
361                        heTable[tidx][5] = heTable[tidx][3]  # vert source surface edges
362                        heTable[tidx][6] = heTable[tidx][4]  # vert target surface edges
363                        heTable[tidx][3] = 0
364                        heTable[tidx][4] = 1
365
366                    bounded_mesh = cls._create()
367                    bounded_mesh.vertices = jnp.array(vertTable, dtype=jnp.result_type(float))
368                    bounded_mesh.angles = jnp.array(angTable, dtype=jnp.result_type(float))
369                    bounded_mesh.faces = jnp.array(faceTable, dtype=np.int32)
370                    bounded_mesh.edges = jnp.array(heTable, dtype=np.int32)
371                    bounded_mesh.width = width
372                    bounded_mesh.height = height
373
374                    _check_face_orientation(bounded_mesh, "BoundedMesh.from_seeds")
375                    return bounded_mesh
376
377            # If success was 1, we had not enough bounded faces, we add a new seed to see if it helps.
378            # Otherwise we retry with new seeds entirely.
379            seeds = (
380                np.vstack([seeds, (width, height) * rng.random((1, 2))])
381                if success == 1
382                else (width, height) * rng.random((n_cells, 2))
383            )  # type: ignore
384
385    @classmethod
386    def create_empty(cls) -> Self:
387        """Create an empty mesh. Use if you know what you're doing !"""
388        return cls._create()
389
390    @classmethod
391    def copy_mesh(cls, other_mesh: Self) -> Self:
392        """Copy all parameters from another mesh in a new mesh."""
393        mesh = cls._create()
394        mesh.vertices = other_mesh.vertices.copy()
395        mesh.edges = other_mesh.edges.copy()
396        mesh.faces = other_mesh.faces.copy()
397        mesh.angles = other_mesh.angles.copy()
398        mesh.width = other_mesh.width
399        mesh.height = other_mesh.height
400        mesh.vertices_params = other_mesh.vertices_params.copy()
401        mesh.edges_params = other_mesh.edges_params.copy()
402        mesh.faces_params = other_mesh.faces_params.copy()
403
404        return mesh
405
406    def save_mesh(self, path: str) -> None:
407        """Save mesh to a file.
408
409        All BoundedMesh data is saved.
410
411        Args:
412            path (str): Path to the saved file. The extension is .npz.
413        """
414        Path(path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
415        np.savez_compressed(
416            path,
417            allow_pickle=False,
418            vertices=self.vertices,
419            edges=self.edges,
420            faces=self.faces,
421            angles=self.angles,
422            width=self.width,
423            height=self.height,
424            vertices_params=self.vertices_params,
425            edges_params=self.edges_params,
426            faces_params=self.faces_params,
427        )
428
429    @classmethod
430    def load_mesh(cls, path: str) -> Self:
431        """Load a mesh from a file.
432
433        All BoundedMesh data is reloaded.
434
435        Args:
436            path (str): Path to the mesh file (.npz).
437
438        Returns:
439            Mesh: the mesh loaded from the .npz file.
440
441        Raises:
442            ValueError: if the faces of the mesh are clockwise (see `BoundedMesh`).
443
444        Warns:
445            UserWarning: if some faces have a turned-over chord polygon (a crescent, or a fold).
446        """
447        mesh_file = np.load(path)
448        mesh = cls._create()
449        mesh.vertices, mesh.edges, mesh.faces, mesh.angles = (
450            mesh_file["vertices"],
451            mesh_file["edges"],
452            mesh_file["faces"],
453            mesh_file["angles"],
454        )
455        mesh.width = mesh_file["width"]
456        mesh.height = mesh_file["height"]
457        mesh.vertices_params = mesh_file["vertices_params"]
458        mesh.edges_params = mesh_file["edges_params"]
459        mesh.faces_params = mesh_file["faces_params"]
460        _check_face_orientation(mesh, f"BoundedMesh.load_mesh({path!r})")
461        return mesh
462
463    def save_mesh_txt(
464        self,
465        directory: str,
466        vertices_filename: str = "vertTable.txt",
467        angles_filename: str = "angTable.txt",
468        edges_filename: str = "heTable.txt",
469        faces_filename: str = "faceTable.txt",
470        vertices_params_filename: str = "vertParamsTable.txt",
471        edges_params_filename: str = "heParamsTable.txt",
472        faces_params_filename: str = "faceParamsTable.txt",
473        constants_filename: str = "constants.txt",
474    ) -> None:
475        """Save a mesh in separate text files that can be read by numpy.
476
477        Save the vertices, angles, edges and faces tables, the vertex, edge and face parameter tables and the
478        constants (width and height), one text file each.
479
480        Args:
481            directory (str): Path to the directory where to save the files.
482            vertices_filename (str, optional): Filename for the vertices table. Defaults to "vertTable.txt".
483            angles_filename (str, optional): Filename for the angles table. Defaults to "angTable.txt".
484            edges_filename (str, optional): Filename for the half-edges table. Defaults to "heTable.txt".
485            faces_filename (str, optional): Filename for the faces table. Defaults to "faceTable.txt".
486            vertices_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the vertices parameters table.
487                    Defaults to "vertParamsTable.txt".
488            edges_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the half-edges parameters table.
489                    Defaults to "heParamsTable.txt".
490            faces_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the faces parameters table.
491                    Defaults to "faceParamsTable.txt".
492            constants_filename (str, optional): Filename for width/height.
493                    Defaults to "constants.txt".
494        """
495        dirpath = Path(directory)
496        dirpath.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
497        np.savetxt(dirpath / vertices_filename, self.vertices)
498        np.savetxt(dirpath / angles_filename, self.angles)
499        np.savetxt(dirpath / edges_filename, self.edges)
500        np.savetxt(dirpath / faces_filename, self.faces)
501        np.savetxt(dirpath / vertices_params_filename, self.vertices_params)
502        np.savetxt(dirpath / edges_params_filename, self.edges_params)
503        np.savetxt(dirpath / faces_params_filename, self.faces_params)
504        with (dirpath / constants_filename).open("w") as f:
505            f.write(f"{self.width} {self.height}")
506
507    @classmethod
508    def load_mesh_txt(
509        cls,
510        directory: str,
511        vertices_filename: str = "vertTable.txt",
512        angles_filename: str = "angTable.txt",
513        edges_filename: str = "heTable.txt",
514        faces_filename: str = "faceTable.txt",
515        vertices_params_filename: str = "vertParamsTable.txt",
516        edges_params_filename: str = "heParamsTable.txt",
517        faces_params_filename: str = "faceParamsTable.txt",
518        constants_filename: str = "constants.txt",
519    ) -> Self:
520        """Load a mesh from text files.
521
522        Load the vertices, angles, edges and faces tables, the vertex, edge and face parameter tables and the
523        constants (width and height), one text file each.
524
525        Args:
526            directory (str): Directory where the text files are stored.
527            vertices_filename (str, optional): Filename for the vertices table. Defaults to "vertTable.txt".
528            angles_filename (str, optional): Filename for the angles table. Defaults to "angTable.txt".
529            edges_filename (str, optional): Filename for the half-edges table. Defaults to "heTable.txt".
530            faces_filename (str, optional): Filename for the faces table. Defaults to "faceTable.txt".
531            vertices_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the vertices parameters table.
532                    Defaults to "vertParamsTable.txt".
533            edges_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the half-edges parameters table.
534                    Defaults to "heParamsTable.txt".
535            faces_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the faces parameters table.
536                    Defaults to "faceParamsTable.txt".
537            constants_filename (str, optional): Filename for width/height/MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE.
538                    Defaults to "constants.txt".
539
540        Returns:
541            Self: The loaded mesh.
542
543        Raises:
544            ValueError: if the faces of the mesh are clockwise (see `BoundedMesh`).
545
546        Warns:
547            UserWarning: if some faces have a turned-over chord polygon (a crescent, or a fold).
548        """
549        dirpath = Path(directory)
550        dirpath.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
551
552        mesh = cls._create()
553        # Index tables are WRITTEN by `np.savetxt` in float notation ('0.00...e+00'), so reading
554        # them with `dtype=np.int64` makes numpy parse an integer via a float -- a
555        # DeprecationWarning that this project's `filterwarnings = ["error"]` turns into a hard
556        # error, which is why this loader had no test. Read as float and cast, which also keeps
557        # every file written by earlier versions readable.
558        mesh.vertices = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / vertices_filename, dtype=np.float64))
559        mesh.angles = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / angles_filename, dtype=np.float64))
560        mesh.edges = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / edges_filename, dtype=np.float64).astype(np.int64))
561        mesh.faces = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / faces_filename, dtype=np.float64).astype(np.int64))
562        # `edges_params` and `faces_params` are PHYSICAL PARAMETERS (tensions, target areas,
563        # shape factors), never indices, so they must be read as float: reading them with
564        # `dtype=np.int64` silently truncates -- a tension field of mean 1 and spread 0.1
565        # round-trips to all-ones, destroying the whole signal. See tests/test_mesh_txt_roundtrip.py.
566        mesh.vertices_params = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / vertices_params_filename, dtype=np.float64))
567        mesh.edges_params = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / edges_params_filename, dtype=np.float64))
568        mesh.faces_params = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / faces_params_filename, dtype=np.float64))
569        with (dirpath / constants_filename).open("r") as f:
570            numbers = f.readline().split()
571            mesh.width = float(numbers[0])
572            mesh.height = float(numbers[1])
573        _check_face_orientation(mesh, f"BoundedMesh.load_mesh_txt({str(directory)!r})")
574        return mesh
575
576    def get_length(self, half_edge_id: Array) -> Array:
577        """Get the length of an edge."""
578        vertTable = jnp.vstack([jnp.array([[0.0, 0.0], [1.0, 1.0]]), self.vertices])
579        angTable = jnp.repeat(self.angles, 2)
580
581        def _get_length(half_edge_id: Array) -> Array:
582            return get_any_length(half_edge_id, vertTable, angTable, self.edges)
583
584        return jax.vmap(_get_length)(half_edge_id)
585
586    def get_perimeter(self, face_id: Array) -> Array:
587        """Get the area of a face."""
588        vertTable = jnp.vstack([jnp.array([[0.0, 0.0], [1.0, 1.0]]), self.vertices])
589        angTable = jnp.repeat(self.angles, 2)
590
591        def _get_perimeter(face_id: Array) -> Array:
592            return get_perimeter_bounded(face_id, vertTable, angTable, self.edges, self.faces)
593
594        return jax.vmap(_get_perimeter)(face_id)
595
596    def get_area(self, face_id: Array) -> Array:
597        """Get the area of a face."""
598        vertTable = jnp.vstack([jnp.array([[0.0, 0.0], [1.0, 1.0]]), self.vertices])
599        angTable = jnp.repeat(self.angles, 2)
600
601        def _get_area(face_id: Array) -> Array:
602            return get_area_bounded(face_id, vertTable, angTable, self.edges, self.faces)
603
604        return jax.vmap(_get_area)(face_id)

Bounded mesh with arc circles for boundary cells.

For a BoundedMesh, vertices is a 2D array of floats of size (nb_vertices, 2) ; with the coordinates of the vertices (in ]0, width[ x ]0, height[ ).

edges is a 2D array of integers of size (nb_half_edges, 8), with:

  • id of previous half-edge,
  • id of next half-edge,
  • id of twin half-edge,
  • id of source vertex + 2 if current half-edge is an inside edge, else 0,
  • id of target vertex + 2 if current half-edge is an inside edge, else 1,
  • id of source vertex + 2 if current half-edge is an outside edge, else 0,
  • id of target vertex + 2 if current half-edge is an outside edge, else 1,
  • id of the face containing the half-edge.

faces is a 2D array of integers of size (nb_faces, 2), with:

  • id of a half-edge belonging to the face,
  • fate marker of the cell, between 0 and nb_fates - 1 (see from_seeds).

angles is a 1D array of floats of size (nb_angles), with the angles sustaining the arcs of the free interfaces ; between 0 and PI / 2.

Every face is traversed counterclockwise (from_seeds orders it so, and T1 transitions keep it), and the arc of a free interface bulges to the right of the directed chord of its half-edge, away from the cell. Cell areas (vertax.geo) rely on this orientation and do not read it from the sign of a cell's chord polygon, which turns over when the cell's interior vertices cross the chord of its arc while the cell keeps its side. A mesh built outside VertAX must therefore list its faces counterclockwise; load_mesh and load_mesh_txt refuse a clockwise mesh.

The floats of vertices and angles use JAX's default float dtype: float32, or float64 when jax_enable_x64 is enabled before the mesh is built.

@classmethod
def from_random_seeds( cls, nb_seeds: int, width: float, height: float, random_key: int, nb_fates: int = 2) -> Self: 
124    @classmethod
125    def from_random_seeds(cls, nb_seeds: int, width: float, height: float, random_key: int, nb_fates: int = 2) -> Self:
126        """Create a bounded Mesh from random seeds, based on a Voronoi diagram with arced free interfaces.
127
128        Args:
129            nb_seeds (int): Number of random seeds to use.
130            width (float): width of the box containing the seeds.
131            height (float): height of the box containing the seeds.
132            random_key (int): seed for a random number generator to add new seeds if needed, decide on cell fates...
133            nb_fates (int, default=2): number of possible different fate marker for a cell.
134
135        Returns:
136            Self: The corresponding mesh.
137        """
138        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=random_key)
139        seeds = rng.random((nb_seeds, 2)) * (width, height)
140        return cls.from_seeds(seeds, width, height, random_key, nb_fates)

Create a bounded Mesh from random seeds, based on a Voronoi diagram with arced free interfaces.

Args: nb_seeds (int): Number of random seeds to use. width (float): width of the box containing the seeds. height (float): height of the box containing the seeds. random_key (int): seed for a random number generator to add new seeds if needed, decide on cell fates... nb_fates (int, default=2): number of possible different fate marker for a cell.

Returns: Self: The corresponding mesh.

@classmethod
def from_seeds( cls, seeds: numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[+_ScalarType_co]], width: float, height: float, random_key: int, nb_fates: int = 2) -> Self: 
142    @classmethod
143    def from_seeds(cls, seeds: NDArray, width: float, height: float, random_key: int, nb_fates: int = 2) -> Self:  # noqa: C901
144        """Create a bounded Mesh from a list of given seeds.
145
146        The seeds are assumed to have x-coordinate in ]0, width[ and y-coordinate in ]0, height[.
147        Note that the final mesh might not use your seeds if they don't work to create a correct
148        bounded mesh via our method.
149
150        Args:
151            seeds (Array): jax float array of seed positions of shape (nbSeeds, 2).
152            width (float): width of the box containing the seeds.
153            height (float): height of the box containing the seeds.
154            random_key (int): seed for a random number generator to add new seeds if needed, decide on cell fates...
155            nb_fates (int, default=2): number of possible different fate marker for a cell.
156        """
157        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=random_key)
158        n_cells = len(seeds)  # starting number of seeds must be equal to the desired number of cells (faces)
159
160        # We'll try to construct a Voronoi diagram with n_cells closed (bounded) cells.
161        # This will not work with exactly n_cells seeds because there will be unbounded cells.
162        # If the number of bounded cells is insufficient, we add a new seed to the list.
163        # If there is too many bounded cells, we retry with entirely new seeds.
164        # We also check that the bounded cells are connected.
165        while True:
166            success = 0  # if 1 : not enough bounded cells. If 2 : too many bounded cells.
167
168            # Create the Voronoi diagrams from current seed list.
169            voronoi = Voronoi(seeds)
170            vertices = voronoi.vertices
171            edges = voronoi.ridge_vertices
172            faces = voronoi.regions  # regions = faces = cells
173
174            # We count the number of bounded cells and the connectivity of vertices.
175            inbound_faces = []
176            inbound_vertices = np.zeros(vertices.shape[0], dtype=np.int32)
177            for face in faces:
178                if face and all(item > -1 for item in face):  # the face must not be an empty list
179                    face_vertices_positions = vertices[face]
180                    # We check that all of the face's vertices are in a box [0, width]x[0, height]
181                    if (
182                        np.all(face_vertices_positions[:, 0] < width)
183                        and np.all(face_vertices_positions[:, 1] < height)
184                        and np.all(face_vertices_positions > 0)
185                    ):
186                        inbound_faces.append(face)  # the face is bounded
187                        inbound_vertices[face] += 1  # +1 to the connectivity of the face's vertices.
188
189            # getting rid of faces connected to a single other inbound face
190            # (these can be problematic and lead to many special cases later on)
191            while True:
192                num_infaces = len(inbound_faces)
193                del_count = 0
194                for i, face in enumerate(reversed(inbound_faces)):
195                    # only 2 (or less (not sure it's possible)) vertices of the face are shared with other faces :
196                    # that means it is connected to one other bounded face only -> We remove it.
197                    if np.sum(inbound_vertices[face] > 1) <= 2:
198                        inbound_vertices[face] -= 1
199                        del inbound_faces[num_infaces - i - 1]
200                        del_count += 1
201                # Removing one face can possibly alter other faces so we might do another loop.
202                # We stop when there is no more face to remove.
203                if del_count == 0:
204                    break
205
206            # Check that we have the correct number of cells.
207            if num_infaces < n_cells:
208                success = 1
209            elif num_infaces > n_cells:
210                success = 2
211            else:
212                # There is exactly n_cells connected bounded faces.
213                # Now, it is possible that a bounded face has vertices or edges
214                # that are not shared with other faces. We get rid of those,
215                # in order to have only one exterior edge that will be an arc circle.
216                for i, face in enumerate(inbound_faces):
217                    useful_vertices = []  # List of the face vertices that are shared with other.
218                    # (We'll keep them and call them "useful").
219                    extra_edges = []  # List of edges to replace what we have removed
220                    last_useful = -1  # ID of the last "useful" vertex. -1 at the beginning (we'll treat that case)
221                    new_edge = []  # New edge that will replace current vertices we're trying to remove
222                    incomplete_new_edge = False  # State boolean : are we replacing vertices right now ?
223                    for vertex in face:
224                        if inbound_vertices[vertex] == 1:  # We found a vertex that is not shared with other faces.
225                            # We plan to remove it by not adding it to the useful vertices list,
226                            # and by creating a new edge from last useful vertex to the next one.
227                            if not incomplete_new_edge:  # Detect if we're not already in the incomplete edge state
228                                new_edge = []  # re-init
229                                new_edge.append(last_useful)
230                                incomplete_new_edge = True  # Move to incomplete edge state.
231                        else:  # We found a useful vertex
232                            useful_vertices.append(vertex)
233                            last_useful = vertex
234                            if incomplete_new_edge:  # If in incomplete edge state we can finally close the new edge.
235                                new_edge.append(vertex)
236                                extra_edges.append(new_edge)
237                                incomplete_new_edge = False
238                    # After looping through the vertices of the face, we need to take care of
239                    # two special cases : the first or the last vertex is not shared.
240                    if extra_edges and extra_edges[0][0] == -1:
241                        extra_edges[0][0] = useful_vertices[-1]
242                    elif incomplete_new_edge:
243                        new_edge.append(useful_vertices[0])
244                        extra_edges.append(new_edge)
245                    # The extra edges are added to the list of all edges
246                    edges.extend(extra_edges)
247                    inbound_faces[i] = tuple(
248                        sorted(useful_vertices)
249                    )  # And the face itself is replaced by only the useful vertices.
250                    # Note that the vertices here are not ordered in clockwise or counterclockwise order anymore.
251                useful_vertices_set = set(np.where(inbound_vertices > 1)[0])  # We filter the useful vertices.
252
253                # HALF EDGE DATA STRUCTURE
254                # Filter edges with useful vertices only.
255                useful_edges = [tuple(sorted(e)) for e in edges if set(e).issubset(useful_vertices_set)]
256
257                # failing to abide by the following relation results in disconnected topologies
258                if len(useful_edges) != (n_cells - 1) * 3:
259                    success = 2  # Case : we want to restart with new seeds because current solution is not OK.
260                else:
261                    # We construct the half-edges.
262                    half_edges = []
263                    for e in useful_edges:
264                        half_edges.append(e)
265                        # reciprocating edges
266                        half_edges.append((e[1], e[0]))
267
268                    # finding clockwise (or counterclockwise) half edge set for each face,
269                    # as we broke it earlier.
270                    ordered_edges_inbound_faces = []
271                    for face in inbound_faces:
272                        # Find all edges fon this face and we'll loow through them to order them.
273                        edges_face = [(f1, f2) for f1 in face for f2 in face if (f1, f2) in useful_edges]
274
275                        i = 0
276                        start_edge = edges_face[i]
277                        ordered_face = [start_edge]
278                        e = start_edge
279                        visited = [e]
280                        while sorted(edges_face) != sorted(visited):
281                            if e[0] == start_edge[1] and e not in visited:
282                                ordered_face.append(e)
283                                start_edge = e
284                                visited.append(e)
285                            # We must be careful because some edges might be in the wrong order.
286                            if e[1] == start_edge[1] and e not in visited:
287                                ordered_face.append((e[1], e[0]))
288                                start_edge = (e[1], e[0])
289                                visited.append(e)
290                            i += 1
291                            e = edges_face[i % len(edges_face)]
292
293                        # Sanity check : do we have a correct ordering ?
294                        order = 0
295                        for e in ordered_face:
296                            idx0 = e[0]
297                            idx1 = e[1]
298
299                            order += (vertices[idx1][0] - vertices[idx0][0]) * (vertices[idx1][1] + vertices[idx0][1])
300
301                        if order < 0:
302                            ordered_edges_inbound_faces.append(ordered_face)
303                        if order > 0:
304                            ordered_edges_inbound_faces.append([(e[1], e[0]) for e in reversed(ordered_face)])
305                        if order == 0:
306                            print("\nError: no order detected for face " + str(face) + "\n")
307                            exit()
308
309                    # Now we fill the tables with the info we have.
310                    useful_vertices_list = list(useful_vertices_set)
311                    vertTable = np.zeros((len(useful_vertices_list), 2))
312                    for i, idx in enumerate(useful_vertices_list):
313                        pos = vertices[idx]
314                        vertTable[i][0] = pos[0]  # x pos vert
315                        vertTable[i][1] = pos[1]  # y pos vert
316
317                    faceTable = np.zeros((len(inbound_faces), 1), dtype=np.int32)
318                    for i, hedges_face in enumerate(ordered_edges_inbound_faces):
319                        for j, he in enumerate(half_edges):
320                            if he == hedges_face[0]:
321                                faceTable[i] = j  # he_inside
322                    faceTable = _fate_selection(faceTable, nb_fates, rng)
323
324                    nb_half_edges = len(half_edges)
325                    heTable = np.zeros((nb_half_edges, 8), dtype=np.int32)
326                    heTable[:, 4] = 1
327                    heTable[:, 6] = 1
328                    relevant_twins = []
329                    # HE TABLE :
330                    # 0 : previous half-edge.
331                    # 1 : next half-edge.
332                    # 2 : twin half-edge.
333                    # 3 : source vertex id + 2 if edge is inside, 0 if the edge is outside
334                    # 4 : target vertex id + 2 if edge is inside, 0 if the edge is outside
335                    # 5 : source vertex id + 2 if edge is outside, 0 if the edge is inside
336                    # 6 : target vertex id + 2 if edge is outside, 0 if the edge is inside
337                    # 7 : id of the face containing this half-edge.
338                    for i, he in enumerate(half_edges):
339                        belongs_to_any_face = False
340                        for hedges_face in ordered_edges_inbound_faces:
341                            if he in hedges_face:
342                                idx = hedges_face.index(he)
343                                heTable[i][0] = half_edges.index(hedges_face[(idx - 1) % len(hedges_face)])  # he_prev
344                                heTable[i][1] = half_edges.index(hedges_face[(idx + 1) % len(hedges_face)])  # he_next
345                                # indices 0 and 1 are reserved for source or target vertices of "outside" edges.
346                                # So we have to add +2 to other indices.
347                                heTable[i][3] = useful_vertices_list.index(he[0]) + 2  # vert source inner edges
348                                heTable[i][4] = useful_vertices_list.index(he[1]) + 2  # vert target inner edges
349                                heTable[i][7] = ordered_edges_inbound_faces.index(hedges_face)  # face
350                                belongs_to_any_face = True
351                                break
352                        twin_idx = half_edges.index((he[1], he[0]))
353                        heTable[i][2] = twin_idx  # he twin
354                        if not belongs_to_any_face:
355                            relevant_twins.append(twin_idx)
356
357                    # Angles are randomly chosen between 0 and pi/2 (with some margin to avoid extreme cases).
358                    angTable = np.ones(nb_half_edges // 2)
359                    for tidx in relevant_twins:
360                        angTable[tidx // 2] = rng.random() * (np.pi / 2 - 0.018) + 0.017
361                        heTable[tidx][5] = heTable[tidx][3]  # vert source surface edges
362                        heTable[tidx][6] = heTable[tidx][4]  # vert target surface edges
363                        heTable[tidx][3] = 0
364                        heTable[tidx][4] = 1
365
366                    bounded_mesh = cls._create()
367                    bounded_mesh.vertices = jnp.array(vertTable, dtype=jnp.result_type(float))
368                    bounded_mesh.angles = jnp.array(angTable, dtype=jnp.result_type(float))
369                    bounded_mesh.faces = jnp.array(faceTable, dtype=np.int32)
370                    bounded_mesh.edges = jnp.array(heTable, dtype=np.int32)
371                    bounded_mesh.width = width
372                    bounded_mesh.height = height
373
374                    _check_face_orientation(bounded_mesh, "BoundedMesh.from_seeds")
375                    return bounded_mesh
376
377            # If success was 1, we had not enough bounded faces, we add a new seed to see if it helps.
378            # Otherwise we retry with new seeds entirely.
379            seeds = (
380                np.vstack([seeds, (width, height) * rng.random((1, 2))])
381                if success == 1
382                else (width, height) * rng.random((n_cells, 2))
383            )  # type: ignore

444        Warns:

454        )

456        mesh.height = mesh_file["height"]
457        mesh.vertices_params = mesh_file["vertices_params"]
458        mesh.edges_params = mesh_file["edges_params"]
459        mesh.faces_params = mesh_file["faces_params"]
460        _check_face_orientation(mesh, f"BoundedMesh.load_mesh({path!r})")
461        return mesh

def save_mesh_txt( self, directory: str, vertices_filename: str = 'vertTable.txt', angles_filename: str = 'angTable.txt', edges_filename: str = 'heTable.txt', faces_filename: str = 'faceTable.txt', vertices_params_filename: str = 'vertParamsTable.txt', edges_params_filename: str = 'heParamsTable.txt', faces_params_filename: str = 'faceParamsTable.txt', constants_filename: str = 'constants.txt') -> None: 
463    def save_mesh_txt(
464        self,
465        directory: str,
466        vertices_filename: str = "vertTable.txt",
467        angles_filename: str = "angTable.txt",
468        edges_filename: str = "heTable.txt",
469        faces_filename: str = "faceTable.txt",
470        vertices_params_filename: str = "vertParamsTable.txt",
471        edges_params_filename: str = "heParamsTable.txt",
472        faces_params_filename: str = "faceParamsTable.txt",
473        constants_filename: str = "constants.txt",
474    ) -> None:
475        """Save a mesh in separate text files that can be read by numpy.
476
477        Save the vertices, angles, edges and faces tables, the vertex, edge and face parameter tables and the
478        constants (width and height), one text file each.
479
480        Args:
481            directory (str): Path to the directory where to save the files.
482            vertices_filename (str, optional): Filename for the vertices table. Defaults to "vertTable.txt".
483            angles_filename (str, optional): Filename for the angles table. Defaults to "angTable.txt".
484            edges_filename (str, optional): Filename for the half-edges table. Defaults to "heTable.txt".
485            faces_filename (str, optional): Filename for the faces table. Defaults to "faceTable.txt".
486            vertices_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the vertices parameters table.
487                    Defaults to "vertParamsTable.txt".
488            edges_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the half-edges parameters table.
489                    Defaults to "heParamsTable.txt".
490            faces_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the faces parameters table.
491                    Defaults to "faceParamsTable.txt".
492            constants_filename (str, optional): Filename for width/height.
493                    Defaults to "constants.txt".
494        """
495        dirpath = Path(directory)
496        dirpath.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
497        np.savetxt(dirpath / vertices_filename, self.vertices)
498        np.savetxt(dirpath / angles_filename, self.angles)
499        np.savetxt(dirpath / edges_filename, self.edges)
500        np.savetxt(dirpath / faces_filename, self.faces)
501        np.savetxt(dirpath / vertices_params_filename, self.vertices_params)
502        np.savetxt(dirpath / edges_params_filename, self.edges_params)
503        np.savetxt(dirpath / faces_params_filename, self.faces_params)
504        with (dirpath / constants_filename).open("w") as f:
505            f.write(f"{self.width} {self.height}")

Defaults to "vertParamsTable.txt". edges_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the half-edges parameters table. Defaults to "heParamsTable.txt". faces_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the faces parameters table. Defaults to "faceParamsTable.txt". constants_filename (str, optional): Filename for width/height. Defaults to "constants.txt".

@classmethod
def load_mesh_txt( cls, directory: str, vertices_filename: str = 'vertTable.txt', angles_filename: str = 'angTable.txt', edges_filename: str = 'heTable.txt', faces_filename: str = 'faceTable.txt', vertices_params_filename: str = 'vertParamsTable.txt', edges_params_filename: str = 'heParamsTable.txt', faces_params_filename: str = 'faceParamsTable.txt', constants_filename: str = 'constants.txt') -> Self: 
507    @classmethod
508    def load_mesh_txt(
509        cls,
510        directory: str,
511        vertices_filename: str = "vertTable.txt",
512        angles_filename: str = "angTable.txt",
513        edges_filename: str = "heTable.txt",
514        faces_filename: str = "faceTable.txt",
515        vertices_params_filename: str = "vertParamsTable.txt",
516        edges_params_filename: str = "heParamsTable.txt",
517        faces_params_filename: str = "faceParamsTable.txt",
518        constants_filename: str = "constants.txt",
519    ) -> Self:
520        """Load a mesh from text files.
521
522        Load the vertices, angles, edges and faces tables, the vertex, edge and face parameter tables and the
523        constants (width and height), one text file each.
524
525        Args:
526            directory (str): Directory where the text files are stored.
527            vertices_filename (str, optional): Filename for the vertices table. Defaults to "vertTable.txt".
528            angles_filename (str, optional): Filename for the angles table. Defaults to "angTable.txt".
529            edges_filename (str, optional): Filename for the half-edges table. Defaults to "heTable.txt".
530            faces_filename (str, optional): Filename for the faces table. Defaults to "faceTable.txt".
531            vertices_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the vertices parameters table.
532                    Defaults to "vertParamsTable.txt".
533            edges_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the half-edges parameters table.
534                    Defaults to "heParamsTable.txt".
535            faces_params_filename (str, optional): Filename for the faces parameters table.
536                    Defaults to "faceParamsTable.txt".
537            constants_filename (str, optional): Filename for width/height/MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE.
538                    Defaults to "constants.txt".
539
540        Returns:
541            Self: The loaded mesh.
542
543        Raises:
544            ValueError: if the faces of the mesh are clockwise (see `BoundedMesh`).
545
546        Warns:
547            UserWarning: if some faces have a turned-over chord polygon (a crescent, or a fold).
548        """
549        dirpath = Path(directory)
550        dirpath.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
551
552        mesh = cls._create()
553        # Index tables are WRITTEN by `np.savetxt` in float notation ('0.00...e+00'), so reading
554        # them with `dtype=np.int64` makes numpy parse an integer via a float -- a
555        # DeprecationWarning that this project's `filterwarnings = ["error"]` turns into a hard
556        # error, which is why this loader had no test. Read as float and cast, which also keeps
557        # every file written by earlier versions readable.
558        mesh.vertices = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / vertices_filename, dtype=np.float64))
559        mesh.angles = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / angles_filename, dtype=np.float64))
560        mesh.edges = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / edges_filename, dtype=np.float64).astype(np.int64))
561        mesh.faces = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / faces_filename, dtype=np.float64).astype(np.int64))
562        # `edges_params` and `faces_params` are PHYSICAL PARAMETERS (tensions, target areas,
563        # shape factors), never indices, so they must be read as float: reading them with
564        # `dtype=np.int64` silently truncates -- a tension field of mean 1 and spread 0.1
565        # round-trips to all-ones, destroying the whole signal. See tests/test_mesh_txt_roundtrip.py.
566        mesh.vertices_params = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / vertices_params_filename, dtype=np.float64))
567        mesh.edges_params = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / edges_params_filename, dtype=np.float64))
568        mesh.faces_params = jnp.array(np.loadtxt(dirpath / faces_params_filename, dtype=np.float64))
569        with (dirpath / constants_filename).open("r") as f:
570            numbers = f.readline().split()
571            mesh.width = float(numbers[0])
572            mesh.height = float(numbers[1])
573        _check_face_orientation(mesh, f"BoundedMesh.load_mesh_txt({str(directory)!r})")
574        return mesh

class BilevelOptimizationMethod(enum.Enum): 
 7class BilevelOptimizationMethod(Enum):
 8    """Which optimization method to use in the bi-level optimization."""
 9
10    AUTOMATIC_DIFFERENTIATION = "ad"
11    """Unrolls the inner optimization steps and differentiates through them in reverse mode
12    (`jax.grad`) ; memory and cost scale with the number of unrolled inner iterations, and
13    line-search inner solvers are not supported."""
14    EQUILIBRIUM_PROPAGATION = "ep"
15    """Estimates the gradient from perturbed free vs nudged equilibria ; no backdrop required.
16    Most efficient but depends on the perturbation size β."""
17    IMPLICIT_DIFFERENTIATION = "id"
18    """Differentiates the optimality condition ∇ₓE=0 via Implicit Function Theorem ; JVP variant ;
19    requires Hessian solve and sensitive to ill-conditioning."""
20    ADJOINT_STATE = "as"
21    """Differentiates the optimality condition ∇ₓE=0 via Implicit Function Theorem ; VJP variant ;
22    requires Hessian solve or sensitive to ill-conditioning."""

Which optimization method to use in the bi-level optimization.

AUTOMATIC_DIFFERENTIATION = <BilevelOptimizationMethod.AUTOMATIC_DIFFERENTIATION: 'ad'>

EQUILIBRIUM_PROPAGATION = <BilevelOptimizationMethod.EQUILIBRIUM_PROPAGATION: 'ep'>

IMPLICIT_DIFFERENTIATION = <BilevelOptimizationMethod.IMPLICIT_DIFFERENTIATION: 'id'>

ADJOINT_STATE = <BilevelOptimizationMethod.ADJOINT_STATE: 'as'>
