def cg_linesearch( restart_every: int = 10, max_linesearch_steps: int = 20, linesearch_initial_guess: str = 'keep') -> optax._src.base.GradientTransformationExtraArgs: 
 93def cg_linesearch(
 94    restart_every: int = 10,
 95    max_linesearch_steps: int = 20,
 96    linesearch_initial_guess: str = "keep",
 97) -> optax.GradientTransformationExtraArgs:
 98    """Polak-Ribière nonlinear conjugate gradient with restarts + zoom line search.
 99
100    Args:
101        restart_every: force a steepest-descent restart every this many steps.
102            Smaller = more robust on strongly non-quadratic objectives, larger =
103            longer conjugate runs.
104        max_linesearch_steps: maximum zoom line-search iterations per step.
105        linesearch_initial_guess: step length from which each line search starts, passed to
106            ``optax.scale_by_zoom_linesearch`` as ``initial_guess_strategy``. ``"keep"`` (default)
107            starts from the last accepted step. Combined with a per-vertex step cap, one very short
108            accepted step can then persist and a single long call stalls; restarting the call
109            resets it. ``"one"`` starts every line search from a unit step and does not stall, at
110            the price of more energy evaluations per step.
111
112    Returns:
113        An ``optax`` solver. Its ``update`` requires ``value``, ``grad`` and
114        ``value_fn`` keyword arguments (see module docstring).
115    """
116    linesearch = optax.scale_by_zoom_linesearch(
117        max_linesearch_steps=max_linesearch_steps, initial_guess_strategy=linesearch_initial_guess
118    )
119
120    def init_fn(params: optax.Params) -> NonlinearCGState:
121        return NonlinearCGState(
122            count=jnp.zeros([], jnp.int32),
123            grad_prev=otu.tree_zeros_like(params),
124            dir_prev=otu.tree_zeros_like(params),
125            ls_state=linesearch.init(params),
126        )
127
128    def update_fn(
129        updates: optax.Updates,  # = grad, by optax convention  # noqa: ARG001
130        state: NonlinearCGState,
131        params: optax.Params | None = None,
132        *,
133        value: jax.Array | None = None,
134        grad: optax.Updates | None = None,
135        value_fn=None,  # noqa: ANN001
136        **extra_args: Any,  # noqa: ANN401, ARG001
137    ) -> tuple[optax.Updates, NonlinearCGState]:
138        if params is None or value is None or grad is None or value_fn is None:
139            msg = (
140                "cg_linesearch.update requires `params`, `value`, `grad` and "
141                "`value_fn` (it performs a line search). Pass them from the loop."
142            )
143            raise ValueError(msg)
144
145        g = grad
146        g_prev = state.grad_prev
147        d_prev = state.dir_prev
148
149        # On the very first step grad_prev is zero → force a steepest-descent start.
150        is_first = state.count == 0
151
152        # (1) Polak-Ribière coefficient.
153        gg_prev = otu.tree_vdot(g_prev, g_prev) + 1e-12  # ‖g_{k-1}‖²
154        y = otu.tree_sub(g, g_prev)  # g_k - g_{k-1}
155        beta_pr = otu.tree_vdot(g, y) / gg_prev
156
157        # (2) Restart: periodic, or PR+ (β ≤ 0), or first step.
158        do_restart = is_first | (state.count % restart_every == 0) | (beta_pr <= 0.0)
159        beta = jnp.where(do_restart, 0.0, beta_pr)
160
161        # (3) Conjugate direction d = -g + β · d_prev.
162        d = otu.tree_add_scalar_mul(otu.tree_scalar_mul(-1.0, g), beta, d_prev)
163
164        # (4) Descent-direction guard: ensure ⟨d, g⟩ < 0, else use -g.
165        is_descent = otu.tree_vdot(d, g) < 0.0
166        d = jax.lax.cond(is_descent, lambda: d, lambda: otu.tree_scalar_mul(-1.0, g))
167
168        # (5) Zoom line search along d → updates = step · d.
169        step_updates, ls_state = linesearch.update(
170            updates=d,
171            state=state.ls_state,
172            params=params,
173            value=value,
174            grad=g,
175            value_fn=value_fn,
176        )
177
178        new_state = NonlinearCGState(
179            count=state.count + 1,
180            grad_prev=g,
181            dir_prev=d,
182            ls_state=ls_state,
183        )
184        return step_updates, _keep_integer_dtypes(new_state, state)
185
186    return optax.GradientTransformationExtraArgs(init_fn, update_fn)  # ty:ignore[invalid-argument-type]

Polak-Ribière nonlinear conjugate gradient with restarts + zoom line search.

Args: restart_every: force a steepest-descent restart every this many steps. Smaller = more robust on strongly non-quadratic objectives, larger = longer conjugate runs. max_linesearch_steps: maximum zoom line-search iterations per step. linesearch_initial_guess: step length from which each line search starts, passed to optax.scale_by_zoom_linesearch as initial_guess_strategy. "keep" (default) starts from the last accepted step. Combined with a per-vertex step cap, one very short accepted step can then persist and a single long call stalls; restarting the call resets it. "one" starts every line search from a unit step and does not stall, at the price of more energy evaluations per step.

Returns: An optax solver. Its update requires value, grad and value_fn keyword arguments (see module docstring).

def gd_linesearch( max_linesearch_steps: int = 20, linesearch_initial_guess: str = 'keep') -> optax._src.base.GradientTransformationExtraArgs: 
195def gd_linesearch(
196    max_linesearch_steps: int = 20,
197    linesearch_initial_guess: str = "keep",
198) -> optax.GradientTransformationExtraArgs:
199    """Steepest descent with a zoom (Wolfe) line search for the step size.
200
201    Plain gradient descent picks the search direction ``d = -g`` but leaves the
202    step size to a fixed learning rate. This solver keeps ``d = -g`` (no conjugate
203    term, unlike :func:`cg_linesearch`) but chooses the step by the same
204    ``optax.scale_by_zoom_linesearch`` used by CG / lbfgs, so each step satisfies
205    the strong Wolfe conditions instead of relying on a hand-tuned learning rate.
206
207    Like every line-search solver, its ``update`` requires ``value``, ``grad`` and
208    ``value_fn`` (it re-evaluates the loss along ``d``); the enclosing loop must
209    forward them, exactly as for :func:`cg_linesearch`.
210
211    Note (AD incompatibility): the zoom line search runs an inner
212    ``lax.while_loop`` with dynamic bounds, which reverse-mode AD cannot
213    differentiate through. So — like ``cg_linesearch`` — this solver is
214    incompatible with the AUTOMATIC_DIFFERENTIATION bilevel method; the factory
215    name contains ``"linesearch"`` so the guard in ``bilevelopt.py`` rejects the
216    combination automatically.
217
218    ``linesearch_initial_guess`` has the meaning it has in :func:`cg_linesearch`.
219    """
220    linesearch = optax.scale_by_zoom_linesearch(
221        max_linesearch_steps=max_linesearch_steps, initial_guess_strategy=linesearch_initial_guess
222    )
223
224    def init_fn(params: optax.Params) -> GDLineSearchState:
225        return GDLineSearchState(ls_state=linesearch.init(params))
226
227    def update_fn(
228        updates: optax.Updates,  # = grad, by optax convention  # noqa: ARG001
229        state: GDLineSearchState,
230        params: optax.Params | None = None,
231        *,
232        value: jax.Array | None = None,
233        grad: optax.Updates | None = None,
234        value_fn=None,  # noqa: ANN001
235        **extra_args: Any,  # noqa: ANN401, ARG001
236    ) -> tuple[optax.Updates, GDLineSearchState]:
237        if params is None or value is None or grad is None or value_fn is None:
238            msg = (
239                "gd_linesearch.update requires `params`, `value`, `grad` and "
240                "`value_fn` (it performs a line search). Pass them from the loop."
241            )
242            raise ValueError(msg)
243
244        # Steepest-descent direction d = -g (always a valid descent direction).
245        d = otu.tree_scalar_mul(-1.0, grad)
246
247        # Zoom line search along d → updates = step · d.
248        step_updates, ls_state = linesearch.update(
249            updates=d,
250            state=state.ls_state,
251            params=params,
252            value=value,
253            grad=grad,
254            value_fn=value_fn,
255        )
256        return step_updates, _keep_integer_dtypes(GDLineSearchState(ls_state=ls_state), state)
257
258    return optax.GradientTransformationExtraArgs(init_fn, update_fn)  # ty:ignore[invalid-argument-type]

Steepest descent with a zoom (Wolfe) line search for the step size.

Plain gradient descent picks the search direction d = -g but leaves the step size to a fixed learning rate. This solver keeps d = -g (no conjugate term, unlike cg_linesearch()) but chooses the step by the same optax.scale_by_zoom_linesearch used by CG / lbfgs, so each step satisfies the strong Wolfe conditions instead of relying on a hand-tuned learning rate.

Like every line-search solver, its update requires value, grad and value_fn (it re-evaluates the loss along d); the enclosing loop must forward them, exactly as for cg_linesearch().

Note (AD incompatibility): the zoom line search runs an inner lax.while_loop with dynamic bounds, which reverse-mode AD cannot differentiate through. So — like cg_linesearch — this solver is incompatible with the AUTOMATIC_DIFFERENTIATION bilevel method; the factory name contains "linesearch" so the guard in bilevelopt.py rejects the combination automatically.

linesearch_initial_guess has the meaning it has in cg_linesearch().

def cost_v2v( vertTable: jax.Array, heTable: jax.Array, faceTable: jax.Array, width: float, height: float, vertTable_target: jax.Array, heTable_target: jax.Array, faceTable_target: jax.Array, selected_verts: jax.Array | None = None, selected_hes: jax.Array | None = None, selected_faces: jax.Array | None = None, _image_target: jax.Array | None = None) -> jax.Array: 
215@partial(jit, static_argnums=(3, 4))
216def cost_v2v(
217    vertTable: Array,
218    heTable: Array,
219    faceTable: Array,
220    width: float,
221    height: float,
222    vertTable_target: Array,
223    heTable_target: Array,
224    faceTable_target: Array,
225    selected_verts: Array | None = None,
226    selected_hes: Array | None = None,
227    selected_faces: Array | None = None,
228    _image_target: Array | None = None,
229) -> Array:
230    """Cost vertex to vertex. Compare the positions of given vertices to target vertices (`PbcMesh`)."""
231    if selected_verts is None:
232        selected_verts = jnp.arange(vertTable.shape[0])
233    if selected_hes is None:
234        selected_hes = jnp.arange(heTable.shape[0])
235    if selected_faces is None:
236        selected_faces = jnp.arange(faceTable.shape[0])
237
238    def squared_distance(v: Array, vertTable: Array, vertTable_target: Array, width: float, height: float) -> Array:
239        """Nearest-periodic-image squared distance for vertex ``v`` -- the C_v2v summand.
240
241        Delegates to :func:`vertax.geo.min_image_sq_dist`, which documents why this must not be
242        respelled as a min over nine scalars, nor as ``(min sqrt(u))**2``. The
243        same helper is used by the periodic T1 swap-repair criterion so the two cannot drift.
244        """
245        return min_image_sq_dist(vertTable[v], vertTable_target[v], width, height)
246
247    def mapped_fn(v: Array) -> Array:
248        return squared_distance(v, vertTable, vertTable_target, width, height)
249
250    distances = vmap(mapped_fn)(selected_verts)
251
252    return (1.0 / (2 * len(distances))) * jnp.sum(distances)

@jit
def cost_mesh2image( vertTable: jax.Array, heTable: jax.Array, _faceTable: jax.Array, width: float, height: float, _vertTable_target: jax.Array, _heTable_target: jax.Array, _faceTable_target: jax.Array, _selected_verts: jax.Array, selected_hes: jax.Array, _selected_faces: jax.Array, image_target: jax.Array, sigma_psf: jax.Array) -> jax.Array: 
255@jit
256def cost_mesh2image(
257    vertTable: Array,
258    heTable: Array,
259    _faceTable: Array,
260    width: float,
261    height: float,
262    _vertTable_target: Array,
263    _heTable_target: Array,
264    _faceTable_target: Array,
265    _selected_verts: Array,
266    selected_hes: Array,
267    _selected_faces: Array,
268    image_target: Array,
269    sigma_psf: Array,
270) -> Array:
271    """Cost mesh to image. Compare the given vertices positions to a target image (`PbcMesh`).
272
273    `sigma_psf` is REQUIRED and is a parameter of the cost, not a module setting. It is traced,
274    so `jax.grad(..., argnums=12)` differentiates the cost with respect to the PSF width and a
275    trainable PSF is possible without touching this function.
276
277    This is the direct entry point, and it is the one to use when `sigma_psf` is itself being
278    optimized. For the fixed-width 12-argument outer-cost protocol used by the optimizers, use
279    :func:`make_cost_mesh2image`, which closes over the width instead.
280
281    Every result recorded before the width became an argument was produced at
282    :data:`LEGACY_PSF_SIGMA`; pass that value to reproduce one.
283    """
284    wh = jnp.asarray([width, height])
285    starting = (vertTable[heTable[selected_hes, 3], :2]) * 2 / wh  # (M, 2)
286    # ending = (vertTable[heTable[selected_hes, 4], :2]) * 2 / L_box  # (M, 2)
287    ending = (
288        (
289            vertTable[heTable[selected_hes, 4], :2]
290            + jnp.stack(
291                [
292                    heTable[selected_hes, 6],
293                    heTable[selected_hes, 7],
294                ],
295                axis=-1,
296            )
297            * wh
298        )
299        * 2
300        / wh
301    )
302
303    he_edges = stack((starting, ending), axis=1)  # (N, 2, 2)
304    x = he_edges.transpose(1, 2, 0) - 1  # (2, 2, N)
305
306    # Blur
307    image = _gaussian_blur_line_segments(x, sigma_psf).real
308
309    # Normalization
310    image = image / image.sum()
311    image_target = image_target / image_target.sum()
312
313    l2_norm = jnp.linalg.norm(jnp.sqrt(jnp.sum(((image - image_target) ** 2) * (1 - image_target), axis=-1)).flatten())
314
315    return l2_norm

Cost mesh to image. Compare the given vertices positions to a target image (PbcMesh).

sigma_psf is REQUIRED and is a parameter of the cost, not a module setting. It is traced, so jax.grad(..., argnums=12) differentiates the cost with respect to the PSF width and a trainable PSF is possible without touching this function.

This is the direct entry point, and it is the one to use when sigma_psf is itself being optimized. For the fixed-width 12-argument outer-cost protocol used by the optimizers, use make_cost_mesh2image(), which closes over the width instead.

def make_cost_mesh2image(sigma_psf: float): 
319def make_cost_mesh2image(sigma_psf: float):
320    """Bind a PSF width to `cost_mesh2image`, giving the 12-argument outer-cost protocol form.
321
322    Parallel to :func:`make_cost_dmic`. The closure is a convenience for the case where the PSF
323    width is FIXED, which is what the bilevel optimizers' 12-argument protocol assumes. It is
324    deliberately not the traceable entry point for a TRAINABLE width -- closing over `sigma_psf`
325    makes it a constant of the returned function. To differentiate with respect to the PSF width,
326    call :func:`cost_mesh2image` directly and pass the width as its thirteenth argument.
327
328    Args:
329        sigma_psf: PSF standard deviation, in the units of the box the Fourier grid spans.
330
331    Returns:
332        A 12-argument callable matching the outer-cost protocol.
333    """
334
335    @jit
336    def cost(
337        vertTable: Array,
338        heTable: Array,
339        faceTable: Array,
340        width: float,
341        height: float,
342        vertTable_target: Array,
343        heTable_target: Array,
344        faceTable_target: Array,
345        selected_verts: Array,
346        selected_hes: Array,
347        selected_faces: Array,
348        image_target: Array,
349    ) -> Array:
350        return cost_mesh2image(
351            vertTable, heTable, faceTable, width, height,
352            vertTable_target, heTable_target, faceTable_target,
353            selected_verts, selected_hes, selected_faces, image_target, sigma_psf,
354        )
355
356    return cost

It is deliberately not the traceable entry point for a TRAINABLE width -- closing over sigma_psf makes it a constant of the returned function. def cost_areas( vertTable: jax.Array, heTable: jax.Array, faceTable: jax.Array, width: float, height: float, vertTable_target: jax.Array, heTable_target: jax.Array, faceTable_target: jax.Array, _selected_verts: jax.Array | None = None, _selected_hes: jax.Array | None = None, selected_faces: jax.Array | None = None, _image_target: jax.Array | None = None) -> jax.Array: 
359@partial(jit, static_argnums=(3, 4))
360def cost_areas(
361    vertTable: Array,
362    heTable: Array,
363    faceTable: Array,
364    width: float,
365    height: float,
366    vertTable_target: Array,
367    heTable_target: Array,
368    faceTable_target: Array,
369    _selected_verts: Array | None = None,
370    _selected_hes: Array | None = None,
371    selected_faces: Array | None = None,
372    _image_target: Array | None = None,
373) -> Array:
374    """Cost areas : compare the areas of the given mesh versus the areas of the target mesh (`PbcMesh`).
375
376    Mean over the selected faces (all faces if `selected_faces` is None) of the squared difference
377    between the area of a face and the area of the same face in the target mesh, which must have
378    the same faces.
379    """
380    if selected_faces is None:
381        selected_faces = jnp.arange(faceTable.shape[0])
382
383    def mapped_fn(f: Array) -> Array:
384        return (
385            get_area(f, vertTable, heTable, faceTable, width, height, MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE)
386            - get_area(f, vertTable_target, heTable_target, faceTable_target, width, height, MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE)
387        ) ** 2
388
389    difference = vmap(mapped_fn)(selected_faces)
390    return (1.0 / len(difference)) * jnp.sum(difference)

def topological_distance( vertTable: jax.Array, heTable: jax.Array, faceTable: jax.Array, width: float, height: float, vertTable_target: jax.Array, heTable_target: jax.Array, faceTable_target: jax.Array, selected_verts: jax.Array | None = None, selected_hes: jax.Array | None = None, selected_faces: jax.Array | None = None, _image_target: jax.Array | None = None) -> int: 
482def topological_distance(
483    vertTable: Array,
484    heTable: Array,
485    faceTable: Array,
486    width: float,
487    height: float,
488    vertTable_target: Array,
489    heTable_target: Array,
490    faceTable_target: Array,
491    selected_verts: Array | None = None,
492    selected_hes: Array | None = None,
493    selected_faces: Array | None = None,
494    _image_target: Array | None = None,
495) -> int:
496    r"""Discrete topological distance ``d_topo`` between two meshes: differing cell contacts.
497
498    Builds the dual (cell) adjacency matrix of each mesh, ``A[a, b] = 1`` iff cells ``a`` and ``b``
499    share a junction, puts the two cell labellings into correspondence with the Hungarian
500    algorithm (cell labels are arbitrary), and counts the cell--cell contacts on which the two
501    meshes then disagree, each unordered pair once:
502
503    .. math::
504        d_{topo} = \sum_{a<b} \bigl| A^{(1)}_{ab} - A^{(2)}_{\sigma(a)\sigma(b)} \bigr| .
505
506    An elementary T1 transition destroys exactly one contact and creates exactly one other, so it
507    changes **two** upper-triangle entries. Therefore ``d_topo`` is always **even**, and
508    ``d_topo / 2`` is the number of T1 events separating the two topologies. (Verified against the
509    Figure-3 synthetic dataset, whose levels 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 this function reproduces exactly.)
510
511    **This is a measurement, not an objective.** It returns a Python ``int`` and provides no
512    gradient, so it cannot be assigned to ``loss_function_outer``. Use it to quantify topological
513    distance and to time phase switches in a staged schedule. Separately, any purely topological or
514    edge-level cost is a strict information loss for edge-tension inference relative to a
515    vertex-level cost such as :func:`cost_v2v` -- the cell-adjacency Laplacian has a large null
516    space -- so topology should not be used to infer tensions in the first place.
517    """
518
519    def build_dual_adj_np(heTable: Array, n_faces: int) -> NDArray:
520        face = heTable[:, 5]
521        twin = heTable[:, 2]
522
523        face_twin = face[twin]
524        mask = (face != face_twin).astype(float)
525
526        A = np.zeros((n_faces, n_faces))
527
528        A[face, face_twin] += mask
529        A[face_twin, face] += mask
530
531        A = np.clip(A, 0.0, 1.0)
532        return A
533
534    n1 = len(faceTable)
535    n2 = len(faceTable_target)
536
537    if n1 != n2:
538        msg = "This version requires same number of faces"
539        raise ValueError(msg)
540
541    n = n1
542
543    A1 = build_dual_adj_np(heTable, n)
544    A2 = build_dual_adj_np(heTable_target, n)
545
546    # --- Step 1: node matching via Hungarian ---
547    # cost between nodes = L1 difference of adjacency rows
548    C = np.sum(np.abs(A1[:, None, :] - A2[None, :, :]), axis=-1)
549
550    row_ind, col_ind = linear_sum_assignment(C)
551
552    # permutation: face i in A1 ↔ face col_ind[i] in A2
553    P = np.zeros((n, n))
554    P[row_ind, col_ind] = 1.0
555
556    # --- Step 2: permute A2 ---
557    A2_perm = P @ A2 @ P.T
558
559    # --- Step 3: count edge mismatches ---
560    diff = np.abs(A1 - A2_perm)
561
562    # count each edge once
563    diff_upper = np.triu(diff, k=1)
564
565    loss = int(np.sum(diff_upper))
566
567    return loss

An elementary T1 transition destroys exactly one contact and creates exactly one other, so it changes two upper-triangle entries. Therefore d_topo is always even, and d_topo / 2 is the number of T1 events separating the two topologies. (Verified against the Figure-3 synthetic dataset, whose levels 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 this function reproduces exactly.)

875def cost_dmic(

877    heTable: Array,

882    _heTable_target: Array | None = None,
883    _faceTable_target: Array | None = None,
884    _selected_verts: Array | None = None,

895    """Differentiable-microscopy outer cost: `0.5 * ||M * (Ihat(theta) - I_obs)||^2`.
896
897    **Squared**, so the gradient vanishes at a perfect fit and the cost is dimensionally consistent
898    with `cost_v2v`. Both images carry unit total intensity, so the cost cannot be reduced by
899    changing overall brightness -- which a mesh can do by changing total edge length.
900
901    Prefer `make_cost_dmic(sigma_psf, ...)` when using this as an outer loss: the bilevel optimizer
902    calls outer costs with a fixed 12-argument signature and cannot pass keyword arguments, so the
903    default `sigma_psf` here would silently apply.
904

906        sigma_psf: PSF standard deviation in **physical** units. The default is a placeholder; it
907            should be set from the imaging system, and swept rather than assumed.
908        mask: optional comparison mask. `None` compares the whole frame, correct for a periodic
909            image; use `erode_mask_for_psf` for a bounded or cropped one.
910        pixel_footprint: average each pixel over its footprint instead of point-sampling it; see
911            `render_interface_image`.
912    """
913    return make_cost_dmic(sigma_psf, mask, intensity_weighted=intensity_weighted,
914                          weight_floor=weight_floor, pixel_footprint=pixel_footprint)(
915        vertTable, heTable, faceTable, width, height,
916        _vertTable_target, _heTable_target, _faceTable_target,
917        _selected_verts, selected_hes, _selected_faces, image_target,
918    )

Differentiable-microscopy outer cost: 0.5 * ||M * (Ihat(theta) - I_obs)||^2.

Squared, so the gradient vanishes at a perfect fit and the cost is dimensionally consistent with cost_v2v. Both images carry unit total intensity, so the cost cannot be reduced by changing overall brightness -- which a mesh can do by changing total edge length.

Prefer make_cost_dmic(sigma_psf, ...) when using this as an outer loss: the bilevel optimizer calls outer costs with a fixed 12-argument signature and cannot pass keyword arguments, so the default sigma_psf here would silently apply.

Args: sigma_psf: PSF standard deviation in physical units. The default is a placeholder; it should be set from the imaging system, and swept rather than assumed. mask: optional comparison mask. None compares the whole frame, correct for a periodic image; use erode_mask_for_psf for a bounded or cropped one. pixel_footprint: average each pixel over its footprint instead of point-sampling it; see render_interface_image.

@jit
def cost_ratio( vertTable: jax.Array, _angTable: jax.Array | None = None, _heTable: jax.Array | None = None, _faceTable: jax.Array | None = None, _vertTable_target: jax.Array | None = None, _angTable_target: jax.Array | None = None, _heTable_target: jax.Array | None = None, _faceTable_target: jax.Array | None = None, _selected_verts: jax.Array | None = None, _selected_hes: jax.Array | None = None, _selected_faces: jax.Array | None = None, _image_target: jax.Array | None = None) -> jax.Array: 
393@jit
394def cost_ratio(
395    vertTable: Array,
396    _angTable: Array | None = None,
397    _heTable: Array | None = None,
398    _faceTable: Array | None = None,
399    _vertTable_target: Array | None = None,
400    _angTable_target: Array | None = None,
401    _heTable_target: Array | None = None,
402    _faceTable_target: Array | None = None,
403    _selected_verts: Array | None = None,
404    _selected_hes: Array | None = None,
405    _selected_faces: Array | None = None,
406    _image_target: Array | None = None,
407) -> Array:
408    """Cost that nudges a `BoundedMesh` to elongate along one axis while narrowing along the orthogonal axis."""
409    # Compute pairwise squared distances by broadcasting
410    # diff shape: (n, n, d)
411    diff = vertTable[:, None, :] - vertTable[None, :, :]
412    sq_dists = jnp.sum(diff**2, axis=-1)  # (n, n)
413    distances = jnp.sqrt(sq_dists + 1e-12)  # small eps for numerical stability
414
415    # For each row, get index of farthest point
416    max_distances = jnp.max(distances, axis=1)
417    max_idx_1 = jnp.argmax(max_distances)  # index of row with largest max distance
418    long_axis = max_distances[max_idx_1]  # longest distance (already excludes diagonal)
419    max_idx_2 = jnp.argmax(distances[max_idx_1])  # the farthest point from max_idx_1
420
421    max_point_1 = vertTable[max_idx_1]
422    max_point_2 = vertTable[max_idx_2]
423    long_axis_vector = max_point_2 - max_point_1
424    long_axis_vector = long_axis_vector / (jnp.linalg.norm(long_axis_vector) + 1e-12)
425
426    # Short axis (perpendicular)
427    short_axis_vector = jnp.array([long_axis_vector[1], -long_axis_vector[0]])
428
429    # Project points onto short axis: signed distances
430    # If vertTable is (n,2) this works. If higher dim, modify accordingly.
431    signed_distances_to_long_axis = jnp.dot(vertTable - max_point_1, short_axis_vector)
432
433    short_axis = jnp.max(signed_distances_to_long_axis) - jnp.min(signed_distances_to_long_axis)
434
435    # Numerically stabilize division
436    ratio = long_axis / (short_axis + 1e-12)
437    return (ratio - TARGET_RATIO) ** 2

Cost that nudges a BoundedMesh to elongate along one axis while narrowing along the orthogonal axis.

@jit
def cost_checkerboard( vertTable: jax.Array, _angTable: jax.Array, heTable: jax.Array, faceTable: jax.Array, _vertTable_target: jax.Array | None = None, _angTable_target: jax.Array | None = None, _heTable_target: jax.Array | None = None, _faceTable_target: jax.Array | None = None, _selected_verts: jax.Array | None = None, _selected_hes: jax.Array | None = None, _selected_faces: jax.Array | None = None, _image_target: jax.Array | None = None) -> jax.Array: 
440@jit
441def cost_checkerboard(
442    vertTable: Array,
443    _angTable: Array,
444    heTable: Array,
445    faceTable: Array,
446    _vertTable_target: Array | None = None,
447    _angTable_target: Array | None = None,
448    _heTable_target: Array | None = None,
449    _faceTable_target: Array | None = None,
450    _selected_verts: Array | None = None,
451    _selected_hes: Array | None = None,
452    _selected_faces: Array | None = None,
453    _image_target: Array | None = None,
454) -> Array:
455    """Cost that nudges a `BoundedMesh` with different fated cells to avoid having neighboring cells with same fate.
456
457    This leads to a checkerboard pattern when there is 2 fates.
458    """
459
460    def body_fun(i: int, current_len: Array) -> Array:
461        idx = 2 * i
462        he_twin = heTable[idx, 2]
463        he_face = heTable[idx, 7]
464        he_fate = faceTable[he_face, 1]
465        he_face_twin = heTable[he_twin, 7]
466        he_fate_twin = faceTable[he_face_twin, 1]
467        v_source = heTable[idx, 3] - 2
468        v_target = heTable[idx, 4] - 2
469        pos_source = vertTable[v_source]
470        pos_target = vertTable[v_target]
471        return current_len + jnp.where(
472            jnp.logical_and(he_fate == he_fate_twin, heTable[idx, 3] > 0), jnp.sum((pos_target - pos_source) ** 2), 0.0
473        )
474
475    n_edges = heTable.shape[0] // 2
476    return fori_loop(0, n_edges, body_fun, 0.0)

Cost that nudges a BoundedMesh with different fated cells to avoid having neighboring cells with same fate.

This leads to a checkerboard pattern when there is 2 fates.

def energy_shape_factor_homo( vertTable: jax.Array, heTable: jax.Array, faceTable: jax.Array, width: float, height: float, face_params: jax.Array) -> jax.Array: 
57def energy_shape_factor_homo(
58    vertTable: Array,

def make_energy_shape_factor(lambda_area: float | jax.Array = 1.0) -> Callable: 
 94def make_energy_shape_factor(lambda_area: float | Array = 1.0) -> Callable:
 95    r"""Factory for the periodic E1 energy with an **explicit** area stiffness.
 96
 97    Returns a callable with the signature of :func:`energy_shape_factor_hetero`, implementing
 98
 99    .. math::
100        E_1 = \sum_\alpha \lambda_A\,(A_\alpha - 1)^2 + (P_\alpha - p^0_\alpha)^2 ,
101
102    with ``face_params`` holding the per-cell preferred perimeter :math:`p^0_\alpha`. At
103    ``lambda_area = 1`` it is :func:`energy_shape_factor_hetero` exactly.
104
105    ``lambda_area`` is closed over, not stored at module level, and it is never converted to a
106    Python float, so it may be a traced array. That is what makes it trainable: an energy that
107    reads ``lambda_area = exp(kappa)`` from an outer-parameter slot can call this factory inside
108    itself, and ``jax.grad`` with respect to ``kappa`` flows through the area term. The
109    exponential keeps the stiffness positive without a constraint.
110    """
111
112    def energy_shape_factor(
113        vertTable: Array,
114        heTable: Array,
115        faceTable: Array,
116        width: float,
117        height: float,
118        selected_faces: Array,
119        face_params: Array,
120    ) -> Array:
121        """E1 energy with per-cell preferred perimeters and area stiffness `lambda_area`."""
122
123        def mapped_fn(face: Array, param: Array) -> Array:
124            area = get_area(face, vertTable, heTable, faceTable, width, height, MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE)
125            perimeter = get_perimeter(face, vertTable, heTable, faceTable, width, height, MAX_EDGES_IN_ANY_FACE)
126            return (lambda_area * (area - 1) ** 2) + ((perimeter - param) ** 2)
127
128        cell_energies = vmap(mapped_fn)(selected_faces, face_params[selected_faces])
129        return jnp.sum(cell_energies)
130
131    return energy_shape_factor

Factory for the periodic E1 energy with an explicit area stiffness.

Returns a callable with the signature of energy_shape_factor_hetero(), implementing

$$E_1 = \sum_\alpha \lambda_A\,(A_\alpha - 1)^2 + (P_\alpha - p^0_\alpha)^2 ,$$

with face_params holding the per-cell preferred perimeter \( p^0_\alpha \). At lambda_area = 1 it is energy_shape_factor_hetero() exactly.

lambda_area is closed over, not stored at module level, and it is never converted to a Python float, so it may be a traced array. That is what makes it trainable: an energy that reads lambda_area = exp(kappa) from an outer-parameter slot can call this factory inside itself, and jax.grad with respect to kappa flows through the area term. The exponential keeps the stiffness positive without a constraint.

def make_energy_line_tensions(K_areas: float) -> Callable: 
155def make_energy_line_tensions(K_areas: float) -> Callable:
156    r"""Factory for the periodic E2 energy with an **explicit** area stiffness.
157
158    Returns the function ``energy_line_tensions(vertTable, heTable, faceTable, width, height,
159    he_params, face_params)``, implementing exactly
160
161    .. math::
162        E_2 = \tfrac12\sum_{he}\Lambda_{he}\,\ell_{he}
163            + \tfrac{K}{2}\sum_\alpha (A_\alpha - A^0_\alpha)^2 ,
164
165    where the leading 1/2 on the tension term cancels the half-edge double count, so
166    ``he_params`` stores the physical per-edge tension directly.
167
168    ``K_areas`` is a required argument: it must be passed explicitly at every call site so
169    that the value used is always visible in the driver/notebook rather than buried in the
170    library.
171
172    The returned function takes the box size and not ``vert_params``, so it does not have the
173    6-argument inner-loss signature of the periodic optimizers (see the module docstring). Wrap it
174    to use it as ``PbcBilevelOptimizer.loss_function_inner``:
175
176    ```python
177    E2 = make_energy_line_tensions(K_areas)
178    optimizer.loss_function_inner = lambda v, h, f, _vp, hp, fp: E2(v, h, f, width, height, hp, fp)
179    ```
180    """
181
182    def energy_line_tensions(
183        vertTable: Array,
184        heTable: Array,
185        faceTable: Array,
186        width: float,
187        height: float,
188        he_params: Array,
189        face_params: Array,
190    ) -> Array:
191        """E2 energy for PBC meshes: elastic penalty on cell areas + line tensions x edge lengths."""
192
193        def mapped_areas_part(face: Array, face_param: Array) -> Array:
194            return _area_part(face, face_param, vertTable, heTable, faceTable, width, height)
195
196        def mapped_hedges_part(he: Array, he_param: Array) -> Array:
197            return _hedge_part(he, he_param, vertTable, heTable, faceTable, width, height)
198
199        areas_part = vmap(mapped_areas_part)(jnp.arange(len(faceTable)), face_params)
200        hedges_part = vmap(mapped_hedges_part)(jnp.arange(len(heTable)), he_params)
201        return (0.5 * jnp.sum(hedges_part)) + (0.5 * K_areas) * jnp.sum(areas_part)
202
203    return energy_line_tensions

Factory for the periodic E2 energy with an explicit area stiffness.

Returns the function energy_line_tensions(vertTable, heTable, faceTable, width, height, he_params, face_params), implementing exactly

$$E_2 = \tfrac12\sum_{he}\Lambda_{he}\,\ell_{he} + \tfrac{K}{2}\sum_\alpha (A_\alpha - A^0_\alpha)^2 ,$$

where the leading 1/2 on the tension term cancels the half-edge double count, so he_params stores the physical per-edge tension directly.

K_areas is a required argument: it must be passed explicitly at every call site so that the value used is always visible in the driver/notebook rather than buried in the library.

The returned function takes the box size and not vert_params, so it does not have the 6-argument inner-loss signature of the periodic optimizers (see the module docstring). Wrap it to use it as PbcBilevelOptimizer.loss_function_inner:

E2 = make_energy_line_tensions(K_areas)
optimizer.loss_function_inner = lambda v, h, f, _vp, hp, fp: E2(v, h, f, width, height, hp, fp)
def make_energy_line_tensions_bounded(K_areas: float, *, sigmoid_tensions: bool = False) -> Callable: 
232def make_energy_line_tensions_bounded(K_areas: float, *, sigmoid_tensions: bool = False) -> Callable:
233    r"""Factory for the bounded E2 energy, in the **same** convention as the periodic one.
234
235    .. math::
236        E_2 = \sum_{\text{edges}}\Lambda_e\,\ell_e
237            + \tfrac{K}{2}\sum_\alpha (A_\alpha - A^0_\alpha)^2 .
238
239    In this convention:
240
241    * ``K_areas`` is an explicit argument, so the area-stiffness value used is always visible
242      at the call site, and matches ``K_areas`` used by every periodic driver.
243    * Target areas are taken **per cell** from ``face_params``, so heterogeneous target areas
244      are supported.
245    * ``sigmoid_tensions`` is **off by default**: ``he_params`` are the raw physical tensions,
246      as in the periodic case. When enabled, ``he_params`` is instead passed through
247      ``sigmoid(he_params) + 1``, confining tensions to ``(1, 2)``; this is an opt-in option
248      because it usefully enforces positivity for inverse-design runs, but it makes
249      ``he_params`` mean a different quantity than in the periodic case, so it must be
250      requested explicitly and reported.
251    """
252
253    @jit
254    def energy_line_tensions_bounded(
255        vertTable: Array,
256        angTable: Array,
257        heTable: Array,
258        faceTable: Array,
259        _selected_verts: Array | None,
260        _selected_hes: Array | None,
261        _selected_faces: Array | None,
262        _vert_params: Array,
263        he_params: Array,
264        face_params: Array,
265    ) -> Array:
266        """E2 energy for bounded meshes: elastic penalty on cell areas + line tensions x edge lengths."""
267        num_faces = faceTable.shape[0]
268        faces = jnp.arange(num_faces)
269        num_edges = angTable.size
270        num_half_edges = num_edges * 2
271        unique_edges = jnp.arange(num_edges) * 2
272        edges = jnp.arange(num_half_edges)
273        vertTable = jnp.vstack([jnp.array([[0.0, 0.0], [1.0, 1.0]]), vertTable])
274        angTable = jnp.repeat(angTable, 2)
275        if sigmoid_tensions:
276            he_params = jax.nn.sigmoid(he_params) + 1
277        target_areas = jnp.broadcast_to(jnp.asarray(face_params).reshape(-1)[:1], (num_faces,)) \
278            if jnp.asarray(face_params).size == 1 else jnp.asarray(face_params).reshape(-1)[:num_faces]
279
280        def mapped_fn_area(face: Array, target_area: Array) -> Array:
281            return _cell_area_energy(face, target_area, vertTable, angTable, heTable, faceTable)
282
283        cell_area_energies = jnp.sum(vmap(mapped_fn_area)(faces, target_areas))
284
285        def mapped_fn_inner(edge: Array, tension: Array) -> Array:
286            return _inner_edge_energy(edge, tension, vertTable, heTable)
287
288        inner_edge_energies = jnp.sum(vmap(mapped_fn_inner)(unique_edges, he_params))
289
290        def mapped_fn_surface(edge: Array, tension: Array) -> Array:
291            return _surface_edge_energy(edge, tension, vertTable, angTable, heTable)
292
293        surface_edge_energies = jnp.sum(vmap(mapped_fn_surface)(edges, jnp.repeat(he_params, 2)))
294        return (0.5 * K_areas) * cell_area_energies + inner_edge_energies + surface_edge_energies
295
296    return energy_line_tensions_bounded

Factory for the bounded E2 energy, in the same convention as the periodic one.

$$E_2 = \sum_{\text{edges}}\Lambda_e\,\ell_e + \tfrac{K}{2}\sum_\alpha (A_\alpha - A^0_\alpha)^2 .$$

In this convention:

  • K_areas is an explicit argument, so the area-stiffness value used is always visible at the call site, and matches K_areas used by every periodic driver.
  • Target areas are taken per cell from face_params, so heterogeneous target areas are supported.
  • sigmoid_tensions is off by default: he_params are the raw physical tensions, as in the periodic case. When enabled, he_params is instead passed through sigmoid(he_params) + 1, confining tensions to (1, 2); this is an opt-in option because it usefully enforces positivity for inverse-design runs, but it makes he_params mean a different quantity than in the periodic case, so it must be requested explicitly and reported.
@dataclass
class TracedMesh: 
109@dataclass
110class TracedMesh:
111    """Straight-edge mesh traced from one label mask, in **pixel** units."""
112
113    stem: str
114    shape: tuple[int, int]
115    verts: NDArray            # (Nv, 2) float64, (x, y) in pixel-corner coordinates
116    vert_labels: list[frozenset]   # labels meeting at each vertex (may include 0 = background)
117    vert_cluster_size: NDArray     # (Nv,) int, number of lattice corners fused into this vertex
118    edges: NDArray            # (Ne, 2) int, vertex indices
119    edge_labels: NDArray      # (Ne, 2) int, the two labels the edge separates (sorted)
120    edge_arc_len: NDArray     # (Ne,) float64, length of the pixel-lattice polyline (staircase)
121    faces: list[list[int]]    # per cell, CCW cycle of vertex indices
122    face_labels: NDArray      # (Nf,) int, the cell label of each face
123    failures: dict            # cell label -> reason, for labels that did not close into a face
124    unmodelled: frozenset     # labels treated as missing environment (always contains 0)
125    junction_census: dict
126    diagnostics: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
127
128    # -- derived ---------------------------------------------------------------------
129    @property
130    def n_verts(self) -> int:
131        return len(self.verts)
132
133    @property
134    def n_edges(self) -> int:
135        return len(self.edges)
136
137    @property
138    def n_faces(self) -> int:
139        return len(self.faces)
140
141    @property
142    def clamped(self) -> NDArray:
143        """(Nv,) bool -- True where an unmodelled material is one of the incident labels."""
144        return np.array([bool(s & self.unmodelled) for s in self.vert_labels], dtype=bool)
145
146    @property
147    def free(self) -> NDArray:
148        return ~self.clamped
149
150    @property
151    def edge_is_cell_cell(self) -> NDArray:
152        """True iff both flanking materials are modelled cells (a real interface)."""
153        um = self.unmodelled
154        return np.array([(int(a) not in um) and (int(b) not in um)
155                         for a, b in self.edge_labels], dtype=bool)
156
157    @property
158    def face_is_interior(self) -> NDArray:
159        """A face is interior iff none of its edges borders an unmodelled material."""
160        touching = set()
161        for (a, b) in self.edge_labels[~self.edge_is_cell_cell]:
162            a, b = int(a), int(b)
163            if a not in self.unmodelled:
164                touching.add(a)
165            if b not in self.unmodelled:
166                touching.add(b)
167        return np.array([int(l) not in touching for l in self.face_labels], dtype=bool)
168
169    def face_areas(self, verts: NDArray | None = None) -> NDArray:
170        v = self.verts if verts is None else verts
171        return np.array([_shoelace(v[f]) for f in self.faces])
172
173    def face_perimeters(self, verts: NDArray | None = None) -> NDArray:
174        v = self.verts if verts is None else verts
175        out = []
176        for f in self.faces:
177            p = v[f]
178            out.append(float(np.linalg.norm(np.roll(p, -1, axis=0) - p, axis=1).sum()))
179        return np.array(out)
180
181    def edge_lengths(self, verts: NDArray | None = None) -> NDArray:
182        v = self.verts if verts is None else verts
183        return np.linalg.norm(v[self.edges[:, 1]] - v[self.edges[:, 0]], axis=1)

Straight-edge mesh traced from one label mask, in pixel units.

161        for (a, b) in self.edge_labels[~self.edge_is_cell_cell]:
162            a, b = int(a), int(b)
163            if a not in self.unmodelled:
164                touching.add(a)
165            if b not in self.unmodelled:
166                touching.add(b)
167        return np.array([int(l) not in touching for l in self.face_labels], dtype=bool)

A face is interior iff none of its edges borders an unmodelled material.

def face_areas( self, verts: numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[+_ScalarType_co]] | None = None) -> numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[+_ScalarType_co]]: 
169    def face_areas(self, verts: NDArray | None = None) -> NDArray:
170        v = self.verts if verts is None else verts
171        return np.array([_shoelace(v[f]) for f in self.faces])
def face_perimeters( self, verts: numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[+_ScalarType_co]] | None = None) -> numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[+_ScalarType_co]]: 
173    def face_perimeters(self, verts: NDArray | None = None) -> NDArray:
174        v = self.verts if verts is None else verts
175        out = []
176        for f in self.faces:
177            p = v[f]
178            out.append(float(np.linalg.norm(np.roll(p, -1, axis=0) - p, axis=1).sum()))
179        return np.array(out)
def edge_lengths( self, verts: numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[+_ScalarType_co]] | None = None) -> numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[+_ScalarType_co]]: 
181    def edge_lengths(self, verts: NDArray | None = None) -> NDArray:
182        v = self.verts if verts is None else verts
183        return np.linalg.norm(v[self.edges[:, 1]] - v[self.edges[:, 0]], axis=1)
def regularize( mask: numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[+_ScalarType_co]]) -> tuple[numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[+_ScalarType_co]], dict]: 
556def regularize(mask: NDArray) -> tuple[NDArray, dict]:
557    """Remove label debris from a segmentation mask, and report exactly how much was moved.
558
559    Automatic segmentation leaves pixel-level debris: a label may own stray one- or two-pixel
560    islands disconnected from its main body. These are not tissue, and they matter here because
561    they are **topological** rather than merely cosmetic. A stray island of label ``L`` sitting
562    inside cell ``M`` creates a closed boundary loop; if that loop's junction corners fall into a
563    single 8-connected cluster it collapses to a self-loop arc, which no straight-edge polygon can
564    represent, and which can in turn break the outline of the cell that owns it.
565
566    The rule, and it is deliberately the weakest one that fixes the problem:
567
568        For every label, keep only its largest 8-connected component. Pixels in the smaller
569        components are reassigned to the label of the nearest surviving pixel, which may be
570        background.
571
572    **Nothing else is touched** -- no dilation, no erosion, no hole filling, no smoothing, no
573    relabelling, no gap filling across the background margin. Anything more would be editing the
574    data rather than making it representable.
575
576    Args:
577        mask: integer label image; `0` is unsegmented space. Not modified.
578
579    Returns:
580        `(clean, report)`. `report` carries `n_labels_with_islands`, `n_pixels_moved`,
581        `frac_pixels_moved` and the per-label island sizes.
582
583    Note:
584        `report["frac_pixels_moved"]` is not decoration — **check it.** It should be negligible
585        (order `1e-4` or below on a good segmentation). If it is not, that is a finding about the
586        segmentation and should be investigated, not a licence to clean harder.
587    """
588    mask = np.asarray(mask)
589    out = mask.copy()
590    removed = np.zeros(mask.shape, dtype=bool)
591    per_label: dict[int, list[int]] = {}
592
593    for lv in np.unique(mask):
594        lv = int(lv)
595        if lv == 0:
596            continue
597        sel = mask == lv
598        comp, k = ndi.label(sel, structure=STRUCT8)
599        if k <= 1:
600            continue
601        sizes = np.asarray(ndi.sum(sel, comp, index=np.arange(1, k + 1)))
602        keep = int(np.argmax(sizes)) + 1
603        drop = sel & (comp != keep)
604        removed |= drop
605        per_label[lv] = sorted((sizes[np.arange(1, k + 1) != keep]).astype(int).tolist(),
606                               reverse=True)
607
608    n_removed = int(removed.sum())
609    if n_removed:
610        out[removed] = 0
611        _, idx = ndi.distance_transform_edt(removed, return_indices=True)
612        out[removed] = out[tuple(i[removed] for i in idx)]
613
614    report = {
615        "n_labels_with_islands": len(per_label),
616        "n_pixels_moved": n_removed,
617        "frac_pixels_moved": n_removed / mask.size,
618        "island_sizes_per_label": per_label,
619    }
620    return out, report

Remove label debris from a segmentation mask, and report exactly how much was moved.

Automatic segmentation leaves pixel-level debris: a label may own stray one- or two-pixel islands disconnected from its main body. These are not tissue, and they matter here because they are topological rather than merely cosmetic. A stray island of label L sitting inside cell M creates a closed boundary loop; if that loop's junction corners fall into a single 8-connected cluster it collapses to a self-loop arc, which no straight-edge polygon can represent, and which can in turn break the outline of the cell that owns it.

The rule, and it is deliberately the weakest one that fixes the problem:

For every label, keep only its largest 8-connected component. Pixels in the smaller
components are reassigned to the label of the nearest surviving pixel, which may be
background.

Nothing else is touched -- no dilation, no erosion, no hole filling, no smoothing, no relabelling, no gap filling across the background margin. Anything more would be editing the data rather than making it representable.

Args: mask: integer label image; 0 is unsegmented space. Not modified.

Returns: (clean, report). report carries n_labels_with_islands, n_pixels_moved, frac_pixels_moved and the per-label island sizes.

Note: report["frac_pixels_moved"] is not decoration — check it. It should be negligible (order 1e-4 or below on a good segmentation). If it is not, that is a finding about the segmentation and should be investigated, not a licence to clean harder.

def trace_mask( mask: numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[+_ScalarType_co]], stem: str = '', rim_tol: float = 2.0, unmodelled: Iterable[int] = (0,)) -> TracedMesh: 
261def trace_mask(mask: NDArray, stem: str = "", rim_tol: float = 2.0,
262               unmodelled: Iterable[int] = (0,)) -> TracedMesh:
263    """Trace one label mask into a straight-edge mesh.
264
265    Args:
266        mask: integer label image, `0` for unsegmented space. Not modified.
267        stem: optional identifier carried through onto the returned mesh, for reporting.
268        rim_tol: Ramer-Douglas-Peucker tolerance in pixels, applied to **clamped cell-background
269            arcs only**. Interior cell-cell interfaces are always single straight chords whatever
270            this is set to, so `rim_tol` cannot affect an interior cell's area. See the module
271            docstring for why the rim is treated differently and why this adds no free parameter.
272        unmodelled: labels treated as missing environment. Background `0` is always included,
273            whatever is passed. A cell whose outline does not close into a simple cycle — a
274            segmentation topology defect, such as a region pinched to a point — must be added here
275            and the trace repeated; the reason is the same one that clamps the background rim, that
276            its mechanics cannot be written from the data, so every vertex it touches loses its
277            force balance. `trace_mask_closed` performs that iteration automatically and is usually
278            what you want.
279
280    Returns:
281        A `TracedMesh`. Cells that failed to close are recorded in `TracedMesh.failures` and are
282        **not** faces; this call does not raise on them.
283
284    Raises:
285        AssertionError: if a lattice corner comes out with boundary degree 1, which is
286            geometrically impossible and therefore means this tracer is wrong rather than that the
287            mask is unusual.
288    """
289    unmodelled = frozenset(int(u) for u in unmodelled) | frozenset({0})
290    mask = np.asarray(mask)
291    H, W = mask.shape
292    NW, NE, SW, SE, deg = _corner_fields(mask)
293
294    if (deg == 1).any():
295        raise AssertionError("corner of boundary degree 1 -- impossible, tracer is wrong")
296
297    # -- vertices: 8-connected clusters of degree>=3 corners --------------------------
298    jmask = deg >= 3
299    lab, n_clusters = ndi.label(jmask, structure=np.ones((3, 3), dtype=int))
300    corner_to_vert = np.full(jmask.shape, -1, dtype=np.int64)
301    corner_to_vert[jmask] = lab[jmask] - 1
302
303    verts = np.zeros((n_clusters, 2), dtype=np.float64)
304    vert_labels: list[frozenset] = [frozenset() for _ in range(n_clusters)]
305    cluster_size = np.zeros(n_clusters, dtype=np.int64)
306    ii, jj = np.nonzero(jmask)
307    acc = np.zeros((n_clusters, 2), dtype=np.float64)
308    lsets: list[set] = [set() for _ in range(n_clusters)]
309    for i, j in zip(ii.tolist(), jj.tolist()):
310        v = int(corner_to_vert[i, j])
311        acc[v] += (j, i)                       # (x, y)
312        cluster_size[v] += 1
313        lsets[v].update((int(NW[i, j]), int(NE[i, j]), int(SW[i, j]), int(SE[i, j])))
314    verts = acc / cluster_size[:, None]
315    vert_labels = [frozenset(s) for s in lsets]
316
317    # -- arcs: walk each degree-2 chain between two vertex clusters --------------------
318    used: set[tuple] = set()
319    arcs: list[tuple[int, int, tuple, NDArray]] = []     # (v0, v1, label_pair, polyline)
320    self_loops: list[tuple] = []
321    for i0, j0 in zip(ii.tolist(), jj.tolist()):
322        v0 = int(corner_to_vert[i0, j0])
323        for (nb, pair, seg) in _incident(i0, j0, NW, NE, SW, SE):
324            if seg in used:
325                continue
326            ni, nj = nb
327            if corner_to_vert[ni, nj] == v0:
328                used.add(seg)                  # segment internal to the junction cluster
329                continue
330            used.add(seg)
331            path = [(i0, j0), (ni, nj)]
332            prev, cur = (i0, j0), (ni, nj)
333            steps = 0
334            while corner_to_vert[cur[0], cur[1]] < 0:
335                nxt = None
336                for (nb2, pair2, seg2) in _incident(cur[0], cur[1], NW, NE, SW, SE):
337                    if nb2 == prev or seg2 in used:
338                        continue
339                    nxt = (nb2, pair2, seg2)
340                if nxt is None:
341                    raise AssertionError(f"dead end while tracing arc from {(i0, j0)}")
342                if nxt[1] != pair:
343                    raise AssertionError("label pair changed along a degree-2 chain")
344                used.add(nxt[2])
345                prev, cur = cur, nxt[0]
346                path.append(cur)
347                steps += 1
348                if steps > 4 * (H + W):
349                    raise AssertionError("runaway arc walk")
350            v1 = int(corner_to_vert[cur[0], cur[1]])
351            poly = np.array([(c, r) for (r, c) in path], dtype=np.float64)   # (x, y)
352            if v1 == v0:
353                self_loops.append((pair, float(len(path) - 1)))
354                continue
355            arcs.append((v0, v1, pair, poly))
356
357    # -- straight edges; clamped cell-background arcs are subdivided (no free DOF added) ---
358    n_junc = int(n_clusters)                        # junction vertices, before any subdivision
359    vert_list = [verts[k] for k in range(n_clusters)]
360    lset_list = list(lsets)
361    csize_list = cluster_size.tolist()
362    e_ends: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
363    e_labels: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
364    e_arclen: list[float] = []
365    sagitta_cc: list[float] = []
366    sagitta_cc_rel: list[float] = []
367    n_inserted = 0
368    for (v0, v1, pair, poly) in arcs:
369        arclen = float(len(poly) - 1)
370        if (pair[0] not in unmodelled) and (pair[1] not in unmodelled):   # real interface: chord
371            e_ends.append((v0, v1))
372            e_labels.append(pair)
373            e_arclen.append(arclen)
374            s = _sagitta(poly)
375            sagitta_cc.append(s)
376            chord = float(np.linalg.norm(poly[-1] - poly[0]))
377            sagitta_cc_rel.append(s / chord if chord > 0 else np.nan)
378            continue
379        # clamped arc: subdivide. The arc's polyline runs from a corner of cluster v0 to a
380        # corner of cluster v1; anchor its ends on the cluster centroids so the mesh stays closed.
381        keep = _rdp(poly, rim_tol)
382        chain = [v0]
383        for k in keep[1:-1]:
384            vert_list.append(poly[k])
385            lset_list.append(set(pair))
386            csize_list.append(1)
387            chain.append(len(vert_list) - 1)
388            n_inserted += 1
389        chain.append(v1)
390        for a, b in zip(chain[:-1], chain[1:]):
391            e_ends.append((a, b))
392            e_labels.append(pair)
393            e_arclen.append(arclen / (len(chain) - 1))
394
395    verts = np.asarray(vert_list, dtype=np.float64)
396    vert_labels = [frozenset(s) for s in lset_list]
397    cluster_size = np.asarray(csize_list, dtype=np.int64)
398    n_clusters = len(verts)
399    edges = np.array(e_ends, dtype=np.int64).reshape(-1, 2)
400    edge_labels = np.array(e_labels, dtype=np.int64).reshape(-1, 2)
401    edge_arc_len = np.array(e_arclen, dtype=np.float64)
402
403    # -- faces: for each cell label, close the cycle of its edges ----------------------
404    cell_labels = sorted(int(l) for l in np.unique(mask) if int(l) not in unmodelled)
405    inc: dict[int, list[int]] = defaultdict(list)
406    for k, (a, b) in enumerate(edge_labels.tolist()):
407        if a not in unmodelled:
408            inc[a].append(k)
409        if b not in unmodelled:
410            inc[b].append(k)
411
412    faces: list[list[int]] = []
413    face_labels: list[int] = []
414    failures: dict[int, str] = {}
415    for cl in cell_labels:
416        ek = inc.get(cl, [])
417        if len(ek) < 3:
418            failures[cl] = f"only {len(ek)} incident edges"
419            continue
420        adj: dict[int, list[int]] = defaultdict(list)
421        for k in ek:
422            a, b = int(edges[k, 0]), int(edges[k, 1])
423            adj[a].append(b)
424            adj[b].append(a)
425        bad = [v for v, nb in adj.items() if len(nb) != 2]
426        if bad:
427            failures[cl] = f"{len(bad)} vertices of cell-degree != 2 (non-manifold outline)"
428            continue
429        start = next(iter(adj))
430        cycle = [start]
431        prev, cur = start, adj[start][0]
432        while cur != start:
433            cycle.append(cur)
434            nb = adj[cur]
435            nxt = nb[0] if nb[0] != prev else nb[1]
436            prev, cur = cur, nxt
437            if len(cycle) > len(ek) + 1:
438                break
439        if len(cycle) != len(ek):
440            failures[cl] = f"outline is not one closed cycle ({len(cycle)} of {len(ek)} edges)"
441            continue
442        poly = verts[cycle]
443        if _shoelace(poly) < 0:
444            cycle = cycle[::-1]
445        faces.append(cycle)
446        face_labels.append(cl)
447
448    junc_lsets = [frozenset(s) for s in lsets]
449    census = {
450        "n_junction_corners": int(jmask.sum()),
451        "n_junction_vertices": n_junc,
452        "n_inserted_rim_vertices": int(n_inserted),
453        "rim_tol_px": float(rim_tol),
454        "cluster_size_hist": dict(sorted(
455            (int(k), int(v)) for k, v in zip(*np.unique(cluster_size[:n_junc],
456                                                        return_counts=True)))),
457        "junction_order_hist": dict(sorted(
458            (int(k), int(v)) for k, v in zip(*np.unique([len(s) for s in junc_lsets],
459                                                        return_counts=True)))),
460        "deg4_corners": int((deg == 4).sum()),
461        "self_loop_arcs": len(self_loops),
462        "self_loop_detail": [(list(p), n) for p, n in self_loops],
463        "sagitta_cc_px_median": float(np.median(sagitta_cc)) if sagitta_cc else float("nan"),
464        "sagitta_cc_px_p90": float(np.percentile(sagitta_cc, 90)) if sagitta_cc else float("nan"),
465        "sagitta_cc_rel_median": float(np.nanmedian(sagitta_cc_rel)) if sagitta_cc else float("nan"),
466        "sagitta_cc_rel_p90": (float(np.nanpercentile(sagitta_cc_rel, 90))
467                               if sagitta_cc else float("nan")),
468    }
469    return TracedMesh(
470        stem=stem, shape=(H, W), verts=verts, vert_labels=vert_labels,
471        vert_cluster_size=cluster_size, edges=edges, edge_labels=edge_labels,
472        edge_arc_len=edge_arc_len, faces=faces, face_labels=np.array(face_labels, dtype=np.int64),
473        failures=failures, unmodelled=unmodelled, junction_census=census,
474    )

Trace one label mask into a straight-edge mesh.

Args: mask: integer label image, 0 for unsegmented space. Not modified. stem: optional identifier carried through onto the returned mesh, for reporting. rim_tol: Ramer-Douglas-Peucker tolerance in pixels, applied to clamped cell-background arcs only. Interior cell-cell interfaces are always single straight chords whatever this is set to, so rim_tol cannot affect an interior cell's area. See the module docstring for why the rim is treated differently and why this adds no free parameter. unmodelled: labels treated as missing environment. Background 0 is always included, whatever is passed. A cell whose outline does not close into a simple cycle — a segmentation topology defect, such as a region pinched to a point — must be added here and the trace repeated; the reason is the same one that clamps the background rim, that its mechanics cannot be written from the data, so every vertex it touches loses its force balance. trace_mask_closed performs that iteration automatically and is usually what you want.

Returns: A TracedMesh. Cells that failed to close are recorded in TracedMesh.failures and are not faces; this call does not raise on them.

Raises: AssertionError: if a lattice corner comes out with boundary degree 1, which is geometrically impossible and therefore means this tracer is wrong rather than that the mask is unusual.

def trace_mask_closed( mask: numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[+_ScalarType_co]], stem: str = '', rim_tol: float = 2.0, max_rounds: int = 4) -> TracedMesh: 
477def trace_mask_closed(mask: NDArray, stem: str = "", rim_tol: float = 2.0,
478                      max_rounds: int = 4) -> TracedMesh:
479    """Trace, then demote any cell whose outline did not close to unmodelled, and re-trace.
480
481    A cell that fails to close is a segmentation topology defect (e.g. a region pinched to a
482    point, which is 8-connected but not simply connected as a polygon). It is handled exactly as
483    the background is: it becomes missing environment, its vertices are clamped, and no tension is
484    charged on its interfaces. It does not raise. The cumulative list of demoted cells is reported
485    in `mesh.diagnostics["failures_cumulative"]` and their number in
486    `mesh.diagnostics["n_demoted_cells"]`; if cells still fail to close after `max_rounds` rounds,
487    `mesh.diagnostics["unresolved"]` is True and `mesh.failures` lists them.
488    """
489    um: set[int] = {0}
490    hist: dict[int, str] = {}
491    for _ in range(max_rounds):
492        m = trace_mask(mask, stem=stem, rim_tol=rim_tol, unmodelled=um)
493        if not m.failures:
494            m.diagnostics["failures_cumulative"] = dict(hist)
495            m.diagnostics["n_demoted_cells"] = len(um) - 1
496            return m
497        hist.update(m.failures)
498        um |= set(m.failures)
499    m.diagnostics["failures_cumulative"] = dict(hist)
500    m.diagnostics["n_demoted_cells"] = len(um) - 1
501    m.diagnostics["unresolved"] = True
502    return m

Trace, then demote any cell whose outline did not close to unmodelled, and re-trace.

A cell that fails to close is a segmentation topology defect (e.g. a region pinched to a point, which is 8-connected but not simply connected as a polygon). It is handled exactly as the background is: it becomes missing environment, its vertices are clamped, and no tension is charged on its interfaces. It does not raise. The cumulative list of demoted cells is reported in mesh.diagnostics["failures_cumulative"] and their number in mesh.diagnostics["n_demoted_cells"]; if cells still fail to close after max_rounds rounds, mesh.diagnostics["unresolved"] is True and mesh.failures lists them.

def vertex_degrees( m: TracedMesh) -> numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[+_ScalarType_co]]: 
506def vertex_degrees(m: TracedMesh) -> NDArray:
507    """Number of edges incident to each vertex of a traced mesh, as an integer array of length ``m.n_verts``."""
508    d = np.zeros(m.n_verts, dtype=np.int64)
509    for a, b in m.edges.tolist():
510        d[a] += 1
511        d[b] += 1
512    return d

Number of edges incident to each vertex of a traced mesh, as an integer array of length m.n_verts.

def rasterize_face( m: TracedMesh, k: int) -> tuple[numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[+_ScalarType_co]], tuple[int, int, int, int]]: 
515def rasterize_face(m: TracedMesh, k: int) -> tuple[NDArray, tuple[int, int, int, int]]:
516    """Boolean raster of face k over its bounding box, using pixel centres."""
517    from matplotlib.path import Path
518
519    poly = m.verts[m.faces[k]]
520    x0 = max(int(np.floor(poly[:, 0].min())) - 1, 0)
521    x1 = min(int(np.ceil(poly[:, 0].max())) + 1, m.shape[1])
522    y0 = max(int(np.floor(poly[:, 1].min())) - 1, 0)
523    y1 = min(int(np.ceil(poly[:, 1].max())) + 1, m.shape[0])
524    xs = np.arange(x0, x1) + 0.5
525    ys = np.arange(y0, y1) + 0.5
526    gx, gy = np.meshgrid(xs, ys)
527    pts = np.column_stack([gx.ravel(), gy.ravel()])
528    inside = Path(poly).contains_points(pts).reshape(len(ys), len(xs))
529    return inside, (y0, y1, x0, x1)

Boolean raster of face k over its bounding box, using pixel centres.

def normalized( m: TracedMesh, a_ref: float) -> numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[+_ScalarType_co]]: 
532def normalized(m: TracedMesh, a_ref: float) -> NDArray:
533    """Vertex coordinates in units of sqrt(A_ref), so that <A_interior> = 1 by construction."""
534    return m.verts / np.sqrt(a_ref)

Vertex coordinates in units of sqrt(A_ref), so that = 1 by construction.

def interior_area_ref(m: TracedMesh) -> float: 
537def interior_area_ref(m: TracedMesh) -> float:
538    """Reference cell area: the mean area of the interior (non-rim) faces of a traced mesh.
539
540    Falls back to the mean over all faces when the mesh has no interior face.
541    """
542    A = m.face_areas()
543    sel = m.face_is_interior
544    if sel.sum() == 0:
545        return float(A.mean())
546    return float(A[sel].mean())

Reference cell area: the mean area of the interior (non-rim) faces of a traced mesh.

Falls back to the mean over all faces when the mesh has no interior face.

@dataclass
class ClampedPatch: 
111@dataclass
112class ClampedPatch:
113    """Geometry and boundary partition of one clamped patch, in units of `sqrt(A_ref)`.
114
115    Faces are stored as a flat list of polygon corners rather than as cycles, so that areas and
116    perimeters are one `segment_sum` each: `PA[i] -> PB[i]` is a polygon edge belonging to face
117    `PF[i]`.
118
119    Attributes:
120        stem: identifier of the crop this came from.
121        x0: `(Nv, 2)` observed vertex positions, normalised by `sqrt(A_ref)`.
122        PA, PB, PF: polygon-corner arrays — start vertex, end vertex, owning face.
123        nf: number of faces.
124        EA, EB: endpoints of the **cell-cell** edges only. Edges bordering unimaged space carry no
125            tension and exert no force on any free vertex; see `clamped_edges_are_inert`.
126        free_idx: indices of vertices whose force balance can be written from the data.
127        n_free: `len(free_idx)`, cached because the residual normalises by it.
128        a_ref_px: the reference area in px², i.e. the square of the length unit.
129        face_is_interior: faces none of whose edges borders unimaged space.
130        face_labels: original segmentation label of each face.
131    """
132
133    stem: str
134    x0: NDArray
135    PA: NDArray
136    PB: NDArray
137    PF: NDArray
138    nf: int
139    EA: NDArray
140    EB: NDArray
141    free_idx: NDArray
142    a_ref_px: float
143    face_is_interior: NDArray
144    face_labels: NDArray
145    n_free: int

Geometry and boundary partition of one clamped patch, in units of sqrt(A_ref).

Faces are stored as a flat list of polygon corners rather than as cycles, so that areas and perimeters are one segment_sum each: PA[i] -> PB[i] is a polygon edge belonging to face PF[i].

Attributes: stem: identifier of the crop this came from. x0: (Nv, 2) observed vertex positions, normalised by sqrt(A_ref). PA, PB, PF: polygon-corner arrays — start vertex, end vertex, owning face. nf: number of faces. EA, EB: endpoints of the cell-cell edges only. Edges bordering unimaged space carry no tension and exert no force on any free vertex; see clamped_edges_are_inert. free_idx: indices of vertices whose force balance can be written from the data. n_free: len(free_idx), cached because the residual normalises by it. a_ref_px: the reference area in px², i.e. the square of the length unit. face_is_interior: faces none of whose edges borders unimaged space. face_labels: original segmentation label of each face.
