def patch_geometry(x, patch: ClampedPatch, eps: float = 0.0): 
246def patch_geometry(x, patch: ClampedPatch, eps: float = 0.0):  # noqa: ANN001, ANN201
247    """Signed face areas, face perimeters and cell-cell edge lengths at configuration `x`.
248
249    The three quantities every energy on a patch is built from, computed together because they
250    share the same gather. Areas are signed — see `signed_face_areas`.
251
252    Args:
253        x: `(Nv, 2)` vertex positions in normalised units.
254        patch: the patch whose connectivity to use.
255        eps: edge-length smoothing, passed to `smoothed_norm`. Applies to perimeters and edge
256            lengths; areas are polynomial and need no smoothing.
257
258    Returns:
259        `(areas, perimeters, edge_lengths)`, with `edge_lengths` over cell-cell edges only.
260    """
261    pa, pb = x[patch.PA], x[patch.PB]
262    A = _areas_from_corners(pa, pb, patch)
263    P = segment_sum(smoothed_norm(pb - pa, eps), patch.PF, patch.nf)
264    L = smoothed_norm(x[patch.EB] - x[patch.EA], eps)
265    return A, P, L

Signed face areas, face perimeters and cell-cell edge lengths at configuration x.

The three quantities every energy on a patch is built from, computed together because they share the same gather. Areas are signed — see signed_face_areas.

Args: x: (Nv, 2) vertex positions in normalised units. patch: the patch whose connectivity to use. eps: edge-length smoothing, passed to smoothed_norm. Applies to perimeters and edge lengths; areas are polynomial and need no smoothing.

Returns: (areas, perimeters, edge_lengths), with edge_lengths over cell-cell edges only.

def signed_face_areas(x, patch: ClampedPatch): 
219def signed_face_areas(x, patch: ClampedPatch):  # noqa: ANN001, ANN201
220    """Shoelace area per face, **signed**, counter-clockwise positive.
221
222    Explicitly signed, and not `vertax.geo.get_area`, which returns `0.5 * |shoelace|`. The absolute
223    value is right for the periodic meshes that function serves and is left alone; here it would
224    hide the two failure modes that matter on real geometry. An area term built on `|A|` has a
225    spurious minimum at `A = 0`, so a collapsing cell reads as an improvement, and it scores an
226    inverted cell identically to a healthy one.
227
228    Callers should treat `A <= 0` as an inverted face and a small positive `A` as a collapsing one.
229    """
230    pa, pb = x[patch.PA], x[patch.PB]
231    return _areas_from_corners(pa, pb, patch)

Shoelace area per face, signed, counter-clockwise positive.

Explicitly signed, and not vertax.geo.get_area, which returns 0.5 * |shoelace|. The absolute value is right for the periodic meshes that function serves and is left alone; here it would hide the two failure modes that matter on real geometry. An area term built on |A| has a spurious minimum at A = 0, so a collapsing cell reads as an improvement, and it scores an inverted cell identically to a healthy one.

Callers should treat A <= 0 as an inverted face and a small positive A as a collapsing one.

def clamped_edges_are_inert(mesh_npz: str | pathlib.Path) -> dict: 
477def clamped_edges_are_inert(mesh_npz: str | Path) -> dict:
478    """Check that edges bordering unimaged space exert no force on any free vertex.
479
480    This module drops the tension term on cell-background edges entirely. That is only legitimate
481    if those edges cannot influence the force balance where it is written — and they cannot,
482    because both endpoints of such an edge are clamped by construction. The claim is checkable, so
483    it should be checked rather than assumed.
484
485    Builds the tension energy twice, over all edges and over cell-cell edges only, and compares the
486    two gradients on the free components. They must agree to machine precision.
487
488    Returns:
489        `max_abs_diff_free` (expected ~1e-16), `rel` relative to the cell-cell gradient scale, and
490        `max_abs_diff_clamped`, which is expected to be LARGE — the clamped rows are exactly where
491        the dropped term does act, and it is not a residual there because no equation is written.
492    """
493    z = np.load(mesh_npz, allow_pickle=True)
494    a_ref = float(z["a_ref_px"])
495    x = jnp.asarray(np.asarray(z["verts_px"], np.float64) / np.sqrt(a_ref))
496    e_all = jnp.asarray(np.asarray(z["edges"]))
497    cc = np.asarray(z["edge_is_cellcell"], bool)
498    free = np.nonzero(np.asarray(z["free"], bool))[0]
499
500    def tens(edges):  # noqa: ANN001, ANN202
501        """Unit-tension energy over the given edge set: sum of edge lengths."""
502        return lambda xx: jnp.sum(jnp.linalg.norm(xx[edges[:, 1]] - xx[edges[:, 0]], axis=1))
503
504    g_all = np.asarray(jax.grad(tens(e_all))(x))
505    g_cc = np.asarray(jax.grad(tens(jnp.asarray(np.asarray(z["edges"])[cc])))(x))
506    d = np.abs(g_all[free] - g_cc[free]).max()
507    return {"max_abs_diff_free": float(d),
508            "rel": float(d / max(np.abs(g_cc[free]).max(), 1e-300)),
509            "max_abs_diff_clamped": float(np.abs(g_all - g_cc).max())}

Check that edges bordering unimaged space exert no force on any free vertex.

This module drops the tension term on cell-background edges entirely. That is only legitimate if those edges cannot influence the force balance where it is written — and they cannot, because both endpoints of such an edge are clamped by construction. The claim is checkable, so it should be checked rather than assumed.

Builds the tension energy twice, over all edges and over cell-cell edges only, and compares the two gradients on the free components. They must agree to machine precision.

Returns: max_abs_diff_free (expected ~1e-16), rel relative to the cell-cell gradient scale, and max_abs_diff_clamped, which is expected to be LARGE — the clamped rows are exactly where the dropped term does act, and it is not a residual there because no equation is written.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ShearMode: 
128@dataclass(frozen=True)
129class ShearMode:
130    r"""A single Fourier drive mode: which axis is modulated, which is driven, and the weights.
131
132    ``mod_axis`` selects the modulation direction (0 = :math:`\cos(qx)`, 1 = :math:`\cos(qy)`) and
133    ``pol_axis`` the polarisation of the force and of the observed displacement. The four
134    combinations give three independent constants of an orthotropic 2D tissue:
135
136    ===============  ==============  ============  ==========
137    modulation       polarisation    character     constant
138    ===============  ==============  ============  ==========
139    ``cos(qy)``      ``x``           transverse    ``C66 = G``
140    ``cos(qx)``      ``y``           transverse    ``C66`` (consistency check)
141    ``cos(qy)``      ``y``           longitudinal  ``C22``
142    ``cos(qx)``      ``x``           longitudinal  ``C11``
143    ===============  ==============  ============  ==========
144
145    Attributes:
146        c: Mean-removed weights :math:`\hat c_i`, one per vertex, frozen on the reference state.
147        r0: Reference vertex positions, shape ``(N, 2)``.
148        q: Wavevector :math:`2\pi n/L_{\rm mod}`.
149        n: Mode index.
150        width, height: Box dimensions.
151        mod_axis, pol_axis: See above.
152        rho_v: Vertex number density :math:`N/(WH)` — the force-balance calibration constant.
153        c_sq: :math:`\sum_i\hat c_i^2`.
154        c_sq_ratio: :math:`2\sum\hat c_i^2/N`. **Finite-size diagnostic, not a correction factor.**
155            The continuum calibration :math:`G=\rho_v/(Jq^2)` follows from force balance
156            (:math:`f_x(y)=a\rho_v\cos qy`) and is the definition used here. Equating the *discrete*
157            drive energy :math:`-aU\sum\hat c_i^2` to the continuum :math:`-\tfrac12 FUWH` instead
158            gives :math:`F=2a\sum\hat c_i^2/(WH)`, i.e. the same thing multiplied by this ratio. The
159            two routes agree exactly only for a uniform vertex distribution, so a ratio far from 1
160            measures the density fluctuation the continuum calibration neglects, at
161            :math:`O(N^{-1/2})`. Report it; do not silently divide by it.
162    """
163
164    c: Array
165    r0: Array
166    q: float
167    n: int
168    width: float
169    height: float
170    mod_axis: int
171    pol_axis: int
172    rho_v: float
173    c_sq: float
174    c_sq_ratio: float
175
176    @property
177    def pol_period(self) -> float:
178        """Box length along the polarisation axis — the period for the minimum-image wrap."""
179        return self.width if self.pol_axis == 0 else self.height
180
181    @property
182    def mod_period(self) -> float:
183        """Box length along the modulation axis."""
184        return self.width if self.mod_axis == 0 else self.height
185
186    @property
187    def label(self) -> str:
188        """Short human-readable tag, e.g. ``n1_cosy_polx``."""
189        return f"n{self.n}_cos{'xy'[self.mod_axis]}_pol{'xy'[self.pol_axis]}"

A single Fourier drive mode: which axis is modulated, which is driven, and the weights.

mod_axis selects the modulation direction (0 = \( \cos(qx) \), 1 = \( \cos(qy) \)) and pol_axis the polarisation of the force and of the observed displacement. The four combinations give three independent constants of an orthotropic 2D tissue:

=============== ============== ============ ========== modulation polarisation character constant =============== ============== ============ ========== cos(qy) x transverse C66 = G cos(qx) y transverse C66 (consistency check) cos(qy) y longitudinal C22 cos(qx) x longitudinal C11 =============== ============== ============ ==========

Attributes: c: Mean-removed weights \( \hat c_i \), one per vertex, frozen on the reference state. r0: Reference vertex positions, shape (N, 2). q: Wavevector \( 2\pi n/L_{\rm mod} \). n: Mode index. width, height: Box dimensions. mod_axis, pol_axis: See above. rho_v: Vertex number density \( N/(WH) \) — the force-balance calibration constant. c_sq: \( \sum_i\hat c_i^2 \). c_sq_ratio: \( 2\sum\hat c_i^2/N \). Finite-size diagnostic, not a correction factor. The continuum calibration \( G=\rho_v/(Jq^2) \) follows from force balance (\( f_x(y)=a\rho_v\cos qy \)) and is the definition used here. Equating the discrete drive energy \( -aU\sum\hat c_i^2 \) to the continuum \( -\tfrac12 FUWH \) instead gives \( F=2a\sum\hat c_i^2/(WH) \), i.e. the same thing multiplied by this ratio. The two routes agree exactly only for a uniform vertex distribution, so a ratio far from 1 measures the density fluctuation the continuum calibration neglects, at \( O(N^{-1/2}) \). Report it; do not silently divide by it.

@dataclass
class ShearRheologyOptimizer: 
132@dataclass
133class ShearRheologyOptimizer:
134    r"""Design :math:`\bm\theta` so a periodic tissue attains a prescribed mode compliance.
135
136    Args:
137        energy_theta: the **undriven** vertex-model energy, in the six-argument inner-loss signature
138            ``(vertTable, heTable, faceTable, vert_params, he_params, face_params)``. ``width`` and
139            ``height`` are ``static_argnums`` throughout the library and must be closed over by the
140            caller.
141        mode: the drive mode. Re-reference it from the :math:`a=0` relaxed state at each outer epoch
142            and treat it as a constant of the estimator *within* the epoch.
143        a0: drive amplitude, frozen by V4 before any design run.
144        j_target: target compliance. **Derive it as** ``rheology.target_compliance(G_tgt, mode)``
145            with ``G_tgt`` taken *on the measured forward curve*, so that
146            :math:`\widehat{\mathcal C}` starts :math:`O(1)`. Setting it to a bare constant makes
147            :math:`\beta\widehat{\mathcal C}` comparable to the whole energy and the "nudge" is then a
148            large perturbation — measured, and it invalidated an earlier P5 test.
149        beta: nudge magnitude. Code convention: solves at :math:`\pm\beta`, prefactor
150            :math:`1/(2\beta)`.
151        solver_factory: zero-argument callable returning a fresh optax solver for the inner solve.
152        width, height: box dimensions.
153        min_dist_T1: T1 threshold.
154        free_iters, nudged_iters: inner iteration budgets. **Measure these, do not assume them.**
155            A warm-started driven solve does *not* converge quickly merely because it travels a short
156            distance: CG's iteration count is set by the spectrum, and the drive excites the softest
157            modes. Measured on the 72-cell production box, from a free state at
158            :math:`\|\nabla_xE\|\approx2\times10^{-13}`, the driven solve still needs ~5000
159            iterations for :math:`10^{-8}` and ~20000 for :math:`10^{-13}`.
160        theta_target: which parameter array is designed.
161        update_t1: T1 during the inner solves. **On** for production — it is the fluidity mechanism.
162        cap_vertex_step: per-step vertex displacement cap. Keep **True** with a line-search solver
163            and T1 on.
164        n_sweeps: alternating half-sweep count in the nudged phase. Do **not** raise past 4: if the
165            alternation is not contracting by then, block-coordinate is inadequate and a joint solver
166            is needed — report rather than paper over it.
167    """
168
169    energy_theta: Callable[..., Array]
170    mode: ShearMode
171    a0: float
172    j_target: float
173    beta: float
174    solver_factory: Callable[[], optax.GradientTransformation]
175    width: float
176    height: float
177    min_dist_T1: float = 0.005
178    free_iters: int = 20000
179    nudged_iters: int = 5000
180    theta_target: OptimizationTarget = OptimizationTarget.FACE_PARAMETERS
181    update_t1: bool = True
182    cap_vertex_step: bool = True
183    n_sweeps: int = 2
184    history: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
185
186    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
187        """Validate the conventions that cannot be recovered from a wrong run."""
188        if self.beta <= 0:
189            msg = f"beta must be > 0; got {self.beta}"
190            raise ValueError(msg)
191        if self.n_sweeps < 1 or self.n_sweeps > 4:
192            msg = (f"n_sweeps must be in 1..4; got {self.n_sweeps}. Raising it past 4 hides a "
193                   "non-contracting alternation instead of reporting it.")
194            raise ValueError(msg)
195        if self.theta_target not in (OptimizationTarget.FACE_PARAMETERS,
196                                     OptimizationTarget.EDGE_PARAMETERS,
197                                     OptimizationTarget.VERTEX_PARAMETERS):
198            msg = f"theta_target must be a parameter array, got {self.theta_target}"
199            raise ValueError(msg)
200
201    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ inner
202    def _relax(self, inner_loss, v, he, fa, params, iters):  # noqa: ANN001, ANN202
203        """One inner relaxation of the vertices, through the production `minimize`."""
204        import time
205
206        vp, hp, fp = params
207        t0 = time.perf_counter()
208        (vv, hh, ff, _a, _b, _c), _hist = minimize(
209            jnp.asarray(v, jnp.float64), he, fa, self.width, self.height,
210            jnp.asarray(vp, jnp.float64), jnp.asarray(hp, jnp.float64),
211            jnp.asarray(fp, jnp.float64),
212            inner_loss, self.solver_factory(), self.min_dist_T1,
213            iterations_max=iters, tolerance=0.0, patience=5,
214            optimization_target=OptimizationTarget.VERTICES,
215            update_t1_func=(update_T1 if self.update_t1 else do_not_update_T1),
216            cap_vertex_step=self.cap_vertex_step,
217        )
218        return vv, hh, ff, time.perf_counter() - t0
219
220    def _state(self, inner_loss, v, he, fa, params, ref_sig, secs) -> ShearState:  # noqa: ANN001
221        """Package a relaxed configuration with its diagnostics."""
222        vp, hp, fp = params
223        return ShearState(
224            vertices=v, edges=he, faces=fa,
225            grad_norm=grad_x_norm(inner_loss, v, he, fa, vp, hp, fp),
226            amplitude=float(mode_amplitude(v, self.mode)),
227            t1_events=t1_event_count(ref_sig, topology_signature(he)),
228            conn_hash=connectivity_hash(he),
229            seconds=secs,
230            energy=float(inner_loss(v, he, fa, vp, hp, fp)),
231        )
232
233    # ------------------------------------------------------------ free phase
234    def free_phase(self, vertices, edges, faces, params):  # noqa: ANN001, ANN201
235        r"""Relax the two conditions **independently** at :math:`\beta=0`.
236
237        Returns ``{+1: ShearState, -1: ShearState}``. These are the warm-start points for every
238        nudged solve, and the pair from which :math:`\widehat J` is read.
239        """
240        ref_sig = topology_signature(edges)
241        out = {}
242        for sgn in (+1, -1):
243            inner = make_drive_energy(self.energy_theta, self.mode, sgn * self.a0)
244            v, he, fa, secs = self._relax(inner, vertices, edges, faces, params, self.free_iters)
245            out[sgn] = self._state(inner, v, he, fa, params, ref_sig, secs)
246        return out
247
248    # ---------------------------------------------------------- nudged phase
249    def nudged_phase(self, free, params, b):  # noqa: ANN001, ANN201
250        r"""Alternating (block-coordinate) nudged solves at nudge level ``b``.
251
252        Each half-sweep minimises one condition with the **partner's amplitude frozen**, which is what
253        makes the joint nudged equilibrium expressible against a one-mesh inner solver. Both the
254        :math:`+\beta` and :math:`-\beta` calls enter from the *same* free states, so their residuals
255        are correlated and largely cancel in the difference.
256        """
257        cur = {sgn: (free[sgn].vertices, free[sgn].edges, free[sgn].faces) for sgn in (+1, -1)}
258        amp = {sgn: free[sgn].amplitude for sgn in (+1, -1)}
259        sweep_moves = []
260        for _sweep in range(self.n_sweeps):
261            moved = 0.0
262            for sgn in (+1, -1):
263                cost = make_compliance_cost(self.mode, self.j_target, self.a0,
264                                            partner_amplitude=amp[-sgn], sign=sgn)
265                driven = make_drive_energy(self.energy_theta, self.mode, sgn * self.a0)
266                w, h_, f_ = self.width, self.height, None
267
268                def nudged(vt, ht, ft, vp, hp, fp, _d=driven, _c=cost, _b=b):  # noqa: ANN001, ANN202
269                    return _d(vt, ht, ft, vp, hp, fp) + _b * _c(
270                        vt, ht, ft, w, h_, None, None, None, None, None, None, None)
271
272                v_prev = cur[sgn][0]
273                v, he, fa, secs = self._relax(nudged, *cur[sgn], params, self.nudged_iters)
274                cur[sgn] = (v, he, fa)
275                amp[sgn] = float(mode_amplitude(v, self.mode))
276                moved = max(moved, float(jnp.linalg.norm(v - v_prev) / jnp.linalg.norm(v_prev)))
277            sweep_moves.append(moved)
278
279        out = {}
280        for sgn in (+1, -1):
281            cost = make_compliance_cost(self.mode, self.j_target, self.a0,
282                                        partner_amplitude=amp[-sgn], sign=sgn)
283            driven = make_drive_energy(self.energy_theta, self.mode, sgn * self.a0)
284            w, h_ = self.width, self.height
285
286            def nudged(vt, ht, ft, vp, hp, fp, _d=driven, _c=cost, _b=b):  # noqa: ANN001, ANN202
287                return _d(vt, ht, ft, vp, hp, fp) + _b * _c(
288                    vt, ht, ft, w, h_, None, None, None, None, None, None, None)
289
290            ref_sig = topology_signature(free[sgn].edges)
291            out[sgn] = self._state(nudged, *cur[sgn], params, ref_sig, 0.0)
292        return out, sweep_moves
293
294    # -------------------------------------------------------------- estimator
295    def _theta_grad(self, state: ShearState, params, sgn: int) -> Array:  # noqa: ANN001
296        r"""":math:`\partial_{\bm\theta}\mathcal E` at a recorded state.
297
298        The drive carries no :math:`\bm\theta`, so this is the bare vertex-model parameter gradient —
299        but it is evaluated on the *driven* energy so that a future :math:`\bm\theta`-dependent drive
300        could not silently drop a term.
301        """
302        driven = make_drive_energy(self.energy_theta, self.mode, sgn * self.a0)
303        argnum = {OptimizationTarget.VERTEX_PARAMETERS: 3,
304                  OptimizationTarget.EDGE_PARAMETERS: 4,
305                  OptimizationTarget.FACE_PARAMETERS: 5}[self.theta_target]
306        vp, hp, fp = params
307
308        def e_of_theta(theta):  # noqa: ANN001, ANN202
309            args = [state.vertices, state.edges, state.faces, vp, hp, fp]
310            args[argnum] = theta
311            return driven(*args)
312
313        return jax.grad(e_of_theta)(params[argnum - 3])
314
315    def compliance_gradient(self, nudged_plus, nudged_minus, params):  # noqa: ANN001, ANN201
316        r"""The centered EP estimate, **summed over both conditions**."""
317        plus = sum(self._theta_grad(nudged_plus[s], params, s) for s in (+1, -1))
318        minus = sum(self._theta_grad(nudged_minus[s], params, s) for s in (+1, -1))
319        return (plus - minus) / (2.0 * self.beta)
320
321    # ------------------------------------------------------------ diagnostics
322    def beta_upper_bound(self, j_measured: float, ratio: float = 0.1) -> float:
323        r"""Largest :math:`\beta` at which the nudge is still a perturbation, not a constraint.
324
325        The nudge adds a stiffness :math:`\beta\cdot2/(2a_0J_{\rm tgt})^2` along the mode; the tissue's
326        own mode stiffness is :math:`\sum\hat c^2/J`. Linear response needs the first well below the
327        second, so
328
329        .. math:: \beta \le \text{ratio}\cdot\frac{\sum\hat c^2}{J}\cdot\frac{(2a_0J_{\rm tgt})^2}{2}
330
331        with ``ratio`` the tolerated stiffness fraction (0.1 by default). **This is a necessary
332        condition, not a sufficient one** — confirm linearity empirically by halving :math:`\beta` and
333        checking that the state response halves.
334        """
335        k_mode = self.mode.c_sq / j_measured
336        return ratio * k_mode * (2.0 * self.a0 * self.j_target) ** 2 / 2.0
337
338    def compliance_and_cost(self, states) -> tuple[float, float]:  # noqa: ANN001
339        r"""":math:`(\widehat J, \widehat{\mathcal C})` from a pair of states."""
340        j = float(compliance(states[+1].amplitude, states[-1].amplitude, self.a0))
341        return j, float((j / self.j_target - 1.0) ** 2)
342
343    def beta_diagnostics(self, free, nudged_plus) -> dict[str, float]:  # noqa: ANN001
344        r"""The two numbers D2 requires to be logged at every outer step.
345
346        ``rel_state_change`` must sit in :math:`[10^{-4},10^{-2}]` and ``beta_cost_over_energy``
347        below :math:`10^{-2}`. Outside those the "nudge" is either invisible or is a large
348        perturbation, and in both cases the estimator is not measuring what it claims to.
349        """
350        _j, c = self.compliance_and_cost(free)
351        e_scale = max(abs(free[+1].energy), 1e-300)
352        rel = max(
353            float(jnp.linalg.norm(nudged_plus[s].vertices - free[s].vertices)
354                  / jnp.linalg.norm(free[s].vertices))
355            for s in (+1, -1)
356        )
357        return {
358            "cost_free": c,
359            "beta_times_cost": self.beta * c,
360            "beta_cost_over_energy": self.beta * c / e_scale,
361            "rel_state_change": rel,
362            "in_state_window": float(1e-4 <= rel <= 1e-2),
363            "beta_scale_ok": float(self.beta * c / e_scale < 1e-2),
364        }
365
366    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ epoch
367    def epoch(self, vertices, edges, faces, params, outer_solver, outer_state):  # noqa: ANN001, ANN201
368        r"""One outer step: free phase, both nudged phases, the centered EP estimate, one optax update.
369
370        Returns ``(new_params, new_outer_state, diagnostics)``. The mode is **not** re-referenced
371        here — the caller does that between epochs, so that the reference is a constant of the
372        estimator within the epoch.
373        """
374        free = self.free_phase(vertices, edges, faces, params)
375        j, cost = self.compliance_and_cost(free)
376        n_plus, moves_p = self.nudged_phase(free, params, +self.beta)
377        n_minus, moves_m = self.nudged_phase(free, params, -self.beta)
378        grad = self.compliance_gradient(n_plus, n_minus, params)
379        bd = self.beta_diagnostics(free, n_plus)
380
381        # EP validity: the +-beta solves must cross the SAME T1 events. This must be judged on the
382        # relabelling-invariant face-pair signature, NOT on `conn_hash`: that hash covers the whole
383        # half-edge table including the periodic offset columns, which `update_pbc` rewrites whenever
384        # a vertex crosses the seam. Judging validity on it produces mismatches even on runs with T1
385        # disabled entirely, where no topology change is possible.
386        conn_ok = all(
387            topology_signature(n_plus[s].edges) == topology_signature(n_minus[s].edges)
388            for s in (+1, -1)
389        )
390
391        argnum = {OptimizationTarget.VERTEX_PARAMETERS: 0,
392                  OptimizationTarget.EDGE_PARAMETERS: 1,
393                  OptimizationTarget.FACE_PARAMETERS: 2}[self.theta_target]
394        theta = params[argnum]
395        updates, new_outer_state = outer_solver.update(grad, outer_state, theta)
396        new_theta = optax.apply_updates(theta, updates)
397        new_params = list(params)
398        new_params[argnum] = new_theta
399
400        diag = {
401            "J": j, "G": float(modulus_from_compliance(j, self.mode)),
402            "J_target": self.j_target,
403            "G_target": float(modulus_from_compliance(self.j_target, self.mode)),
404            "cost": cost,
405            "grad_norm_theta": float(jnp.linalg.norm(grad)),
406            "gradE_free_plus": free[+1].grad_norm, "gradE_free_minus": free[-1].grad_norm,
407            "gradE_nudged_max": max(n_plus[s].grad_norm for s in (+1, -1)),
408            "t1_free_plus": free[+1].t1_events, "t1_free_minus": free[-1].t1_events,
409            "t1_nudged_plus": n_plus[+1].t1_events + n_plus[-1].t1_events,
410            "t1_nudged_minus": n_minus[+1].t1_events + n_minus[-1].t1_events,
411            "connectivity_match_pm": int(conn_ok),
412            "ep_step_valid": int(conn_ok),
413            "sweep_moves_plus": moves_p, "sweep_moves_minus": moves_m,
414            "alternation_contracting": int(len(moves_p) < 2 or moves_p[-1] <= moves_p[0]),
415            "theta_mean": float(jnp.mean(new_theta)),
416            "secs": sum(free[s].seconds for s in (+1, -1)),
417            **bd,
418        }
419        self.history.append(diag)
420        return tuple(new_params), new_outer_state, diag

Design \( \bm\theta \) so a periodic tissue attains a prescribed mode compliance.

Args: energy_theta: the undriven vertex-model energy, in the six-argument inner-loss signature (vertTable, heTable, faceTable, vert_params, he_params, face_params). width and height are static_argnums throughout the library and must be closed over by the caller. mode: the drive mode. Re-reference it from the \( a=0 \) relaxed state at each outer epoch and treat it as a constant of the estimator within the epoch. a0: drive amplitude, frozen by V4 before any design run. j_target: target compliance. Derive it as rheology.target_compliance(G_tgt, mode) with G_tgt taken on the measured forward curve, so that \( \widehat{\mathcal C} \) starts \( O(1) \). Setting it to a bare constant makes \( \beta\widehat{\mathcal C} \) comparable to the whole energy and the "nudge" is then a large perturbation — measured, and it invalidated an earlier P5 test. beta: nudge magnitude. Code convention: solves at \( \pm\beta \), prefactor \( 1/(2\beta) \). solver_factory: zero-argument callable returning a fresh optax solver for the inner solve. width, height: box dimensions. min_dist_T1: T1 threshold. free_iters, nudged_iters: inner iteration budgets. Measure these, do not assume them. A warm-started driven solve does not converge quickly merely because it travels a short distance: CG's iteration count is set by the spectrum, and the drive excites the softest modes. Measured on the 72-cell production box, from a free state at \( \|\nabla_xE\|\approx2\times10^{-13} \), the driven solve still needs ~5000 iterations for \( 10^{-8} \) and ~20000 for \( 10^{-13} \). theta_target: which parameter array is designed. update_t1: T1 during the inner solves. On for production — it is the fluidity mechanism. cap_vertex_step: per-step vertex displacement cap. Keep True with a line-search solver and T1 on. n_sweeps: alternating half-sweep count in the nudged phase. Do not raise past 4: if the alternation is not contracting by then, block-coordinate is inadequate and a joint solver is needed — report rather than paper over it.

def free_phase(self, vertices, edges, faces, params): 
234    def free_phase(self, vertices, edges, faces, params):  # noqa: ANN001, ANN201
235        r"""Relax the two conditions **independently** at :math:`\beta=0`.
236
237        Returns ``{+1: ShearState, -1: ShearState}``. These are the warm-start points for every
238        nudged solve, and the pair from which :math:`\widehat J` is read.
239        """
240        ref_sig = topology_signature(edges)
241        out = {}
242        for sgn in (+1, -1):
243            inner = make_drive_energy(self.energy_theta, self.mode, sgn * self.a0)
244            v, he, fa, secs = self._relax(inner, vertices, edges, faces, params, self.free_iters)
245            out[sgn] = self._state(inner, v, he, fa, params, ref_sig, secs)
246        return out

Relax the two conditions independently at \( \beta=0 \).

Returns {+1: ShearState, -1: ShearState}. These are the warm-start points for every nudged solve, and the pair from which \( \widehat J \) is read.

def nudged_phase(self, free, params, b): 
249    def nudged_phase(self, free, params, b):  # noqa: ANN001, ANN201
250        r"""Alternating (block-coordinate) nudged solves at nudge level ``b``.
251
252        Each half-sweep minimises one condition with the **partner's amplitude frozen**, which is what
253        makes the joint nudged equilibrium expressible against a one-mesh inner solver. Both the
254        :math:`+\beta` and :math:`-\beta` calls enter from the *same* free states, so their residuals
255        are correlated and largely cancel in the difference.
256        """
257        cur = {sgn: (free[sgn].vertices, free[sgn].edges, free[sgn].faces) for sgn in (+1, -1)}
258        amp = {sgn: free[sgn].amplitude for sgn in (+1, -1)}
259        sweep_moves = []
260        for _sweep in range(self.n_sweeps):
261            moved = 0.0
262            for sgn in (+1, -1):
263                cost = make_compliance_cost(self.mode, self.j_target, self.a0,
264                                            partner_amplitude=amp[-sgn], sign=sgn)
265                driven = make_drive_energy(self.energy_theta, self.mode, sgn * self.a0)
266                w, h_, f_ = self.width, self.height, None
267
268                def nudged(vt, ht, ft, vp, hp, fp, _d=driven, _c=cost, _b=b):  # noqa: ANN001, ANN202
269                    return _d(vt, ht, ft, vp, hp, fp) + _b * _c(
270                        vt, ht, ft, w, h_, None, None, None, None, None, None, None)
271
272                v_prev = cur[sgn][0]
273                v, he, fa, secs = self._relax(nudged, *cur[sgn], params, self.nudged_iters)
274                cur[sgn] = (v, he, fa)
275                amp[sgn] = float(mode_amplitude(v, self.mode))
276                moved = max(moved, float(jnp.linalg.norm(v - v_prev) / jnp.linalg.norm(v_prev)))
277            sweep_moves.append(moved)
278
279        out = {}
280        for sgn in (+1, -1):
281            cost = make_compliance_cost(self.mode, self.j_target, self.a0,
282                                        partner_amplitude=amp[-sgn], sign=sgn)
283            driven = make_drive_energy(self.energy_theta, self.mode, sgn * self.a0)
284            w, h_ = self.width, self.height
285
286            def nudged(vt, ht, ft, vp, hp, fp, _d=driven, _c=cost, _b=b):  # noqa: ANN001, ANN202
287                return _d(vt, ht, ft, vp, hp, fp) + _b * _c(
288                    vt, ht, ft, w, h_, None, None, None, None, None, None, None)
289
290            ref_sig = topology_signature(free[sgn].edges)
291            out[sgn] = self._state(nudged, *cur[sgn], params, ref_sig, 0.0)
292        return out, sweep_moves

Alternating (block-coordinate) nudged solves at nudge level b.

Each half-sweep minimises one condition with the partner's amplitude frozen, which is what makes the joint nudged equilibrium expressible against a one-mesh inner solver. Both the \( +\beta \) and \( -\beta \) calls enter from the same free states, so their residuals are correlated and largely cancel in the difference.

def compliance_gradient(self, nudged_plus, nudged_minus, params): 
315    def compliance_gradient(self, nudged_plus, nudged_minus, params):  # noqa: ANN001, ANN201
316        r"""The centered EP estimate, **summed over both conditions**."""
317        plus = sum(self._theta_grad(nudged_plus[s], params, s) for s in (+1, -1))
318        minus = sum(self._theta_grad(nudged_minus[s], params, s) for s in (+1, -1))
319        return (plus - minus) / (2.0 * self.beta)

The centered EP estimate, summed over both conditions.

def beta_upper_bound(self, j_measured: float, ratio: float = 0.1) -> float: 
322    def beta_upper_bound(self, j_measured: float, ratio: float = 0.1) -> float:
323        r"""Largest :math:`\beta` at which the nudge is still a perturbation, not a constraint.
324
325        The nudge adds a stiffness :math:`\beta\cdot2/(2a_0J_{\rm tgt})^2` along the mode; the tissue's
326        own mode stiffness is :math:`\sum\hat c^2/J`. Linear response needs the first well below the
327        second, so
328
329        .. math:: \beta \le \text{ratio}\cdot\frac{\sum\hat c^2}{J}\cdot\frac{(2a_0J_{\rm tgt})^2}{2}
330
331        with ``ratio`` the tolerated stiffness fraction (0.1 by default). **This is a necessary
332        condition, not a sufficient one** — confirm linearity empirically by halving :math:`\beta` and
333        checking that the state response halves.
334        """
335        k_mode = self.mode.c_sq / j_measured
336        return ratio * k_mode * (2.0 * self.a0 * self.j_target) ** 2 / 2.0

def make_shear_mode( vertices: jax.Array, width: float, height: float, n: int = 1, mod_axis: int = 1, pol_axis: int = 0, *, mean_tol: float = 1e-12) -> ShearMode: 
192def make_shear_mode(
193    vertices: Array,
194    width: float,
195    height: float,
196    n: int = 1,
197    mod_axis: int = 1,
198    pol_axis: int = 0,
199    *,
200    mean_tol: float = 1e-12,
201) -> ShearMode:
202    r"""Build a drive mode from the **undriven reference configuration**.
203
204    The weights are attached to material points, so ``vertices`` must be the *relaxed* :math:`a=0`
205    state, and the mode must be re-referenced whenever that state moves appreciably (the drift
206    diagnostic is :func:`drive_drift`).
207
208    Args:
209        vertices: Reference positions, shape ``(N, 2)`` — the relaxed ``a = 0`` state.
210        width: Box width.
211        height: Box height.
212        n: Mode index; ``q = 2*pi*n / L_mod``.
213        mod_axis: 0 for ``cos(qx)``, 1 for ``cos(qy)``.
214        pol_axis: 0 to drive/observe ``x``, 1 to drive/observe ``y``.
215        mean_tol: Tolerance on :math:`|\sum_i\hat c_i|`.
216
217    Raises:
218        ValueError: If the mean-removal assertion fails, or the axes are not in ``{0, 1}``, or
219            ``n < 1``.
220    """
221    require_float64()
222    if mod_axis not in (0, 1) or pol_axis not in (0, 1):
223        msg = f"mod_axis and pol_axis must be 0 or 1; got {mod_axis}, {pol_axis}"
224        raise ValueError(msg)
225    if n < 1:
226        msg = f"mode index n must be >= 1 (n = 0 is a rigid translation); got {n}"
227        raise ValueError(msg)
228    r0 = jnp.asarray(vertices[:, :2], dtype=jnp.float64)
229    n_vert = r0.shape[0]
230    mod_period = width if mod_axis == 0 else height
231    q = 2.0 * np.pi * n / mod_period
232    raw = jnp.cos(q * r0[:, mod_axis])
233    c = raw - jnp.mean(raw)
234    resid = float(jnp.abs(jnp.sum(c)))
235    if resid > mean_tol:
236        msg = f"|sum c_i| = {resid:.3e} exceeds {mean_tol:.1e}: the drive carries a net force."
237        raise ValueError(msg)
238    c_sq = float(jnp.sum(c**2))
239    return ShearMode(
240        c=c,
241        r0=r0,
242        q=float(q),
243        n=int(n),
244        width=float(width),
245        height=float(height),
246        mod_axis=int(mod_axis),
247        pol_axis=int(pol_axis),
248        rho_v=n_vert / (width * height),
249        c_sq=c_sq,
250        c_sq_ratio=2.0 * c_sq / n_vert,
251    )

Build a drive mode from the undriven reference configuration.

The weights are attached to material points, so vertices must be the relaxed \( a=0 \) state, and the mode must be re-referenced whenever that state moves appreciably (the drift diagnostic is drive_drift()).

Args: vertices: Reference positions, shape (N, 2) — the relaxed a = 0 state. width: Box width. height: Box height. n: Mode index; q = 2*pi*n / L_mod. mod_axis: 0 for cos(qx), 1 for cos(qy). pol_axis: 0 to drive/observe x, 1 to drive/observe y. mean_tol: Tolerance on \( |\sum_i\hat c_i| \).

Raises: ValueError: If the mean-removal assertion fails, or the axes are not in {0, 1}, or n < 1.

def make_drive_energy( base_energy: Callable[[jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array], jax.Array], mode: ShearMode, a: float) -> Callable[[jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array, jax.Array], jax.Array]: 
282def make_drive_energy(
283    base_energy: Callable[[Array, Array, Array, Array, Array, Array], Array],
284    mode: ShearMode,
285    a: float,
286) -> Callable[[Array, Array, Array, Array, Array, Array], Array]:
287    r"""Wrap an inner loss with the cosine drive potential at amplitude ``a``.
288
289    Args:
290        base_energy: A callable with the **exact** six-argument inner-loss signature
291            ``(vertTable, heTable, faceTable, vert_params, he_params, face_params)``, as
292            ``opt.InnerLossFunction`` requires. ``width``/``height`` are ``static_argnums``
293            throughout the library and are therefore closed over by the caller, not passed here.
294        mode: The drive mode; its weights and reference state are captured by closure.
295        a: Drive amplitude. ``a = 0`` returns the undriven energy up to a term that is identically
296            zero, so it is a valid way to build the free condition.
297
298    Returns:
299        A callable with the same six-argument signature, adding
300        :math:`-a\sum_i\hat c_i\Delta r_i^{\rm pol}`.
301
302    The returned energy raises on a vertex-row-count mismatch. That converts the one silent failure
303    mode of this construction — a partial ``selected_verts``, which slices ``vertTable`` and so
304    mis-pairs weights with vertices — into a loud one.
305    """
306    c = mode.c
307    r0_pol = mode.r0[:, mode.pol_axis]
308    pol = mode.pol_axis
309    period = mode.pol_period
310    n_expected = int(c.shape[0])
311    amp = float(a)
312
313    def energy_with_drive(
314        vertTable: Array,  # noqa: N803
315        heTable: Array,  # noqa: N803
316        faceTable: Array,  # noqa: N803
317        vert_params: Array,
318        he_params: Array,
319        face_params: Array,
320    ) -> Array:
321        """Inner loss = vertex-model energy + cosine drive potential."""
322        if vertTable.shape[0] != n_expected:
323            msg = (
324                f"drive energy built for {n_expected} vertices, called with {vertTable.shape[0]}. "
325                "The weights are attached to vertex rows, so a sliced vertTable (a partial "
326                "selected_verts) would mis-pair them. Pass the full vertex selection."
327            )
328            raise ValueError(msg)
329        base = base_energy(vertTable, heTable, faceTable, vert_params, he_params, face_params)
330        delta = min_image_delta_x(vertTable[:, pol], r0_pol, period)
331        return base - amp * jnp.sum(c * delta)
332
333    return energy_with_drive

Wrap an inner loss with the cosine drive potential at amplitude a.

Args: base_energy: A callable with the exact six-argument inner-loss signature (vertTable, heTable, faceTable, vert_params, he_params, face_params), as opt.InnerLossFunction requires. width/height are static_argnums throughout the library and are therefore closed over by the caller, not passed here. mode: The drive mode; its weights and reference state are captured by closure. a: Drive amplitude. a = 0 returns the undriven energy up to a term that is identically zero, so it is a valid way to build the free condition.

Returns: A callable with the same six-argument signature, adding \( -a\sum_i\hat c_i\Delta r_i^{\rm pol} \).

The returned energy raises on a vertex-row-count mismatch. That converts the one silent failure mode of this construction — a partial selected_verts, which slices vertTable and so mis-pairs weights with vertices — into a loud one.

def make_compliance_cost( mode: ShearMode, j_target: float, a0: float, partner_amplitude: float, sign: Literal[1, -1]) -> Callable[..., jax.Array]: 
377def make_compliance_cost(
378    mode: ShearMode,
379    j_target: float,
380    a0: float,
381    partner_amplitude: float,
382    sign: Literal[1, -1],
383) -> Callable[..., Array]:
384    r"""Outer loss :math:`\mathcal C=(\hat J/J_{\rm tgt}-1)^2` for **one** condition of the pair.
385
386    The partner condition's amplitude is frozen and captured by closure, which is what makes the
387    block-coordinate alternation expressible against the library's one-mesh outer loss.
388    ``sign = +1`` for the :math:`+a_0` condition, ``-1`` for :math:`-a_0`.
389
390    Returns a callable with the exact twelve-argument ``opt.OuterLossFunction`` signature. It uses
391    only ``vertTable``: the cost has **no** parameter dependence, by construction, which is the
392    property that keeps the implemented centered-EP estimator correct.
393    """
394    if sign not in (1, -1):
395        msg = f"sign must be +1 or -1; got {sign}"
396        raise ValueError(msg)
397    two_a0 = 2.0 * float(a0)
398    partner = float(partner_amplitude)
399    jt = float(j_target)
400
401    def cost(
402        vertTable: Array,  # noqa: N803
403        heTable: Array | None = None,  # noqa: N803, ARG001
404        faceTable: Array | None = None,  # noqa: N803, ARG001
405        width: float | None = None,  # noqa: ARG001
406        height: float | None = None,  # noqa: ARG001
407        vertTable_target: Array | None = None,  # noqa: N803, ARG001
408        heTable_target: Array | None = None,  # noqa: N803, ARG001
409        faceTable_target: Array | None = None,  # noqa: N803, ARG001
410        selected_verts: Array | None = None,  # noqa: ARG001
411        selected_hes: Array | None = None,  # noqa: ARG001
412        selected_faces: Array | None = None,  # noqa: ARG001
413        image_target: Array | None = None,  # noqa: ARG001
414    ) -> Array:
415        """Squared relative compliance error, with the partner amplitude held frozen."""
416        u = mode_amplitude(vertTable, mode)
417        j_hat = (u - partner) / two_a0 if sign == 1 else (partner - u) / two_a0
418        return (j_hat / jt - 1.0) ** 2
419
420    return cost

Outer loss \( \mathcal C=(\hat J/J_{\rm tgt}-1)^2 \) for one condition of the pair.

The partner condition's amplitude is frozen and captured by closure, which is what makes the block-coordinate alternation expressible against the library's one-mesh outer loss. sign = +1 for the \( +a_0 \) condition, -1 for \( -a_0 \).

Returns a callable with the exact twelve-argument opt.OuterLossFunction signature. It uses only vertTable: the cost has no parameter dependence, by construction, which is the property that keeps the implemented centered-EP estimator correct.

def min_image_delta_x(x: jax.Array, x0: jax.Array, period: float) -> jax.Array: 
254def min_image_delta_x(x: Array, x0: Array, period: float) -> Array:
255    r"""Minimum-image displacement ``x - x0`` wrapped into the half-open :math:`[-L/2, +L/2)`.
256
257    Spelled ``d - L*floor(d/L + 1/2)``. Three properties matter, and V0 checks all three:
258
259    * **Its derivative is exactly 1 everywhere** in JAX, because ``jnp.floor`` carries a zero JVP.
260      No ``stop_gradient`` is needed, and none is used: the image index ``floor(d/L + 1/2)`` is an
261      integer label of the periodic image, piecewise constant, with derivative zero almost
262      everywhere.
263    * **It is exactly invariant under a lattice translation**, at every point including the
264      tie. The obvious spelling ``d - L*round(d/L)`` is *not*: ``round`` is half-to-even, so it maps
265      both :math:`\pm L/2` to themselves, the interval comes out closed, and the two representatives
266      at exactly :math:`d=L/2` differ by one lattice vector, :math:`|\Delta|=L`. The physics is
267      untouched -- either representative is a valid minimum image -- but an exact invariance is
268      worth more than a caveat, which is why the half-open interval is used here.
269    * **It is not a nine-image ``jnp.min`` reduction**, deliberately: that form has a kink whose AD
270      path is the one ``geo.min_image_sq_dist`` documents as having produced NaN gradients on real
271      meshes.
272    """
273    d = x - x0
274    return d - period * jnp.floor(d / period + 0.5)

Minimum-image displacement x - x0 wrapped into the half-open \( [-L/2, +L/2) \).

Spelled d - L*floor(d/L + 1/2). Three properties matter, and V0 checks all three:

  • Its derivative is exactly 1 everywhere in JAX, because jnp.floor carries a zero JVP. No stop_gradient is needed, and none is used: the image index floor(d/L + 1/2) is an integer label of the periodic image, piecewise constant, with derivative zero almost everywhere.
  • It is exactly invariant under a lattice translation, at every point including the tie. The obvious spelling d - L*round(d/L) is not: round is half-to-even, so it maps both \( \pm L/2 \) to themselves, the interval comes out closed, and the two representatives at exactly \( d=L/2 \) differ by one lattice vector, \( |\Delta|=L \). The physics is untouched -- either representative is a valid minimum image -- but an exact invariance is worth more than a caveat, which is why the half-open interval is used here.
  • It is not a nine-image jnp.min reduction, deliberately: that form has a kink whose AD path is the one geo.min_image_sq_dist documents as having produced NaN gradients on real meshes.
def mode_amplitude(vertices: jax.Array, mode: ShearMode) -> jax.Array: 
336def mode_amplitude(vertices: Array, mode: ShearMode) -> Array:
337    r"""Amplitude of the driven Fourier component of the displacement field,
338    :math:`U=\sum_i\hat c_i\Delta r_i/\sum_i\hat c_i^2` — a **linear** functional of the positions.
339    """
340    delta = min_image_delta_x(vertices[:, mode.pol_axis], mode.r0[:, mode.pol_axis], mode.pol_period)
341    return jnp.sum(mode.c * delta) / mode.c_sq

Amplitude of the driven Fourier component of the displacement field, \( U=\sum_i\hat c_i\Delta r_i/\sum_i\hat c_i^2 \) — a linear functional of the positions.

def compliance( u_plus: jax.Array | float, u_minus: jax.Array | float, a0: float) -> jax.Array: 
344def compliance(u_plus: Array | float, u_minus: Array | float, a0: float) -> Array:
345    r"""Mode compliance :math:`J=(U_+-U_-)/(2a_0)` from the antisymmetric pair.
346
347    The pair removes the :math:`a=0` offset that any finite disordered mesh carries, and with it the
348    leading :math:`O(a_0^2)` nonlinearity. Note :math:`\Delta r^+_i-\Delta r^-_i=r^+_i-r^-_i`
349    exactly, so ``J`` does not depend on the reference positions at all — only the weights do.
350    """
351    return (u_plus - u_minus) / (2.0 * a0)

Mode compliance \( J=(U_+-U_-)/(2a_0) \) from the antisymmetric pair.

The pair removes the \( a=0 \) offset that any finite disordered mesh carries, and with it the leading \( O(a_0^2) \) nonlinearity. Note \( \Delta r^+_i-\Delta r^-_i=r^+_i-r^-_i \) exactly, so J does not depend on the reference positions at all — only the weights do.

def modulus_from_compliance(j: jax.Array | float, mode: ShearMode) -> jax.Array: 
354def modulus_from_compliance(j: Array | float, mode: ShearMode) -> Array:
355    r"""Apparent modulus at the mode's wavevector, :math:`G_n=\rho_v/(Jq_n^2)`.
356
357    This is the force-balance calibration. See
358    :attr:`ShearMode.c_sq_ratio` for the discrete-vs-continuum diagnostic that must be *reported*
359    beside it rather than folded into it. ``G`` diverges as :math:`J\to0`, which is exactly why the
360    outer cost is written on ``J``.
361    """
362    return mode.rho_v / (jnp.asarray(j) * mode.q**2)

Apparent modulus at the mode's wavevector, \( G_n=\rho_v/(Jq_n^2) \).

This is the force-balance calibration. See ShearMode.c_sq_ratio for the discrete-vs-continuum diagnostic that must be reported beside it rather than folded into it. G diverges as \( J\to0 \), which is exactly why the outer cost is written on J.

def target_compliance(g_target: float, mode: ShearMode) -> float: 
365def target_compliance(g_target: float, mode: ShearMode) -> float:
366    r"""Compliance target :math:`J_{\rm tgt}=\rho_v/(G_{\rm tgt}q^2)` for a modulus target."""
367    if g_target <= 0:
368        msg = (
369            f"G_target must be > 0; got {g_target}. A zero-modulus target is the degenerate "
370            "fluid-side case: J_tgt is infinite, the map G -> p0 is many-to-one, and the design "
371            "problem must be reported as a boundary, not optimised against."
372        )
373        raise ValueError(msg)
374    return mode.rho_v / (g_target * mode.q**2)

Compliance target \( J_{\rm tgt}=\rho_v/(G_{\rm tgt}q^2) \) for a modulus target.
